scholarships.name: Creative Academic Merit Scholarship
scholarships.requirements: Must be classified as International for fee purposes; Minimum entry requirements equivalent to BBC at A-Level or equivalent; Submission of a digital portfolio demonstrating high creative potential; Acceptance of a full-time BA (Hons) offer.
scholarships.description: Awarded to incoming international undergraduates at Arts University Plymouth who demonstrate exceptional creative talent and academic promise. This scholarship provides a one-off tuition fee reduction in the first year of study to help foster global artistic diversity.

Applicants will need to meet benchmarks for excellence of portfolio and demonstrate a commitment to study. Creative Scholarships are awarded up to a maximum of £2,000. Tuition Fees for EU and international students are detailed below, and are listed in Pound Sterling (£).

International applicants who need to apply for a Student Visa are required to pay a non-refundable deposit of £2,000 prior to the issuing of a CAS (Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies) by Arts University Plymouth - a CAS will not be issued before this payment is received.

Upon enrolment at the commencement of the academic year, students will then be required to pay the remaining balance of their tuition fees. Please be aware that these fees need to be paid in full upon enrolment - we are unable to accept partial payments, or to arrange payment plans.

We pride ourselves in being committed to offering students accessible and affordable quality programmes. Please note, fees are correct at the time of publication and may be subject to change.

(Fees detailed exclude costs for international students who need a pre-sessional English course and ongoing in-year English language support.)

International Fees for 2026/27 Extended Diplomas £12,500 per year (two year course) Foundation Diploma £12,500 per year (ten month course) BA (Hons) and Extended BA Degrees £17,500 per year (full time 3 year course - 4 years for Extended BA) Masters Degrees £17,500 per year (full time, 1 year course) £9,275 per year (part time, 2 year course) International Fees for 2027/28 Extended Diplomas £13,500 per year (two year course) Foundation Diploma £13,500 per year (ten month course) BA (Hons) and Integrated Foundation Year £18,000 per year (full time 3 year course - 4 years for Integrated Foundation Year route) Masters Degrees £18,000 per year (full time, 1 year course) £9,550 per year (part time, 2 year course) How to pay your fees

Our Finance team will contact you advising when and how to pay your Tuition Fees. Please look out for an email from them.

You will be able to pay by card or via bank transfer online.

Fee Assessing

There are two rates of fee: one is for students who are ordinarily resident in the United Kingdom and who meet the necessary criteria, and one is for students who are ordinarily resident in overseas countries and/or do not meet the necessary immigration criteria. All applications will be fee assessed and you will be contacted if any further information is required to establish your fee status.

Course Materials

Books and course materials will vary between each study programme and subject area, and there will be an additional charge to consider. Full details can be made available to you when you make your application.

Scholarships

Arts University Plymouth offers a range of scholarships to international applicants entering their first year of study at the university. These awards aim to support applicants with the costs of international study, by way of a fee reduction.

International applicants may be eligible to be considered for the below awards:

Creative Scholarships

Our Arts University Plymouth Creative Scholarships are awarded on merit via a panel, and are applied to students entering the first year of study of either an Undergraduate or Postgraduate course. Applicants will need to meet benchmarks for excellence of portfolio and demonstrate a commitment to study. Creative Scholarships are awarded up to a maximum of £2,000.

Applicants to Undergraduate and Postgraduate courses who have submitted a portfolio will be automatically eligible for a Creative Scholarship, and successful applicants will be contacted directly if they meet the criteria to receive an award.

Pro-Vice-Chancellor’s Arts University Plymouth Creative Excellence Award

The Pro-Vice-Chancellor’s Arts University Plymouth Creative Excellence Award is a £2,500 award applied to a student entering the first year of a full-time BA (Hons) Undergraduate degree, awarded on a competitive basis by application with selection at the discretion of the Pro-Vice-Chancellor. There are two of these awards available.

To apply for this bursary please complete this form, providing all requested information including a written statement (no more than 500 words) detailing why you think you should be considered for the role, and explaining how these funds could support you in your studies/creative practice. Please note that you must have submitted a portfolio for review before applying.

Vice-Chancellor’s Arts University Plymouth Excellence Award

The Vice-Chancellor’s Arts University Plymouth Excellence Award is a £3,500 award applied to a student entering a full time 1 year MA programme, awarded on a competitive basis by application and panel selection.

To apply for this bursary please complete this form, providing all requested information including a written statement (no more than 500 words) detailing why you think you should be considered for the role, and explaining how these funds could support you in your studies/creative practice. Please note that you must have submitted a portfolio for review before applying.

To be eligible for any of the above awards, you will need to have submitted an application, portfolio and any other requested information (i.e. English Language qualifications) by 25 February 2026.

If you have any questions regarding eligibility for these awards, please email international@aup.ac.uk

Other Sources of Financial Assistance

For information regarding other sources of financial assistance for international students, the following websites will give more detailed advice

pages.text: Arts University Plymouth Logo Skip to Content Our Courses Open Days Apply Now Menu Apply Now Our Courses Open Days Chevron Down About Us Chevron Down Study Chevron Down International Chevron Down Student Life Alumni Chevron Down Visit Resources Chevron Down Research & Innovation Prospectus Latest News What's On Established 1856 Student Login Staff Login Contact Us Undergraduate Undergraduate Fees, Finance and Funding Last updated October 2026 In this section In this section Undergraduate Undergraduate How to Apply Next Steps After Your Offer Careers & Enterprise Sandwich Year Fees, Finance and Funding Learning, Teaching & Assessment Student Support (Undergraduate) Key Dates (Undergraduate) Parents and guardians: supporting an undergraduate application Frequently Asked Questions Postgraduate progression with the Royal College of Art Postgraduate Pre-Degree Investing in your education is a wise decision and it's important to understand the student finance support available. From tuition fees to maintenance loans and bursaries to cash scholarships — we're here to help you plan your finances. For new students joining us in the academic year 2027/28, the fees for our CertHE, BA (Hons) and Extended BA (Hons) degrees for UK students will be £10,050 per year. The fees for part-time undergraduate programmes will be £5,025. For EU and I nternational students joining the university in 2027/28, fees for our BA (Hons) degrees are £18,000 per year. Scholarships of up to £2,000 per year may be available for international students, subject to eligibility and availability. The university typically raises undergraduate tuition fees annually, for new and current students, in line with tuition fee caps announced by Government. The tuition fee loan available will match the new fee cap each year. Fees outlined are correct at time of publishing and provide an indication of current costs. For more information please email admissions@aup.ac.uk . Bursaries & Hardship Funds As part of the university’s commitment to access and participation, there is a package of financial support available to provide targeted support to students with the greatest additional needs or to those experiencing specific financial burden. This will help enable students to fully partake in university life and have the same opportunities as others to complete their course and progress to graduate employment or further study. Materials Bursary This bursary will be available to students commencing their studies in the 2027/28 academic year, and is designed to assist students in buying materials to support their studies. Eligibility for the Materials Bursary is as follows: Home students only (noting no franchise students included) Based on annual household income of £25k or less Assessed via Student Finance England (SfE) for those in receipt of student finance; self-funded fee payers apply via the University’s online system and are assessed Minimum of 80% attendance at the start of February (including explained absence) Materials Bursary amounts: Extended BA £100 Level 4 £100 Level 5 £200 Level 6 £300 Eligible students will receive their bursary payment in one instalment, in March each year. Care Leavers and Care Experienced Student Bursary The University is also offering an additional bursary to students who are identified as care leavers or care experienced, to provide additional support. Eligibility for the Care Leavers & Care Experienced Bursary is as follows: Home students, who at enrolment declare that they are a care leaver or care experienced (no franchise students included) Assessed via Student Finance England (SfE) for those in receipt of student finance; self-funded fee payers apply via the University’s online system and are assessed Minimum of 80% attendance at the start of February (including explained absence) Amount: £1,000 Eligible students will receive their bursary payment in one instalment, in March each year. Care Leavers may be eligible for additional support from the Local Authority. Click here to find out more. Hardship Fund The HE Hardship Fund is a cash award from the University which does not need to be paid back. It is only available to those HE students experiencing unforeseen and severe financial hardship.     Materials and equipment needs vary between courses - for example, painting/drawing/sculpture materials (Art), fabrics and dyes (Fashion & Textiles), external hard drive (Media). The indicative cost range per year is £50-200 for Year 1, £50-300 for Year 2, £50-400 for Year 3. A typical student cost is estimated at £150 for Year 1, £200 for Year 2 and £300 for Year 3.

  • Printing & Photocopying
    Rates/average costs:
    Black & white - 5p A4, 10p A3.
    Colour - 15p A4, 30p A3.
    Not subsidised but provided at cost. The range of annual student spend is £1-£125, with an average spend per student of £11 per year.

  • Educational visits
    Educational visits are optional and are subsidised by Arts University Plymouth, and the range of costs per year are as follows: In general, the highest cost applies for the most expensive single overseas trip offered, and the lower part of the range represents costs for a number of different visits offered across each year of a programme and generally but not always within the UK. Cost range per year: £50-350 in Year 1, £50-400 in Year 2, £50-400 in Year 3. A typical student cost excluding subsistence is estimated at £100 in Year 1, £200 in Year 2 and £300 in Year 3.

contentBlocks.heading: Internal Progression Scholarship
contentBlocks.bodyText:
We want to retain the best creative talent that we can in Plymouth and know that creative study at pre-degree level at Arts University Plymouth offers an excellent preparation to succeed at one of our undergraduate degrees.

That’s why we offer a one-off £300 cash scholarship to students who progress directly from one of our UAL Extended Diplomas or a UAL Foundation Diploma in Art & Design onto a three or four-year undergraduate degree starting in Autumn 2027 at Arts University Plymouth.

You must also achieve the minimum attendance requirement in your first and second semester to be awarded the £300 scholarship. There is no application process for this scholarship and it is not based on home household income. The scholarship will be paid automatically to all qualifying students in one instalment in your second semester of study.

Students from the EU, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway or Switzerland may be entitled to loans for tuition fees from the Student Loans Company.

Students from the EU may also be entitled to help with living costs if you have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme. Irish citizens do not need to apply for a visa or to the EU Settlement Scheme.

For existing students from the EU and those who submitted their application for student finance before 25 March 2016, the residency in the UK is only three years.

For more information for current and new EU students, visit the Student Finance England web page for EU nationals.

We also welcome applicants who are resident outside of the EU, however, you will need to cover the costs of your tuition fees and living expenses yourself as you will not be entitled to student finance.

For more information and guidance for International students, please see our International Students page.

contentBlocks.heading: Local Authority Support for Care Leavers

contentBlocks.bodyText:
If you're a care leaver entering higher education before your 25th birthday, you may be entitled to a non-taxable £2,000 bursary from your local authority.

To apply, you should contact your pathway planner at your local authority. You should ask about the bursary and also whether there is any additional support for care leavers from your local authority. If you're eligible, make sure you have this agreed in writing as soon as possible. We can help if you need support with this.

For more information about care leavers progressing to higher education take a look at The Complete University Guide and this flowchart from the National Care Leavers Association is useful to check whether you are eligible.

To find out more information about the additional support available to Care Leavers from Plymouth City Council, please visit their website by clicking the link below.

items.heading: Office for Students (OfS)
items.bodyText:
Arts University Plymouth has been accepted onto the OfS Register of English higher education providers. That means we meet the OfS conditions of registration for course quality, academic standards, student support, student protection and more. For more information visit www.officeforstudents.org.uk/the-register.

You can find our Access and Participation plan on our Reports, Policies & Legal page.

items.heading: Further Financial Support
items.bodyText:
Additional support can be available for students with learning difficulties or disabilities, including mental health conditions. For further information, take a look at the Disabled Students’ Allowance web page. Contact our Student Support team for assistance.

There is also additional support available for students with children or dependent adults. Find out more about extra financial help on the Student Finance England website.

contentBlocks.bodyText:
Child Trust Funds or CTFs are tax-free savings accounts for children born between 1 September 2002 and 2 January 2011.

Child Trust Funds were introduced by the UK government with the aim of giving all children a financial nest egg by the time they reached 18. The government paid more than £2 billion into CTFs for 6.3 million children born during the period. Children can access this money when they turn 18, but many have lost track of them.

The scheme was ended in 2011, and parents/guardians were able to switch CTF accounts into a Junior ISA. However, a report by the National Audit Office found that despite this, there are still about 6.3 million CTFs in existence, with the average account holding £1,911.

If you were born between 1 September 2002 and 2 January 2011, and your parents received Child Benefit, you most likely have a Child Trust Fund account. You can find out more online about how to access this account and claim the funds at www.gov.uk/child-trust-funds

  • Read more about Child Trust Funds on thetimes.co.uk
  • Read HMRC's guide, 10 Things to Know About Child Trust Funds

As part of the University’s commitment to access and participation, there is a package of financial support available to provide targeted support to students with the greatest additional needs or to those experiencing specific financial burden. This will help enable students to fully partake in university life and have the same opportunities as others to complete their course and progress to graduate employment or further study.

Hardship Fund

The HE Hardship Fund is a cash award from the University which does not need to be paid back. It is only available to those HE students experiencing unforeseen and severe financial hardship.

The purpose of the fund is to support cases of severe financial hardship, which affect a student continuing with their studies, which could not have been planned for such as:

  • Being made redundant

  • The end of a relationship

  • Needing to move to a new home due to domestic violence or being the victim of theft

  • Significant change in travel or childcare costs or increased care responsibilities

  • Travel costs related to bereavement, or to visit a sick relative, or in connection with your own medical treatment

The fund is open to all Undergraduate and Postgraduate students (not franchise students) who are experiencing hardship and are:

  • enrolled and attending timetabled sessions

  • up to date with tuition fee payments

  • able to provide evidence to support their claim, including bank statements

Before applying for Hardship Funds you are expected to have applied for all funding available to you, for example the maintenance loan, tuition fee loan and any additional grants or benefits/tax credits. You’re also expected to have taken advantage of any alternative sources of funding available to you including an interest free overdraft.

Details on the amount available to claim will be published on the Student Portal at the start of each academic year, and the fund is limited so we may not be able to meet your needs in full or guarantee that funds will be available, especially towards the end of the academic year.

Discounts and progression awards

There are a range of awards and discounts available for those who have previously studied at Arts University Plymouth.

  • Alumni Progression Award: 15% discount on MA fees for Undergraduate, Pre-Degree and FAD graduates who go on to postgraduate study with us.
Postgraduate Funding

If you’re starting a master’s degree, you could get a Postgraduate Master’s Loan to help with course fees and living costs. You can get up to £13,206 if your course starts on or after 1 August 2026. The quickest and easiest way for students to apply is on the UK Government website's postgraduate loan page.

Eligibility depends on:

  • your course

  • your age

  • your nationality or residency status

The amount you’ll get is not based on your income or your family’s.

For an overview of Postgraduate funding visit the UCAS Student Finance guide.

For more information and support on student finances please contact admissions@aup.ac.uk

Further Financial Support

Additional support can be available for students with learning difficulties or disabilities, including mental health conditions. For further information about funding, take a look at the Disabled Students’ Allowance web page. Contact our Student Support team for assistance.

*Fees shown on this page provide an indication of current costs and exclude costs for international students who may need a pre-sessional English course and ongoing in-year English language support. For more information please visit our International pages.

*Fees shown on this page provide an indication of current costs and exclude costs for international students who may need a pre-sessional English course and ongoing in-year English language support. For more information please visit our International pages.

children.title: Student Support (Postgraduate)
children.summary: Our Student Support team offers a team of specialist advisors who can provide MA students with information and guidance in a variety of areas, including finance and funding, disability support, counselling, health and wellbeing.

children.title: Learning, Teaching & Assessment
children.summary: Our Postgraduate courses are delivered and supported through a diverse range of learning and teaching experiences. Here you’ll find fashion designers, ceramicists, games designers, fine artists and photographers, all sharing facilities and ideas.

children.title: Key Dates (Postgraduate)
children.summary: Read our latest update for new and returning postgraduate students, including opening times, term dates, enrolment information, reading weeks, and more.

children.title: Frequently Asked Questions
children.summary: Is an MA the right choice for me? How can I fit it around my other commitments? What do I need in order to apply? See the answers to some of the most frequently asked questions about postgraduate study.

image.title: Smiling students Masters Postgraduate Plymouth College of Art

children.title: Undergraduate
children.summary: As an undergraduate student on one of our BA (Hons) degrees or the four-year Integrated Foundation programme, you will join a close-knit community of creatives, for whom making is as important as reading and writing.

children.title: Postgraduate
children.summary: Explore postgraduate study in art, design, craft and media at Arts University Plymouth, with a practice-led curriculum, a cross-disciplinary postgraduate community, specialist facilities and full-time or part-time study options.

pages.text: Arts University Plymouth Logo Skip to Content Our Courses Open Days Apply Now Menu Apply Now Our Courses Open Days Chevron Down About Us Chevron Down Study Chevron Down International Chevron Down Student Life Alumni Chevron Down Visit Resources Chevron Down Research & Innovation Prospectus Latest News What's On Established 1856 Student Login Staff Login Contact Us Study Study Undergraduate Last updated October 2026 In this section In this section Study Undergraduate How to Apply Next Steps After Your Offer Careers & Enterprise Sandwich Year Fees, Finance and Funding Learning, Teaching & Assessment Student Support (Undergraduate) Key Dates (Undergraduate) Parents and guardians: supporting an undergraduate application Frequently Asked Questions Postgraduate progression with the Royal College of Art Postgraduate Pre-Degree Creativity doesn’t just happen in the studio, workshop or darkroom. It’s a way of life. A lot has changed here since we started out over 170 years ago, but this simple equation of making and living still shapes everything we do. At Arts University Plymouth, we invite and inspire new modes of creative practice that redefine citizenship in the 21st century. Our undergraduate programmes examine the interconnectedness of the arts and society, exploring distinct disciplines, expanded fields of study, and the spaces emerging between, across and beyond. Located in the coastal city of Plymouth with many points of access to the world, we encourage our students to work at the threshold of their practice, gaining new knowledge through shifting boundaries and unexpected routes. Studying here, creative practice is not merely aesthetics or making forms, it is making futures — yours and ours. Our BA Honours degrees demand an energetic and inquisitive approach to critically underpinned practice, which is central to all the programmes. As well as producing practical creative outcomes to a range of projects and live assignments you will also be expected to contextualise your ideas throughout the course, allowing writing to influence the development of practical work and vice versa. Atemporal by Harriet Kotvics, BA (Hons) Fine Art BA (Hons) Degrees Our programme of BA (Hons) degrees has a consistent structure and direction, ensuring that all subjects have business and professional practice embedded throughout. The first year is an introduction to processes and materials, and to the differences, for example between working as a freelancer and as part of an organisation within the industry. You’ll also be introduced to contemporary issues, concepts and approaches in the area that you choose to study. Across the range of programmes, you’ll develop strong visual awareness and communication skills. The second year builds on these foundations, and you’ll concentrate on refining your creative practice by working on live briefs, undertaking work placements, or preparing for internships. It’s an ideal time to explore the potential of cross-disciplinary approaches in the studio, before beginning your third year review of your practice. You’ll continue to refine your practice in the final year, and have the opportunity to enhance your practical and professional skills, culminating in an exhibition at our annual Degree Shows. Students have also exhibited nationally at New Designers, Free Range, D&AD New Blood and Graduate Fashion Week. Duration BA (Hons) degree level study takes place over three years full-time, or six years part-time. Please note a part-time study mode is not available on all courses. For more information visit our course pages. Integrated Foundation students commit to a four-year study programme, including a preparatory year before specialising on a BA (Hons) degree course. Fees Scholarships of up to £2,000 per year may be available for international students, subject to eligibility and availability. For information on part-time study fees please email admissions@aup.ac.uk . Please note we do not offer part-time study for international undergraduate students. BA (Hons) Degrees Full-time UK students: click here Full-time EU & International Students: click here Integrated Foundation (previously titled Extended BA) Full-time UK students: click here Full-time EU & International Students: click here Entry Requirements BA (Hons) Degrees We offer places to students who have a GCSE profile of at least five GCSEs, grades 9 - 4 (A* - C) , including English Language. Applicants also need a portfolio and 104 - 120 UCAS points , earned through an Art & Design Foundation Diploma, A-levels, BTEC Extended Diploma MMM grade, Access to HE Art & Design, T-Levels, Irish/Scottish Highers/Advanced Highers, the International Baccalaureate, or other international qualifications. We welcome applications from candidates without formal qualifications who can provide evidence of their creativity. We also welcome applications directly into the second and third years of our BA (Hons) programmes from students from other degree courses nationally, and from those from Foundation Degrees and Higher National Diplomas (HNDs) who want to complete their full BA (Hons). The tariff points shown online are valid for the current application cycle only. Integrated Foundation We offer places to students who have at least five GCSEs, grades 9 - 4 (A* - C) , including English Language and a combination of AS and A-level qualifications or equivalent (with one in a creative subject). We also welcome applications from mature students who may not have the qualification profile but have other experience and knowledge. All applicants will be required to show a portfolio of creative work. Academics have received overwhelmingly positive feedback from our students on the level of support and personal connection that they continue to receive. In fact, many students have reported that they feel like they’re receiving a more personalised learning experience than ever before. Paul Fieldsend-Danks, Vice-Chancellor Integrated Foundation The Integrated Foundation entry year programme is year one of a four-year degree and is designed as a preparatory year to ready you for the transition to the full degree programme of your choice. This route provides an opportunity to develop your portfolio and technical skills in a specialist subject area. We offer places to students who have at least five GCSEs, grades 9 - 4 (A* - C), including English Language and a combination of AS and A-level qualifications or equivalent (with one in a creative subject). We also welcome applications from mature students who may not have the qualification profile but have other experience and knowledge. All applicants will be required to show a portfolio of creative work. We collaborate We’re an independent arts university with an internationally distinctive identity. Here you’ll find fashion designers, ceramicists, games designers, fine artists and photographers, all sharing facilities and ideas. It’s a truly collaborative cross-disciplinary environment. Nationally, we have been a Founding Associate of Tate Exchange and internationally we act as advisors to the Cheongju International Craft Biennale. Our contribution to the creative industries and cultural agenda continues to grow, offering more opportunities each year to collaborate with leading artists from around the world. Find out about our facilities on the Resources pages or take a virtual tour. Unrivalled access We believe that contemporary arts practice is the catalyst for personal, professional and cultural transformation, and in order to achieve this we pride ourselves in providing high levels of contact time and studio access , not just a few timetabled hours a week. Living what you do means getting immersed in learning, and that requires constant access to the facilities, technicians and tuition that you need to develop. Find out more on our Learning, Teaching and Assessment page. Take a Virtual Tour Explore the university campus and local environment in our latest 360 tour. Arrow Right View our Courses From BA (Hons) and MA degrees, to post-16 Extended Diplomas — find your future in creative education. Arrow Right Industry ready From day one on campus you will be encouraged to think of yourself as a professional practitioner. Whatever you wish to do, we can support you during your studies and help you to fulfil your long-term career aspirations. Our students go on to direct music videos for Dua Lipa , pitch fashions for ASOS, design games for Playstation and shoot photography for The Guardian . Employability is at the heart of our curriculum design. We will bolster your practical and theoretical learning with an enviable programme of visiting lecturers, live projects and industry placements. Alongside professional development, you’ll also gain skills in business planning, entrepreneurialism, project management, creative direction and budgeting. Working with you we’ll ensure your creative practice becomes a springboard to lifelong fulfilment and a rewarding career in the competitive creative industries. Find out more about Employability at Arts University Plymouth on our Careers & Enterprise page. Postgraduate progression with the Royal College of Art Our agreement with the Royal College of Art supports graduates from 13 Arts University Plymouth undergraduate courses who are considering relevant RCA postgraduate programmes. The route provides application guidance, portfolio preparation and progression planning. Undergraduate degrees are taught and awarded by Arts University Plymouth, and admission to the RCA remains subject to its entry requirements. Explore the eligible courses and RCA progression route, including scholarships for 2027/28 entry . Global Horizons Any history of Plymouth has to include the horizon. We are an international arts university, welcoming students from around the world to share ideas and practice, and we encourage our students to explore global opportunities and horizons. We use our onsite exhibition space, MIRROR, to showcase international creative artists, and we welcome guest lecturers from overseas at every opportunity, as well as curating, publishing and exhibiting abroad ourselves, and arranging exchange programmes with our partners overseas. Find out more on our International pages . BA (Hons) Animation students exhibit videomapping at Fete de l'Anim, Euranim Projects 2016. Image © Morgan Rio. Close-knit community Atmosphere is a hard thing to put into words, but so many people who come to our undergraduate campus say the same thing: it feels like home. Small but mighty, our talented community of undergraduate students, expert academics and highly-specialised technicians prides itself on ingenuity. Together we experiment, innovate and make things happen! Our visitors say there’s a “family feeling” and “energy in the air” at Arts University Plymouth, and we have to agree. Wandering our undergraduate campus you’ll find filmmakers mingling with fine artists, ceramicists collaborating with costume designers, and staff conversing with students. You’re not a face in a crowd or a number on the list, you’re our top priority. Hear from current students and discover why they chose to study in Plymouth or find out about our Students' Union . Inspiring surroundings From unspoilt coastline and countryside to top clubs, arts venues and historic sites. Whatever you’re into, there’s something close to Arts University Plymouth for you to enjoy. Whether you’re staying at home or your heart is set on a sea-view apartment, city-centre townhouse or lively student halls experience, Plymouth has a long-held reputation for it’s fun and friendly student scene and there are renting options to suit all budgets. Here you’ll meet new friends, make memories and above all, feel safe and secure in your first home away from home. Find out more on our Student Life pages. Take a virtual walk through some of Plymouth's stunning surrounding coastline. Get in touch When you’re ready to get to know the university further, we recommend you book a one-to-one chat with our student recruitment team. You can informally discuss your aspirations, gain portfolio advice and application support, or ask to be connected with a subject leader from the courses you’re interested in. No question is too big or small! Please email hello@aup.ac.uk or call +44 (0)1752 203434 to get started. You can also speak to us via Whatsapp on 07722 744184 or arrange a video call via Google Meet. Get your prospectus Get to know Arts University Plymouth and our vibrant community in print or request a downloadable PDF. Whether you’re staying at home or your heart is set on a sea-view apartment, city-centre townhouse or lively student halls experience, Plymouth has a long-held reputation for it’s fun and friendly student scene and there are renting options to suit all budgets. Here you’ll meet new friends, make memories and above all, feel safe and secure in your first home away from home.

Find out more on our Student Life pages.

Take a virtual walk through some of Plymouth's stunning surrounding coastline. Get in touch

When you’re ready to get to know the university further, we recommend you book a one-to-one chat with our student recruitment team. You can informally discuss your aspirations, gain portfolio advice and application support, or ask to be connected with a subject leader from the courses you’re interested in. No question is too big or small!

Please email hello@aup.ac.uk or call +44 (0)1752 203434 to get started. You can also speak to us via Whatsapp on 07722 744184 or arrange a video call via Google Meet.

pageEntry.title: Undergraduate
pageEntry.summary: As an undergraduate student on one of our BA (Hons) degrees or the four-year Integrated Foundation programme, you will join a close-knit community of creatives, for whom making is as important as reading and writing.

image.title: Concrete and glass sculpture by Colin Wilkes, BA (Hons) 3D Design Crafts

contentBlocks.text: Creativity doesn’t just happen in the studio, workshop or darkroom. It’s a way of life. A lot has changed here since we started out over 170 years ago, but this simple equation of making and living still shapes everything we do.

contentBlocks.bodyText:
At Arts University Plymouth, we invite and inspire new modes of creative practice that redefine citizenship in the 21st century. Our undergraduate programmes examine the interconnectedness of the arts and society, exploring distinct disciplines, expanded fields of study, and the spaces emerging between, across and beyond.

Located in the coastal city of Plymouth with many points of access to the world, we encourage our students to work at the threshold of their practice, gaining new knowledge through shifting boundaries and unexpected routes. Studying here, creative practice is not merely aesthetics or making forms, it is making futures — yours and ours.

Our BA Honours degrees demand an energetic and inquisitive approach to critically underpinned practice, which is central to all the programmes. As well as producing practical creative outcomes to a range of projects and live assignments you will also be expected to contextualise your ideas throughout the course, allowing writing to influence the development of practical work and vice versa.

image.title: In a white exhibition space, long pieces of off-white fabric hang from the ceiling with the ends tucked into black boxes. The material has black edges with small text printed on it.
image.caption: Atemporal by Harriet Kotvics, BA (Hons) Fine Art

contentBlocks.caption: Atemporal by Harriet Kotvics, BA (Hons) Fine Art

contentBlocks.bodyText:
Our programme of BA (Hons) degrees has a consistent structure and direction, ensuring that all subjects have business and professional practice embedded throughout. The first year is an introduction to processes and materials, and to the differences, for example between working as a freelancer and as part of an organisation within the industry.

You’ll also be introduced to contemporary issues, concepts and approaches in the area that you choose to study. Across the range of programmes, you’ll develop strong visual awareness and communication skills. The second year builds on these foundations, and you’ll concentrate on refining your creative practice by working on live briefs, undertaking work placements, or preparing for internships.

It’s an ideal time to explore the potential of cross-disciplinary approaches in the studio, before beginning your third year review of your practice. You’ll continue to refine your practice in the final year, and have the opportunity to enhance your practical and professional skills, culminating in an exhibition at our annual Degree Shows. Students have also exhibited nationally at New Designers, Free Range, D&AD New Blood and Graduate Fashion Week.

items.heading: Duration
items.bodyText:
• BA (Hons) degree level study takes place over three years full-time, or six years part-time. Please note a part-time study mode is not available on all courses. For more information visit our course pages.
  • Integrated Foundation students commit to a four-year study programme, including a preparatory year before specialising on a BA (Hons) degree course.

items.heading: Fees
items.bodyText:
Scholarships of up to £2,000 per year may be available for international students, subject to eligibility and availability. For information on part-time study fees please email admissions@aup.ac.uk. Please note we do not offer part-time study for international undergraduate students.

items.heading: Entry Requirements
items.bodyText:
• BA (Hons) Degrees
    • We offer places to students who have a GCSE profile of at least five GCSEs, grades 9 - 4 (A* - C), including English Language.
    • Applicants also need a portfolio and 104 - 120 UCAS points, earned through an Art & Design Foundation Diploma, A-levels, BTEC Extended Diploma MMM grade, Access to HE Art & Design, T-Levels, Irish/Scottish Highers/Advanced Highers, the International Baccalaureate, or other international qualifications.
    • We welcome applications from candidates without formal qualifications who can provide evidence of their creativity.
    • We also welcome applications directly into the second and third years of our BA (Hons) programmes from students from other degree courses nationally, and from those from Foundation Degrees and Higher National Diplomas (HNDs) who want to complete their full BA (Hons).
    • The tariff points shown online are valid for the current application cycle only.
  • Integrated Foundation
    • We offer places to students who have at least five GCSEs, grades 9 - 4 (A* - C), including English Language and a combination of AS and A-level qualifications or equivalent (with one in a creative subject).
    • We also welcome applications from mature students who may not have the qualification profile but have other experience and knowledge. All applicants will be required to show a portfolio of creative work.

contentBlocks.blockquote: Academics have received overwhelmingly positive feedback from our students on the level of support and personal connection that they continue to receive. In fact, many students have reported that they feel like they’re receiving a more personalised learning experience than ever before.
contentBlocks.attribution: Paul Fieldsend-Danks, Vice-Chancellor

image.title: A girl in a yellow top sits at a desk working on an art sculpture built from multicoloured strings.

contentBlocks.bodyText:
The Integrated Foundation entry year programme is year one of a four-year degree and is designed as a preparatory year to ready you for the transition to the full degree programme of your choice.

This route provides an opportunity to develop your portfolio and technical skills in a specialist subject area. We offer places to students who have at least five GCSEs, grades 9 - 4 (A* - C), including English Language and a combination of AS and A-level qualifications or equivalent (with one in a creative subject). We also welcome applications from mature students who may not have the qualification profile but have other experience and knowledge. All applicants will be required to show a portfolio of creative work.

image.title: A man stands in a white gallery space looking at two framed photographs showing landscapes of forests.

contentBlocks.heading: We collaborate
contentBlocks.bodyText:
We’re an independent arts university with an internationally distinctive identity. Here you’ll find fashion designers, ceramicists, games designers, fine artists and photographers, all sharing facilities and ideas. It’s a truly collaborative cross-disciplinary environment.

Nationally, we have been a Founding Associate of Tate Exchange and internationally we act as advisors to the Cheongju International Craft Biennale. Our contribution to the creative industries and cultural agenda continues to grow, offering more opportunities each year to collaborate with leading artists from around the world.

Find out about our facilities on the Resources pages or take a virtual tour.

contentBlocks.heading: Unrivalled access
contentBlocks.bodyText:
We believe that contemporary arts practice is the catalyst for personal, professional and cultural transformation, and in order to achieve this we pride ourselves in providing high levels of contact time and studio access, not just a few timetabled hours a week.

Living what you do means getting immersed in learning, and that requires constant access to the facilities, technicians and tuition that you need to develop.

Find out more on our Learning, Teaching and Assessment page.

contentBlocks.heading: Industry ready
contentBlocks.bodyText:
From day one on campus you will be encouraged to think of yourself as a professional practitioner. Whatever you wish to do, we can support you during your studies and help you to fulfil your long-term career aspirations. Our students go on to direct music videos for Dua Lipa, pitch fashions for ASOS, design games for Playstation and shoot photography for The Guardian.

Employability is at the heart of our curriculum design. We will bolster your practical and theoretical learning with an enviable programme of visiting lecturers, live projects and industry placements.

Alongside professional development, you’ll also gain skills in business planning, entrepreneurialism, project management, creative direction and budgeting. Working with you we’ll ensure your creative practice becomes a springboard to lifelong fulfilment and a rewarding career in the competitive creative industries.

Find out more about Employability at Arts University Plymouth on our Careers & Enterprise page.

contentBlocks.heading: Postgraduate progression with the Royal College of Art
contentBlocks.bodyText:
Our agreement with the Royal College of Art supports graduates from 13 Arts University Plymouth undergraduate courses who are considering relevant RCA postgraduate programmes.

The route provides application guidance, portfolio preparation and progression planning. Undergraduate degrees are taught and awarded by Arts University Plymouth, and admission to the RCA remains subject to its entry requirements.

Explore the eligible courses and RCA progression route, including scholarships for 2027/28 entry.

contentBlocks.heading: Global Horizons
contentBlocks.bodyText:
Any history of Plymouth has to include the horizon. We are an international arts university, welcoming students from around the world to share ideas and practice, and we encourage our students to explore global opportunities and horizons.

We use our onsite exhibition space, MIRROR, to showcase international creative artists, and we welcome guest lecturers from overseas at every opportunity, as well as curating, publishing and exhibiting abroad ourselves, and arranging exchange programmes with our partners overseas.

Find out more on our International pages.

image.title: An evening in the city of Lille, France looking out onto a large crowd all watching a videomapped projection on an old building.

contentBlocks.caption: BA (Hons) Animation students exhibit videomapping at Fete de l'Anim, Euranim Projects 2016. Image © Morgan Rio.

contentBlocks.heading: Close-knit community
contentBlocks.bodyText:
Atmosphere is a hard thing to put into words, but so many people who come to our undergraduate campus say the same thing: it feels like home.

Small but mighty, our talented community of undergraduate students, expert academics and highly-specialised technicians prides itself on ingenuity. Together we experiment, innovate and make things happen!

Our visitors say there’s a “family feeling” and “energy in the air” at Arts University Plymouth, and we have to agree. Wandering our undergraduate campus you’ll find filmmakers mingling with fine artists, ceramicists collaborating with costume designers, and staff conversing with students. You’re not a face in a crowd or a number on the list, you’re our top priority.

Hear from current students and discover why they chose to study in Plymouth or find out about our Students' Union.

Last updated April 2026 In this section In this section Study Undergraduate Postgraduate How to Apply Our Postgraduate Staff The Postgraduate Centre Fees, Finance & Funding Student Support (Postgraduate) Learning, Teaching & Assessment Key Dates (Postgraduate) Frequently Asked Questions Pre-Degree Our postgraduate programmes invite you to explore and refine your creative practice by critically engaging with the cultural, technological and economic changes shaping our world. At Arts University Plymouth, you will study in a specialist arts university led by practising artists, designers and researchers, and join the Postgraduate Centre, an active, cross-disciplinary community of makers and thinkers. Whether you want to deepen your existing practice, change direction or accelerate your career, postgraduate study here gives you the time, space and critical support to develop a substantial body of work in Plymouth, a creative coastal city in the South West. At a glance Study a portfolio of MA courses across design , studio arts , media and craft disciplines Choose full-time study over one year or part-time study over two years Learn through a practice-led curriculum built around research methods, creative development and a final independent project Join the Postgraduate Centre , a dedicated cross-disciplinary community shared by MA students and alumni Learn from research-active staff, practising artists, designers and visiting experts Access specialist workshops, studios and technical support, alongside MIRROR, Plymouth Arts Cinema and Fab Lab South West Take part in Research Intensives, critiques, exhibitions and professional development opportunities Arts University Plymouth alumni can receive a 15% fee discount through the Alumni Progression Award Why choose Postgraduate study at Arts University Plymouth? Postgraduate study at Arts University Plymouth is designed for artists, designers, makers, writers, educators and creative practitioners who want to push their work further in a critical, practice-led environment. You might be building on a recent degree, returning to study after time in industry, or looking for a focused space in which to test ideas, expand your research and develop a clearer professional direction. Our MA courses bring together specialist study and cross-disciplinary exchange. You will develop your work within your chosen discipline while learning alongside students from different creative backgrounds, helping you see your own practice from fresh perspectives and situate it more clearly within contemporary culture. As a small specialist university, Arts University Plymouth offers a distinctive postgraduate experience: close staff contact, a strong sense of community, and a city-centre creative environment connected to Plymouth, the South West and wider professional networks. GRADUATE SHOWS 2025 | Postgraduate Private View at Arts University Plymouth What is the Postgraduate Centre? As an MA student at Arts University Plymouth you will join our Postgraduate Centre, an active, cross-disciplinary community of makers and thinkers. It is a dedicated base for postgraduate study, used by MA cohorts and alumni, and a space for discussion, making, peer exchange and reflective development. This shared environment is central to how postgraduate study works here. Studio conversations, seminars, critiques and self-directed study all contribute to a culture in which your ideas can be tested, refined and challenged in dialogue with others. The Postgraduate Centre also reflects one of the university’s key strengths: an arts university run by artists and designers, for artists and designers, where thinking and making are closely connected. What and how will you study on an MA? Our postgraduate courses allow you to learn your chosen discipline through a practice-led curriculum that helps you encounter how it is currently understood and challenged within contemporary culture. You will learn by developing a body of work, informed by research methods that help you delve deeper into the theories, practices and professional contexts most relevant to your field. All MA courses are organised around three units of study: Unit 701: Practice-Led Research Methods You will start to build an iterative body of written or studio-based work and be introduced to research-based skills and frameworks. Unit 702: Creative & Critical Development You will put your research into action through participation in Research Intensives that expand your knowledge and understanding of your subject. Unit 703: Final Independent Project You will develop a final body of work or project, culminating in a public display or presentation. The learning modality for MA study is a combination of taught content through lectures, critiques and tutorials and self-directed study. A full-time student would need to commit at least four days per week to MA study. A part-time student should commit at least two days per week to MA study, including one taught day and one self-directed study day. Take a look at our Postgraduate courses Join an active, cross-disciplinary community of makers and thinkers. Arrow Right What postgraduate courses can you study? Our portfolio of MA courses spans design disciplines and studio art, media and craft disciplines, giving you the opportunity to deepen your specialist practice within a multidisciplinary environment. Design-focused MA courses MA Design MA Design (Built Environment) MA Design (Communication) MA Design (Fashion) MA Design (Textiles) Studio art, media and craft MA courses MA Craft & Material Practices MA Fine Art MA Glass MA Immersive Media MA Museum Studies MA courses in design share a concern for designing with planet and people in mind, while MA courses in studio arts, media and craft support the development of an independent voice through self-directed practice and critical reflection. Across both areas, the emphasis is on building a body of work that reflects your unique voice, skills and insights. What do our MA students say? “Completing my MA at Arts University Plymouth was almost like being in a production house. Everything is at your fingertips. You just have to ask. I could move between glass casting, projection mapping and VR with support from artists and technicians who were excited to help. Bring your skills and your intentions with you. Even if you’re not tech-savvy, don’t be put off. You can learn quickly. What matters most is your ideas.” Kelly Bryant, MA Fine Art What facilities, research and opportunities will support your practice? Postgraduate students study in a research-intensive environment shaped by active makers and researchers. Alongside specialist workshops, studios and technical support, you will engage with a wider research culture through seminars, critiques, public talks and Research Intensives led by research-active staff and external specialists. You will also be in regular contact with Fab Lab South West , part of the international MIT Fab Lab network, Plymouth Arts Cinema , the only independent cinema in Plymouth, and MIRROR , our on-campus public gallery. Together, these spaces help connect your work to current conversations in contemporary art, design, media and material practice. Depending on your course and timing, postgraduate study can also open up opportunities including professional exhibitions, residencies, placements, fellowships, bursaries and research activity. These opportunities help you test your ideas beyond the taught curriculum and build confidence in presenting your work publicly and professionally. How does postgraduate study connect to research and innovation? Arts University Plymouth is a centre of practice-led creative research where artists, designers and authors explore new ideas through making. As a postgraduate student, you study within this wider research environment and benefit from direct contact with emergent thinking in creative practice, creative education, material innovation and cross-disciplinary enquiry. This environment is shaped by staff-led research groups including Making Learning , Memory, Site, Artefact and Material Futures , as well as initiatives such as StudioLab for Embodied Media , the Centre for Circular Materials and the biennial Making Futures™ conference. For students who want to deepen their practice, develop new methods or build towards future research, this creates a strong context for ambitious postgraduate study. Whether you want to deepen your existing practice, change direction or accelerate your career, postgraduate study here gives you the time, space and critical support to develop a substantial body of work in Plymouth, a creative coastal city in the South West.

At a glance

Why choose Postgraduate study at Arts University Plymouth?

Postgraduate study at Arts University Plymouth is designed for artists, designers, makers, writers, educators and creative practitioners who want to push their work further in a critical, practice-led environment. You might be building on a recent degree, returning to study after time in industry, or looking for a focused space in which to test ideas, expand your research and develop a clearer professional direction.

Our MA courses bring together specialist study and cross-disciplinary exchange. You will develop your work within your chosen discipline while learning alongside students from different creative backgrounds, helping you see your own practice from fresh perspectives and situate it more clearly within contemporary culture.

As a small specialist university, Arts University Plymouth offers a distinctive postgraduate experience: close staff contact, a strong sense of community, and a city-centre creative environment connected to Plymouth, the South West and wider professional networks.

GRADUATE SHOWS 2025 | Postgraduate Private View at Arts University Plymouth What is the Postgraduate Centre?

As an MA student at Arts University Plymouth you will join our Postgraduate Centre, an active, cross-disciplinary community of makers and thinkers. It is a dedicated base for postgraduate study, used by MA cohorts and alumni, and a space for discussion, making, peer exchange and reflective development.

This shared environment is central to how postgraduate study works here. Studio conversations, seminars, critiques and self-directed study all contribute to a culture in which your ideas can be tested, refined and challenged in dialogue with others.

The Postgraduate Centre also reflects one of the university’s key strengths: an arts university run by artists and designers, for artists and designers, where thinking and making are closely connected.

What and how will you study on an MA?

Our postgraduate courses allow you to learn your chosen discipline through a practice-led curriculum that helps you encounter how it is currently understood and challenged within contemporary culture. You will learn by developing a body of work, informed by research methods that help you delve deeper into the theories, practices and professional contexts most relevant to your field.

All MA courses are organised around three units of study:

  • Unit 701: Practice-Led Research Methods
    You will start to build an iterative body of written or studio-based work and be introduced to research-based skills and frameworks.

  • Unit 702: Creative & Critical Development
    You will put your research into action through participation in Research Intensives that expand your knowledge and understanding of your subject.

  • Unit 703: Final Independent Project
    You will develop a final body of work or project, culminating in a public display or presentation.

The learning modality for MA study is a combination of taught content through lectures, critiques and tutorials and self-directed study. A full-time student would need to commit at least four days per week to MA study. A part-time student should commit at least two days per week to MA study, including one taught day and one self-directed study day.

Take a look at our Postgraduate courses Join an active, cross-disciplinary community of makers and thinkers. Arrow Right What postgraduate courses can you study?

Our portfolio of MA courses spans design disciplines and studio art, media and craft disciplines, giving you the opportunity to deepen your specialist practice within a multidisciplinary environment.

Design-focused MA courses

  • MA Design
  • MA Design (Built Environment)
  • MA Design (Communication)
  • MA Design (Fashion)
  • MA Design (Textiles)

Studio art, media and craft MA courses

  • MA Craft & Material Practices
  • MA Fine Art
  • MA Glass
  • MA Immersive Media
  • MA Museum Studies

MA courses in design share a concern for designing with planet and people in mind, while MA courses in studio arts, media and craft support the development of an independent voice through self-directed practice and critical reflection. Across both areas, the emphasis is on building a body of work that reflects your unique voice, skills and insights.

What do our MA students say? “Completing my MA at Arts University Plymouth was almost like being in a production house. Everything is at your fingertips. You just have to ask. I could move between glass casting, projection mapping and VR with support from artists and technicians who were excited to help. Bring your skills and your intentions with you. Even if you’re not tech-savvy, don’t be put off. You can learn quickly. What matters most is your ideas.” Kelly Bryant, MA Fine Art What facilities, research and opportunities will support your practice?

Postgraduate students study in a research-intensive environment shaped by active makers and researchers. Alongside specialist workshops, studios and technical support, you will engage with a wider research culture through seminars, critiques, public talks and Research Intensives led by research-active staff and external specialists.

You will also be in regular contact with Fab Lab South West, part of the international MIT Fab Lab network, Plymouth Arts Cinema, the only independent cinema in Plymouth, and MIRROR, our on-campus public gallery. Together, these spaces help connect your work to current conversations in contemporary art, design, media and material practice.

Depending on your course and timing, postgraduate study can also open up opportunities including professional exhibitions, residencies, placements, fellowships, bursaries and research activity. These opportunities help you test your ideas beyond the taught curriculum and build confidence in presenting your work publicly and professionally.

How does postgraduate study connect to research and innovation?

Arts University Plymouth is a centre of practice-led creative research where artists, designers and authors explore new ideas through making. As a postgraduate student, you study within this wider research environment and benefit from direct contact with emergent thinking in creative practice, creative education, material innovation and cross-disciplinary enquiry.

This environment is shaped by staff-led research groups including Making Learning, Memory, Site, Artefact and Material Futures, as well as initiatives such as StudioLab for Embodied Media, the Centre for Circular Materials and the biennial Making Futures™ conference.

For students who want to deepen their practice, develop new methods or build towards future research, this creates a strong context for ambitious postgraduate study.

The university’s Careers and Enterprise team provides tools and workshops during your studies to help you plan your next steps after graduation, whether that means independent practice, portfolio work, further study, research, teaching or roles across the wider creative and cultural sectors.

The course encouraged me to connect digital innovation with emotional experiences, helping me create work that exists between art, design, and audience participation. Having access to such a collaborative environment really shaped how I thought about immersion, not just as technology but as a way to invite people into new ways of thinking, seeing, and feeling.” Jay Alexander, MA Immersive Media How do you apply?

To enrol on one of our MA courses, a first degree of at least a lower second class honours (2:2) in an art, design, craft or media discipline is normally required. We may also consider equivalent professional knowledge and demonstrated industry experience in individual cases.

As part of your application, you will be asked to provide digital images of your work and submit a short Personal Statement and Project Proposal, each with a maximum of 300 words. The Project Proposal is your opportunity to tell us what you want to investigate on your chosen MA course, the ideas or practitioners that inspire you, and your longer-term personal and professional goals.

You can apply via the Apply Now button on each course page. The best deadline to submit your MA application is 1 July, although late applications may be considered until the start of the course if places are still available. If you are an international applicant, please visit our website and search your country for country-specific entry and English language guidance.

Talk to us about postgraduate study

If you are considering postgraduate study, we recommend visiting an Open Event or arranging a one-to-one pre-application advisory meeting or campus tour. These are a good way to explore the university, hear from staff, students and alumni, and get a clearer sense of whether postgraduate study at Arts University Plymouth is right for you.

You can also download our latest Prospectus, read our Portfolio Guide, or book an informal online chat about postgraduate study with a member of our academic team.

For further information, email postgraduate@aup.ac.uk or call +44 (0)1752 203434.

Alumni Progression Award

Did you know Arts University Plymouth graduates are offered a discount of 15% on Masters programme fees? The Alumni Progression Award is available to all alumni, regardless of when they studied with us previously. The discount applies if you studied on one of our pre-degree, foundation or undergraduate programmes.

For more information please email hello@aup.ac.uk

contentBlocks.bodyText:
If you are considering postgraduate study, we recommend visiting an Open Event or arranging a one-to-one pre-application advisory meeting or campus tour. These are a good way to explore the university, hear from staff, students and alumni, and get a clearer sense of whether postgraduate study at Arts University Plymouth is right for you.

You can also download our latest Prospectus, read our Portfolio Guide, or book an informal online chat about postgraduate study with a member of our academic team.

For further information, email postgraduate@aup.ac.uk or call +44 (0)1752 203434.

Did you know Arts University Plymouth graduates are offered a discount of 15% on Masters programme fees? The Alumni Progression Award is available to all alumni, regardless of when they studied with us previously. The discount applies if you studied on one of our pre-degree, foundation or undergraduate programmes.

For more information please email hello@aup.ac.uk

stories.title: Alumni Shorts: Sue Lewry
stories.caption: An alumna of our BA (Hons) Graphic Communication and our MA Printmaking courses, Sue Lewry is a printmaker-artist whose interdisciplinary practice explores materiality, testing and experimenting. Sue uses digital and traditional methods to explore the agile art form of printmaking in both social engagement and solo practice.

stories.title: Gallery Shorts: Eleanor Duffin | A Phantom Limb
stories.caption: The Gallery, our on-site international exhibition space at Tavistock Place, recently presented A Phantom Limb - a series of letters written by Eleanor Duffin to the artist Barbara Hepworth.

stories.title: How One Designer Turned a City into an Alphabet
stories.caption:
Typetecture is a typographic system developed by designer Elena Ruiz as part of her Master’s degree in Visual Communication at Arts University Plymouth.

Drawing inspiration from Plymouth’s postwar architecture, Elena created a sculptural alphabet built from real-world details, manhole covers, spiral staircases, and the geometric logic of the city itself. The result is a bold, abstract visual language rooted in observation, memory, and place.

stories.title: Hidden Plymouth: Stories of Place and Memory with Jason Hirons
stories.caption: A walking journey with Jason Hirons into the hidden fabric of Plymouth - where place and memory meet.

items.heading: What is postgraduate study at Arts University Plymouth like?
items.bodyText: Postgraduate study at Arts University Plymouth is practice-led, cross-disciplinary and focused on helping you develop a substantial body of work through making, research and critical reflection. You will study within a specialist creative community centred on the Postgraduate Centre.

items.heading: Can I study part-time?
items.bodyText: Yes. You can study full-time over one year or part-time over two years.

items.heading: Do I need a 2:2 to apply?
items.bodyText: Applicants normally need a 2:2 or above in a related art, design, craft or media discipline. Equivalent professional knowledge and industry experience may also be considered in individual cases.

items.heading: What do I need to submit with my application?
items.bodyText: You will usually need digital images of your work, a Personal Statement and a Project Proposal of up to 300 words.

items.heading: Can I speak to someone before I apply?
items.bodyText: Yes. You can attend an Open Event, arrange a one-to-one pre-application advisory meeting or campus tour, or book an informal online chat about postgraduate study.

items.heading: What facilities will I be able to use?
items.bodyText: Postgraduate students benefit from access to specialist workshops, studios, technical support and the wider postgraduate environment, including MIRROR, Plymouth Arts Cinema and Fab Lab South West.

items.heading: Are there discounts for Arts University Plymouth alumni?
items.bodyText: Yes. Arts University Plymouth alumni can receive a 15% fee discount through the Alumni Progression Award.

items.heading: What kinds of opportunities are available beyond the studio?
items.bodyText: Depending on your course and timing, opportunities may include exhibitions, critiques, residencies, placements, fellowships, bursaries and research activity that help you develop your work in professional contexts.

items.heading: Where can I find course-specific information?
items.bodyText: You can explore each MA course in more detail on our postgraduate course pages, including course content, entry requirements and how to apply.

From our Undergraduate BA (Hons) Degree programmes and Integrated Foundation Year to our Postgraduate Masters Degrees and our range of Pre-Degree study options, we offer something for everyone looking to further their artistic practice. How to apply for our creative courses depends on the level of study for you. Applications for Undergraduate Degree programmes (unless part-time) are made via The Universities and Colleges Admissions Service (UCAS), a UK-based organisation whose main role is to operate the application process for British universities. Whilst for our Postgraduate programmes and Pre-Degree courses are made directly to Arts University Plymouth on our website. Undergraduate Applications If you’re over 18 years old and looking to study a BA (Hons) degree, you can apply to one of our undergraduate courses. We offer a range of highly-specialised degrees in art, design and media, providing students with access to state-of-the-art facilities and industry expertise. Follow our step-by-step guide below to begin making your application. 1) Note our UCAS Codes To apply through UCAS you’ll need our institution code P65 and the relevant course code - which is available on each course page . 2) Login to UCAS Apply You can apply to all of our undergraduate courses through UCAS. Click here to login and if you need any support you can call our friendly Admissions team on +44 (0)1752 203400 . Remember, the deadline for the majority of courses is 18:00 GMT on the last Wednesday of January. You can view entry requirements for each degree on our course pages and consult the UCAS Tariff Table . We recognise the value of a variety of qualifications and relevant experience and welcome applications from students who have followed less traditional routes. 2) Submit a portfolio If your application meets our entry requirements, we’ll invite you to submit a portfolio of work to be reviewed by one of our academics. We know there's more to applicants than the information noted on a personal statement, so we’re keen to give you an opportunity to share some of you work - and to show your creative potential for real. In some exceptional cases, we may also invite you to an online interview with a course leader - our Admissions team will contact you to arrange this if neccessary. For more information on preparing your portfolio, check out our top tips on our website. Browse our Undergraduate course listings. Postgraduate Applications As an MA student at Arts University Plymouth you will join our Postgraduate Centre, an active, cross-disciplinary community of makers and thinkers. You can apply for the postgraduate course you are interested in studying by clicking on the 'Apply Now' link situated top left on each course page . See our full-range of MA programmes on our course pages . Applying for an MA MA applicants are normally expected to have an undergraduate degree at 2:2 or above. However, the strength of your creative practice and other forms of experience will be taken into account at the interview stage and we encourage you to start a conversation with us. As part of the application, you will be asked to give the usual application details, to provide some digital images of your work , and to submit a short personal statement (300 words approximately). This personal statement is a chance to tell us what you want to do on your chosen MA. It might include details of the techniques or themes that you want to investigate, the creative practitioners that inspire you, the reading that fires your imagination, and your longer-term professional goals. If you meet the entrance requirements, we will get back to you within three weeks of receiving your application to invite you for an interview. You will have the opportunity to tell us more about your work at this stage and to ask more questions about your course. Alumni Progression Award Arts University Plymouth graduates are offered a discount of 15% on Masters programme fees, regardless of when they studied with us previously. The discount applies if you studied on one of our pre-degree, foundation or undergraduate programmes. Pre-degree Applications Applications to our Extended Diploma are made online. To start your application please click the ‘Apply Now’ button on the top-left of the relevant course page . As part of the pre-degree application process we invite international applicants to an online discussion with a course leader, where you can share your work and discuss the course in more detail. You can also tell us about any additional support you may need to study with us, so we can ensure this can be offered to you. Information regarding entry requirements - including qualifications and English Language requirements - can be found on our Your Country pages, or by emailing international@aup.ac.uk Extended Diplomas Extended Diplomas are a two-year Level 3 qualification, equivalent to 3 A-Levels. For international students, this may be suitable for applicants who may not have completed formal education in their home country or are recent school leavers. Foundation Diploma Our Foundation Diploma course is a 1 year intensive programme, ideally suited to applicants who wish to complete further studies before applying for an Undergraduate degree. We often receive applications from international students who have completed study in their home country but wish to enhance their knowledge and skills before applying for degree-level studies. All offers are subject to interview and a portfolio or showreel of creative work that reflects your commitment, enthusiasm and passion for art, design and media. We also welcome applications from students who may not have the required application profile but have alternative experience and knowledge. Portfolios, Showreels & Interviews All of our courses require a portfolio of work before any decision can be made on an offer of a place; this should be a range of work demonstrating your artistic ability and potential. If you’re successful, we’ll send you a letter offering you a place. In some cases, we will also invite you to an interview: this will be an online or telephone interview for international applicants, where you can meet an experienced member of academic staff who will talk you through the course. We often use Google Chat, Zoom and Whatsapp to hold a conversation with international applicants, so please let us know if you have a preferred means of contact.
