You can view entry requirements for each degree on our course pages and consult the UCAS Tariff Table. We recognise the value of a variety of qualifications and relevant experience and welcome applications from students who have followed less traditional routes.

2) Submit a portfolio

If your application meets our entry requirements, we’ll invite you to submit a portfolio of work to be reviewed by one of our academics. We know there's more to applicants than the information noted on a personal statement, so we’re keen to give you an opportunity to share some of you work - and to show your creative potential for real.

In some exceptional cases, we may also invite you to an online interview with a course leader - our Admissions team will contact you to arrange this if neccessary. For more information on preparing your portfolio, check out our top tips on our website.

Browse our Undergraduate course listings.

items.heading: Postgraduate Applications
items.bodyText:
As an MA student at Arts University Plymouth you will join our Postgraduate Centre, an active, cross-disciplinary community of makers and thinkers. You can apply for the postgraduate course you are interested in studying by clicking on the 'Apply Now' link situated top left on each course page.

See our full-range of MA programmes on our course pages.

Applying for an MA

MA applicants are normally expected to have an undergraduate degree at 2:2 or above. However, the strength of your creative practice and other forms of experience will be taken into account at the interview stage and we encourage you to start a conversation with us.

As part of the application, you will be asked to give the usual application details, to provide some digital images of your work, and to submit a short personal statement (300 words approximately). This personal statement is a chance to tell us what you want to do on your chosen MA. It might include details of the techniques or themes that you want to investigate, the creative practitioners that inspire you, the reading that fires your imagination, and your longer-term professional goals.

If you meet the entrance requirements, we will get back to you within three weeks of receiving your application to invite you for an interview. You will have the opportunity to tell us more about your work at this stage and to ask more questions about your course.

Alumni Progression Award

Arts University Plymouth graduates are offered a discount of 15% on Masters programme fees, regardless of when they studied with us previously. The discount applies if you studied on one of our pre-degree, foundation or undergraduate programmes.

items.heading: Pre-degree Applications
items.bodyText:
Applications to our Extended Diploma are made online. To start your application please click the ‘Apply Now’ button on the top-left of the relevant course page.

As part of the pre-degree application process we invite international applicants to an online discussion with a course leader, where you can share your work and discuss the course in more detail. You can also tell us about any additional support you may need to study with us, so we can ensure this can be offered to you.

Information regarding entry requirements - including qualifications and English Language requirements - can be found on our Your Country pages, or by emailing international@aup.ac.uk

Extended Diplomas

Extended Diplomas are a two-year Level 3 qualification, equivalent to 3 A-Levels. For international students, this may be suitable for applicants who may not have completed formal education in their home country or are recent school leavers.

Foundation Diploma

Our Foundation Diploma course is a 1 year intensive programme, ideally suited to applicants who wish to complete further studies before applying for an Undergraduate degree. We often receive applications from international students who have completed study in their home country but wish to enhance their knowledge and skills before applying for degree-level studies.

All offers are subject to interview and a portfolio or showreel of creative work that reflects your commitment, enthusiasm and passion for art, design and media.

We also welcome applications from students who may not have the required application profile but have alternative experience and knowledge.

contentBlocks.heading: Portfolios, Showreels & Interviews
contentBlocks.bodyText:
All of our courses require a portfolio of work before any decision can be made on an offer of a place; this should be a range of work demonstrating your artistic ability and potential. If you’re successful, we’ll send you a letter offering you a place.

In some cases, we will also invite you to an interview: this will be an online or telephone interview for international applicants, where you can meet an experienced member of academic staff who will talk you through the course.

We often use Google Chat, Zoom and Whatsapp to hold a conversation with international applicants, so please let us know if you have a preferred means of contact.

pages.text: Arts University Plymouth Logo Skip to Content Our Courses Open Days Apply Now Menu Apply Now Our Courses Open Days Chevron Down About Us Chevron Down Study Chevron Down International Chevron Down Student Life Alumni Chevron Down Visit Resources Chevron Down Research & Innovation Prospectus Latest News What's On Established 1856 Student Login Staff Login Contact Us Explore our Undergraduate courses BA (Hons) Painting, Drawing & Printmaking Course Duration Full-time: 3 years / Part-time: 6 years Integrated Foundation: Full-time 4 years / Part-time: 7 years Course Contact hello@aup.ac.uk Admissions Contact admissions@aup.ac.uk +44 (0)1752 203434 UCAS Code Course: WWDF Institution: P65 Apply Now Register your interest Overview Course & Units Entry Requirements Staff Student Work Careers & Alumni Ask a Student Resources Fees & Funding Overview BA (Hons) Painting, Drawing & Printmaking at Arts University Plymouth offers the only undergraduate degree in the UK that brings these three disciplines together in an holistic way, building on their rich history of nourishing and challenging each other. On this course, you'll explore painting , drawing and printmaking as three interconnected ways of thinking and making. You'll be given the space, support and practical skills to discover your artistic voice through imaginative questioning, material experimentation and skilled invention. Find out more about BA (Hons) Painting, Drawing & Printmaking at Arts University Plymouth. At a glance Degree: BA (Hons) Painting, Drawing & Printmaking UCAS codes: 3-year degree WWDF / 4-year Integrated Foundation W102 Typical UCAS points: 104–120 Studio focus: painting, drawing and printmaking taught as interconnected disciplines Why choose this painting, drawing and printmaking degree at Arts University Plymouth? Immerse yourself in material experimentation, critical imagining and skilled invention across painting, drawing and printmaking. Learn from professional artists who understand the challenges and rewards of creative practice and can guide you in developing your own visual language. Study in light and airy studios , with dedicated facilities for crafting an ambitious practice. Build specialist and transferable skills to open up a fulfilling and enduring creative career. “Reflecting back on my degree, it’s certainly been a life changing experience for me as a fine artist and as part of the wider university community. I embarked upon my degree with low self-confidence and self-esteem, and I would never have imagined being confident enough to achieve a degree. The staff at Arts University Plymouth have coached me and taught me how to be a fine artist in today’s world.” Ruth Brown Student work by Matilda Smyth, BA (Hons) Painting, Drawing & Printmaking graduate 2025 What you’ll learn and how you’ll study You’ll learn through hands-on experimentation , testing materials , processes , approaches and ideas , and reflecting on what you’re doing and why. Regular tutorials, seminars, lectures and group discussions help you develop confidence, identify relevant contexts for your work, and engage with diverse histories and current debates. Workshops introduce traditional techniques, including intaglio printing and making your own paints from raw pigments, which you’ll explore alongside technologies and know-how from across Arts University Plymouth’s world-class facilities. A student using the facilities in our fine print studio. You’ll work in a specialist studio environment designed to support focus, curiosity and ambition. As well as course teaching, you can book additional access to specialist facilities for self-directed development through SmartHub, with a guaranteed 11 hours each week during the teaching year. In printmaking, you can develop a broad technical range, with access to processes such as screen-printing, etching, drypoint, aquatint, lino, woodblock, letterpress, monoprint and more, supported by professional presses and equipment. Arts University Plymouth was ranked #1 in the UK for Facilities (Whatuni Student Choice Awards 2026). Trips, exhibitions and the contemporary art world You’ll learn first-hand from artworks through visits to exhibitions in the South West, London and cities such as Berlin and Barcelona, helping you consider your place in the wider landscape of contemporary art. Our links with cultural and community organisations in and around Plymouth offer opportunities throughout the course to explore the roles of an artist and to exhibit your own work. 'Distant' – Student work by Madison Allen, BA (Hons) Painting, Drawing & Printmaking graduate and 2025 Brownston Fresh Talent Award winner National Student Survey 2026 In the National Student Survey (NSS) 2026, BA (Hons) Painting, Drawing & Printmaking students responded most positively to teaching, timely feedback, library resources and freedom of expression. In the NSS 2026, 85.7% of responding students answered positively to the questions “How good are teaching staff at explaining things?” , “How often have you received assessment feedback on time?” and “During your studies, how free did you feel to express your ideas, opinions, and beliefs?” Students also responded positively at 81% to “To what extent have you had the chance to explore ideas and concepts in depth?” , “How often does feedback help you to improve your work?” , “How easy was it to contact teaching staff when you needed to?” and “How well have the library resources (e.g., books, online services and learning spaces) supported your learning?” Arts University Plymouth was a fantastic place to study, with incredible tutors and facilities. The course was exactly what I needed at the time and gave me a great foundation to build on. Artist Amelia Webster, BA (Hons) Painting, Drawing & Printmaking graduate and British Art Prize finalist Careers and future opportunities Career opportunities include: Exhibiting Artists, Teachers, Lecturers, Art Therapists, Illustrators, Curators, Producers, Gallery Managers, Arts Administrators, Community Arts Organisers and Creative Entrepreneurs. Many of our award-winning students continue to postgraduate study at Arts University Plymouth and other institutions nationally, such as The Royal Drawing School and The Royal College of Art. You’ll also be supported by a dedicated Careers and Enterprise service, accredited by AGCAS (Association of Graduate Careers Advisory Services). Postgraduate progression with the Royal College of Art Graduates of this course can access application guidance, portfolio preparation and progression planning for relevant taught postgraduate programmes at the Royal College of Art through our progression agreement. Your undergraduate degree is taught and awarded by Arts University Plymouth. Applications to the RCA follow its normal admissions process, and applicants must meet the entry requirements for their chosen programme. Explore the RCA progression route and scholarships for 2027/28 entry . Integrated Foundation Year This degree is also available as a four-year Integrated Foundation option. Our Integrated Foundation provides you with a preparatory year that will support your creative development, through a broad understanding of art, design and media skills relevant to your chosen degree subject. Learning through experimentation, exploration and discovery will support you in progressing to the next level of your degree at Arts University Plymouth. Support while you study All students at Arts University Plymouth can access specialist advice and guidance, including support for wellbeing, learning support and disability, and information on student finance. Click here to read more about the support we offer. Get in touch Email: admissions@aup.ac.uk Tel: +44 (0)1752 203434 Instagram: @aup_pdp What are my options after completing this degree? After graduating from BA (Hons) Film & Screen Arts, you could continue your studies at Arts University Plymouth on one of the postgraduate courses listed below. Our graduates are entitled to a 15% discount on tuition fees for our MA programmes. Through our partnership with the Royal College of Art , graduates of this course can also access application guidance and portfolio preparation for relevant RCA postgraduate programmes. MA Fine Art Deepen your studio practice, within critical and contemporary contexts, develop your ideas and work in a practice-led, interdisciplinary environment. MA Design (Communication) Explore how current social, critical and technological paradigms are changing how designers create and distribute narrative-driven artefacts and campaigns. MA Design Develop products, practices and applications for contemporary society and imagine design beyond the status quo of production and consumption. MA Museum Studies This postgraduate course offers a unique opportunity to reimagine the role of the museum within contemporary socio-political debates Frequently asked questions What makes BA (Hons) Painting, Drawing & Printmaking at Arts University Plymouth unique? Arts University Plymouth offers the only undergraduate degree in the UK that brings painting, drawing and printmaking together in a holistic way, taught through imaginative questioning and skilled invention across the three interconnected disciplines. What will I study on this course? You’ll study painting, drawing and printmaking as three interconnected disciplines, developing your practice through experimentation with materials, processes, approaches and ideas. How will the course help me develop my own artistic voice? The curriculum is designed to nurture your curiosity, proficiency and confidence within a specialist studio environment, giving you the support and practical skills to discover your own artistic voice. How will I be taught? You’ll be guided by experienced lecturers and tutors and learn through hands-on experimentation, plus seminars, lectures and group discussions to explore diverse histories and current debates. Regular tutorials support you to synthesise your experiences across painting, drawing and printmaking to craft an ambitious practice shaped by your research and what you care about. What practical techniques will I learn? Workshops introduce traditional techniques including intaglio printing and making your own paints from raw pigments, explored alongside technologies and know-how from across the university’s world-class facilities. What kind of studio environment will I study in? You’ll study amongst your peers in light and airy studios, with dedicated facilities to support the development of an ambitious practice. Will I have opportunities to exhibit my work? Yes. Links with cultural and community organisations in and around Plymouth offer opportunities throughout the course to explore the roles of an artist and to exhibit your work. Who will I learn from? You’ll learn from professional artists and experienced lecturers and tutors who understand the challenges and rewards of creative practice and can guide you in developing your own visual language. What skills will I graduate with? You’ll develop depth of knowledge and a range of specialist and transferable skills intended to support a fulfilling and enduring creative career. What career paths can this degree lead to? Career opportunities include: Exhibiting Artists, Teachers, Lecturers, Art Therapists, Illustrators, Curators, Producers, Gallery Managers, Arts Administrators, Community Arts Organisers and Creative Entrepreneurs. Can this course support progression to postgraduate study? Yes. Many award-winning students continue to postgraduate study at Arts University Plymouth and other institutions nationally, such as The Royal Drawing School and The Royal College of Art. Integrated Foundation Year This degree is also available as a four-year Integrated Foundation option, with a preparatory first year that will support your creative development. contentBlocks.text: BA (Hons) Painting, Drawing & Printmaking at Arts University Plymouth offers the only undergraduate degree in the UK that brings these three disciplines together in an holistic way, building on their rich history of nourishing and challenging each other.

contentBlocks.bodyText: On this course, you'll explore painting, drawing and printmaking as three interconnected ways of thinking and making. You'll be given the space, support and practical skills to discover your artistic voice through imaginative questioning, material experimentation and skilled invention.

contentBlocks.caption: Find out more about BA (Hons) Painting, Drawing & Printmaking at Arts University Plymouth.

contentBlocks.heading: At a glance
contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Degree: BA (Hons) Painting, Drawing & Printmaking

  • UCAS codes: 3-year degree WWDF / 4-year Integrated Foundation W102

  • Typical UCAS points: 104–120

  • Studio focus: painting, drawing and printmaking taught as interconnected disciplines

contentBlocks.heading: Why choose this painting, drawing and printmaking degree at Arts University Plymouth?

contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Immerse yourself in material experimentation, critical imagining and skilled invention across painting, drawing and printmaking.

  • Learn from professional artists who understand the challenges and rewards of creative practice and can guide you in developing your own visual language.

  • Study in light and airy studios, with dedicated facilities for crafting an ambitious practice.

  • Build specialist and transferable skills to open up a fulfilling and enduring creative career.

contentBlocks.blockquote: “Reflecting back on my degree, it’s certainly been a life changing experience for me as a fine artist and as part of the wider university community. I embarked upon my degree with low self-confidence and self-esteem, and I would never have imagined being confident enough to achieve a degree. The staff at Arts University Plymouth have coached me and taught me how to be a fine artist in today’s world.”
contentBlocks.attribution: Ruth Brown

contentBlocks.caption: Student work by Matilda Smyth, BA (Hons) Painting, Drawing & Printmaking graduate 2025

contentBlocks.heading: What you’ll learn and how you’ll study

contentBlocks.bodyText:
You’ll learn through hands-on experimentation, testing materials, processes, approaches and ideas, and reflecting on what you’re doing and why. Regular tutorials, seminars, lectures and group discussions help you develop confidence, identify relevant contexts for your work, and engage with diverse histories and current debates.

Workshops introduce traditional techniques, including intaglio printing and making your own paints from raw pigments, which you’ll explore alongside technologies and know-how from across Arts University Plymouth’s world-class facilities.

image.title: Student using facilities in the print making studio

contentBlocks.caption: A student using the facilities in our fine print studio.

contentBlocks.bodyText:
You’ll work in a specialist studio environment designed to support focus, curiosity and ambition. As well as course teaching, you can book additional access to specialist facilities for self-directed development through SmartHub, with a guaranteed 11 hours each week during the teaching year.

In printmaking, you can develop a broad technical range, with access to processes such as screen-printing, etching, drypoint, aquatint, lino, woodblock, letterpress, monoprint and more, supported by professional presses and equipment.

Arts University Plymouth was ranked #1 in the UK for Facilities (Whatuni Student Choice Awards 2026).

image.title: Arts University Plymouth Painting Drawing and Printmaking

contentBlocks.heading: Trips, exhibitions and the contemporary art world

contentBlocks.bodyText:
You’ll learn first-hand from artworks through visits to exhibitions in the South West, London and cities such as Berlin and Barcelona, helping you consider your place in the wider landscape of contemporary art.

Our links with cultural and community organisations in and around Plymouth offer opportunities throughout the course to explore the roles of an artist and to exhibit your own work.

contentBlocks.caption: 'Distant' – Student work by Madison Allen, BA (Hons) Painting, Drawing & Printmaking graduate and 2025 Brownston Fresh Talent Award winner

contentBlocks.heading: National Student Survey 2026
contentBlocks.bodyText:
In the National Student Survey (NSS) 2026, BA (Hons) Painting, Drawing & Printmaking students responded most positively to teaching, timely feedback, library resources and freedom of expression.

In the NSS 2026, 85.7% of responding students answered positively to the questions “How good are teaching staff at explaining things?”, “How often have you received assessment feedback on time?” and “During your studies, how free did you feel to express your ideas, opinions, and beliefs?”

Students also responded positively at 81% to “To what extent have you had the chance to explore ideas and concepts in depth?”, “How often does feedback help you to improve your work?”, “How easy was it to contact teaching staff when you needed to?” and “How well have the library resources (e.g., books, online services and learning spaces) supported your learning?”

contentBlocks.blockquote: Arts University Plymouth was a fantastic place to study, with incredible tutors and facilities. The course was exactly what I needed at the time and gave me a great foundation to build on.
contentBlocks.attribution: Artist Amelia Webster, BA (Hons) Painting, Drawing & Printmaking graduate and British Art Prize finalist

contentBlocks.bodyText:
Career opportunities include: Exhibiting Artists, Teachers, Lecturers, Art Therapists, Illustrators, Curators, Producers, Gallery Managers, Arts Administrators, Community Arts Organisers and Creative Entrepreneurs.

Many of our award-winning students continue to postgraduate study at Arts University Plymouth and other institutions nationally, such as The Royal Drawing School and The Royal College of Art.

You’ll also be supported by a dedicated Careers and Enterprise service, accredited by AGCAS (Association of Graduate Careers Advisory Services).

contentBlocks.heading: Postgraduate progression with the Royal College of Art
contentBlocks.bodyText:
Graduates of this course can access application guidance, portfolio preparation and progression planning for relevant taught postgraduate programmes at the Royal College of Art through our progression agreement.

Your undergraduate degree is taught and awarded by Arts University Plymouth. Applications to the RCA follow its normal admissions process, and applicants must meet the entry requirements for their chosen programme.

Explore the RCA progression route and scholarships for 2027/28 entry.

contentBlocks.heading: Integrated Foundation Year
contentBlocks.bodyText: This degree is also available as a four-year Integrated Foundation option. Our Integrated Foundation provides you with a preparatory year that will support your creative development, through a broad understanding of art, design and media skills relevant to your chosen degree subject. Learning through experimentation, exploration and discovery will support you in progressing to the next level of your degree at Arts University Plymouth.

contentBlocks.heading: Support while you study
contentBlocks.bodyText:
All students at Arts University Plymouth can access specialist advice and guidance, including support for wellbeing, learning support and disability, and information on student finance.

Click here to read more about the support we offer.

contentBlocks.heading: Get in touch
contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Email: admissions@aup.ac.uk
  • Tel: +44 (0)1752 203434
  • Instagram: @aup_pdp

contentBlocks.heading: What are my options after completing this degree?

contentBlocks.bodyText:
After graduating from BA (Hons) Film & Screen Arts, you could continue your studies at Arts University Plymouth on one of the postgraduate courses listed below. Our graduates are entitled to a 15% discount on tuition fees for our MA programmes.

Through our partnership with the Royal College of Art, graduates of this course can also access application guidance and portfolio preparation for relevant RCA postgraduate programmes.

items.heading: What makes BA (Hons) Painting, Drawing & Printmaking at Arts University Plymouth unique?

items.heading: What will I study on this course?
items.bodyText: You’ll study painting, drawing and printmaking as three interconnected disciplines, developing your practice through experimentation with materials, processes, approaches and ideas.

items.heading: How will the course help me develop my own artistic voice?
items.bodyText: The curriculum is designed to nurture your curiosity, proficiency and confidence within a specialist studio environment, giving you the support and practical skills to discover your own artistic voice.

items.heading: How will I be taught?
items.bodyText: You’ll be guided by experienced lecturers and tutors and learn through hands-on experimentation, plus seminars, lectures and group discussions to explore diverse histories and current debates. Regular tutorials support you to synthesise your experiences across painting, drawing and printmaking to craft an ambitious practice shaped by your research and what you care about.

items.heading: What practical techniques will I learn?
items.bodyText: Workshops introduce traditional techniques including intaglio printing and making your own paints from raw pigments, explored alongside technologies and know-how from across the university’s world-class facilities.

items.heading: What kind of studio environment will I study in?
items.bodyText: You’ll study amongst your peers in light and airy studios, with dedicated facilities to support the development of an ambitious practice.

items.heading: Will I have opportunities to exhibit my work?
items.bodyText: Yes. Links with cultural and community organisations in and around Plymouth offer opportunities throughout the course to explore the roles of an artist and to exhibit your work.

items.heading: Who will I learn from?
items.bodyText: You’ll learn from professional artists and experienced lecturers and tutors who understand the challenges and rewards of creative practice and can guide you in developing your own visual language.

items.heading: What skills will I graduate with?
items.bodyText: You’ll develop depth of knowledge and a range of specialist and transferable skills intended to support a fulfilling and enduring creative career.

items.heading: What career paths can this degree lead to?
items.bodyText: Career opportunities include: Exhibiting Artists, Teachers, Lecturers, Art Therapists, Illustrators, Curators, Producers, Gallery Managers, Arts Administrators, Community Arts Organisers and Creative Entrepreneurs.

Whether you want to grow your own personal brand, freelance for agencies, or work for employers on big campaigns, BA (Hons) Content Creation will prepare you to join the next generation of creatives. In an era of rapid technological and cultural change, meaningful communication through digital content is vital across all industries. This fast-paced, industry-focused course equips you with the creative, technical and analytical skills to engage audiences and shape narratives through visual and interactive media. Find out more about BA (Hons) Content Creation at Arts University Plymouth. At a glance Degree: BA (Hons) Content Creation UCAS codes: 3-year degree CW20 / 4-year Integrated Foundation 7PW5 Typical UCAS points: 104–120 Validation status: *Subject to validation What you’ll learn Using the latest technology and software, you will learn to create content in multiple forms including moving image, photography, audio, animation and written communication. You’ll explore marketing, branding and business development principles while examining audience engagement, data-driven content planning and platform-specific production. Photo by Luke Frost Future-facing digital tools and experimentation Through experimentation, you will investigate how digital tools such as AI, immersive media and interactive design can expand creative practice and redefine the relationship between maker and audience. Industry briefs, live projects and professional experience Project-based learning is central to the course. You’ll work on industry briefs and collaborative projects, often in real-world environments and at live events, gaining insight into commercial production workflows and client engagement. You’ll work with The Influencer Academy across all three years of your degree, beginning in your first year with six weeks of focused training in pricing your work, pitching ideas and managing professional collaborations. As the course progresses, you’ll respond to live briefs and pitch content ideas to national brands, with selected work potentially leading to paid commissions. Final-year support will include portfolio reviews and talent development, and standout students may also be considered for agency representation through The Influencer Academy. Access to our extensive industry links offers opportunities for placements, internships and the development of professional networks. The university Equipment Resource Centre, where you can borrow kit like cameras and filming equipment, is [...] seriously underrated. There’s no charge for borrowing industry-standard equipment, so it got to the point where I was borrowing new cameras or lenses every week, honing my skills so that I could handle a really wide range of technology. Tom Bispham, Content Creator and Arts University Plymouth alumni Critical, contextual and ethical practice Your practical work will be underpinned by critical and contextual studies, allowing you to explore the political, social and ethical dimensions of content creation. You’ll examine how media shapes perception and behaviour, and how inclusive storytelling can foster positive change. Why choose this course? Multidisciplinary creativity: learn a broad range of digital production skills across a range of media, including photography, video, sound production, graphic design, publishing, web design and generative AI. Professional portfolio development: graduate with a refined creative identity and a portfolio ready for employment or postgraduate study. Creative process: develop a deep understanding of the creative process, learning how to write, create and publish compelling digital content that engages your audience. Strategic and analytical insight: learn how to plan and create data-informed content, shaped by marketing and branding principles. Marketing and business skills: build knowledge and skills in marketing and business, including understanding consumer behaviour, data analysis and audience metrics, strategic thinking, business planning, and financial management. Industry-focused practice-led learning: explore digital storytelling through hands-on projects that mirror real industry workflows, and gain professional experience through live briefs, placements and collaborations with external partners. Critical and ethical awareness: explore the social, political and cultural impact of digital media and responsible storytelling. Future-facing, vibrant creative community: study within a specialist arts university recognised nationally for teaching excellence and creative innovation, and be part of a university that champions experimentation, collaboration and inclusive creative practice in a changing digital landscape. Students shooting branded content for Yes Colours. Photo by Luke Frost. Arts University Plymouth Logo Skip to Content Our Courses Open Days Apply Now Menu Apply Now Our Courses Open Days Chevron Down About Us Chevron Down Study Chevron Down International Chevron Down Student Life Alumni Chevron Down Visit Resources Chevron Down Research & Innovation Prospectus Latest News What's On Established 1856 Student Login Staff Login Contact Us Explore our Undergraduate courses BA (Hons) Content Creation Course Duration Full-time: 3 years / Part-time: 6 years Integrated Foundation: Full-time 4 years / Part-time: 7 years Course Contact admissions@aup.ac.uk Admissions Contact admissions@aup.ac.uk +44 (0)1752 203434 UCAS Code Course: CW20 Institution: P65 Apply Now Register Your Interest Overview Course & Units Entry Requirements Staff Careers & Alumni Ask a Student Resources Fees & Funding Overview Create compelling content, connect with your audience, and launch your creative career If you love creating digital content (filming, editing, posting and sharing stories), this degree will help you turn that passion into a profession. Whether you want to grow your own personal brand, freelance for agencies, or work for employers on big campaigns, BA (Hons) Content Creation will prepare you to join the next generation of creatives. In an era of rapid technological and cultural change, meaningful communication through digital content is vital across all industries. This fast-paced, industry-focused course equips you with the creative, technical and analytical skills to engage audiences and shape narratives through visual and interactive media. Find out more about BA (Hons) Content Creation at Arts University Plymouth. At a glance

  • Degree: BA (Hons) Content Creation

  • UCAS codes: 3-year degree CW20 / 4-year Integrated Foundation 7PW5

  • Typical UCAS points: 104–120

  • Validation status: *Subject to validation

What you’ll learn

Using the latest technology and software, you will learn to create content in multiple forms including moving image, photography, audio, animation and written communication.

You’ll explore marketing, branding and business development principles while examining audience engagement, data-driven content planning and platform-specific production.

Photo by Luke Frost Future-facing digital tools and experimentation

Through experimentation, you will investigate how digital tools such as AI, immersive media and interactive design can expand creative practice and redefine the relationship between maker and audience.

Industry briefs, live projects and professional experience

Project-based learning is central to the course. You’ll work on industry briefs and collaborative projects, often in real-world environments and at live events, gaining insight into commercial production workflows and client engagement.

You’ll work with The Influencer Academy across all three years of your degree, beginning in your first year with six weeks of focused training in pricing your work, pitching ideas and managing professional collaborations. As the course progresses, you’ll respond to live briefs and pitch content ideas to national brands, with selected work potentially leading to paid commissions. Final-year support will include portfolio reviews and talent development, and standout students may also be considered for agency representation through The Influencer Academy.

Access to our extensive industry links offers opportunities for placements, internships and the development of professional networks.

The university Equipment Resource Centre, where you can borrow kit like cameras and filming equipment, is [...] seriously underrated. There’s no charge for borrowing industry-standard equipment, so it got to the point where I was borrowing new cameras or lenses every week, honing my skills so that I could handle a really wide range of technology. Tom Bispham, Content Creator and Arts University Plymouth alumni Critical, contextual and ethical practice

Your practical work will be underpinned by critical and contextual studies, allowing you to explore the political, social and ethical dimensions of content creation.

You’ll examine how media shapes perception and behaviour, and how inclusive storytelling can foster positive change.

Why choose this course?

  • Multidisciplinary creativity: learn a broad range of digital production skills across a range of media, including photography, video, sound production, graphic design, publishing, web design and generative AI.

  • Professional portfolio development: graduate with a refined creative identity and a portfolio ready for employment or postgraduate study.

  • Creative process: develop a deep understanding of the creative process, learning how to write, create and publish compelling digital content that engages your audience.

  • Strategic and analytical insight: learn how to plan and create data-informed content, shaped by marketing and branding principles.

  • Marketing and business skills: build knowledge and skills in marketing and business, including understanding consumer behaviour, data analysis and audience metrics, strategic thinking, business planning, and financial management.

  • Industry-focused practice-led learning: explore digital storytelling through hands-on projects that mirror real industry workflows, and gain professional experience through live briefs, placements and collaborations with external partners.

  • Critical and ethical awareness: explore the social, political and cultural impact of digital media and responsible storytelling.

  • Future-facing, vibrant creative community: study within a specialist arts university recognised nationally for teaching excellence and creative innovation, and be part of a university that champions experimentation, collaboration and inclusive creative practice in a changing digital landscape.

Students shooting branded content for Yes Colours. Photo by Luke Frost. Your portfolio, careers and next steps

By the end of your degree, you’ll have built a professional portfolio showcasing your creative identity and readiness for employment or postgraduate study.

Career opportunities include: Digital Content Creators, Social Media Executives, Video/Audio Producers, Influencers or Brand Ambassadors, YouTubers, Podcasters, PR Executives, Content Writers or Editors, Branding Strategists, Creative Directors and Freelance Content Consultants.

Frequently asked questions What kinds of content will I learn to create?

You will learn to create content in multiple forms including moving image, photography, audio, animation and written communication.

Will I learn about marketing, branding and business development?

Yes. You’ll explore marketing, branding and business development principles while examining audience engagement, data-driven content planning and platform-specific production.

Will I use emerging digital tools such as AI?

Yes. Through experimentation, you will investigate how digital tools such as AI, immersive media and interactive design can expand creative practice and redefine the relationship between maker and audience.

How will I be taught on the course?

Project-based learning is central to the course, and you’ll work on industry briefs and collaborative projects that mirror real industry workflows.

Will I work on live briefs and in real-world environments?

Yes. You’ll work on industry briefs and collaborative projects, often in real-world environments and at live events, gaining insight into commercial production workflows and client engagement.

Are there opportunities for placements or internships?

Yes. Access to our extensive industry links offers opportunities for placements, internships and the development of professional networks.

How does the course cover ethics and responsible storytelling?

Your practical work will be underpinned by critical and contextual studies exploring the political, social and ethical dimensions of content creation, including how inclusive storytelling can foster positive change.

What will I graduate with?

By the end of your degree, you’ll have built a professional portfolio showcasing your creative identity and readiness for employment or postgraduate study.

What careers could this degree lead to?

Career opportunities include Digital Content Creators, Social Media Executives, Video/Audio Producers, Influencers or Brand Ambassadors, YouTubers, Podcasters, PR Executives, Content Writers or Editors, Branding Strategists, Creative Directors and Freelance Content Consultants.

Studying at Arts University Plymouth gave me the opportunity to grow both creatively and personally in a way I wouldn’t have done anywhere else. Maia Cazzani, BA (Hons) Commercial Photography graduate Integrated Foundation Year

This degree is also available as a four-year Integrated Foundation option. Our Integrated Foundation provides you with a preparatory year that will support your creative development, through a broad understanding of art, design and media skills relevant to your chosen degree subject. Learning through experimentation, exploration and discovery will support you in progressing to the next level of your degree at Arts University Plymouth.

Support while you study

All students at Arts University Plymouth can access specialist support via our Student Support Team. Our trained advisers offer information and guidance on student finance and funding, disability support, counselling and more.

Click here to read more about the support we offer.

Get in touch
  • Email: admissions@aup.ac.uk
What are my options after completing this degree?

After successful completion of BA (Hons) Content Creation, your progression options at Arts University Plymouth could include some of the postgraduate courses listed below. As a graduate of the university, you will be entitled to a discount of 15% on postgraduate study fees if you choose to progress onto one of our MA programmes.

MA Design (Communication) Explore how current social, critical and technological paradigms are changing how designers create and distribute narrative-driven artefacts and campaigns. MA Immersive Media Translate your creative knowledge and digital skills into engaging immersive content and public media experiences for diverse audiences in this exciting and rapidly growing sector. MA Design Develop products, practices and applications for contemporary society and imagine design beyond the status quo of production and consumption. Integrated Foundation Year This degree is also available as a four-year Integrated Foundation option, with a preparatory first year that will support your creative development. contentBlocks.bodyText:
By the end of your degree, you’ll have built a professional portfolio showcasing your creative identity and readiness for employment or postgraduate study.

Career opportunities include: Digital Content Creators, Social Media Executives, Video/Audio Producers, Influencers or Brand Ambassadors, YouTubers, Podcasters, PR Executives, Content Writers or Editors, Branding Strategists, Creative Directors and Freelance Content Consultants.

items.heading: What kinds of content will I learn to create?
items.bodyText: You will learn to create content in multiple forms including moving image, photography, audio, animation and written communication.

items.heading: Will I learn about marketing, branding and business development?
items.bodyText: Yes. You’ll explore marketing, branding and business development principles while examining audience engagement, data-driven content planning and platform-specific production.

items.heading: Will I use emerging digital tools such as AI?
items.bodyText: Yes. Through experimentation, you will investigate how digital tools such as AI, immersive media and interactive design can expand creative practice and redefine the relationship between maker and audience.

items.heading: How will I be taught on the course?
items.bodyText: Project-based learning is central to the course, and you’ll work on industry briefs and collaborative projects that mirror real industry workflows.

items.heading: Will I work on live briefs and in real-world environments?
items.bodyText: Yes. You’ll work on industry briefs and collaborative projects, often in real-world environments and at live events, gaining insight into commercial production workflows and client engagement.

items.heading: Are there opportunities for placements or internships?
items.bodyText: Yes. Access to our extensive industry links offers opportunities for placements, internships and the development of professional networks.

items.heading: How does the course cover ethics and responsible storytelling?
items.bodyText: Your practical work will be underpinned by critical and contextual studies exploring the political, social and ethical dimensions of content creation, including how inclusive storytelling can foster positive change.

items.heading: What will I graduate with?
items.bodyText: By the end of your degree, you’ll have built a professional portfolio showcasing your creative identity and readiness for employment or postgraduate study.

items.heading: What careers could this degree lead to?
items.bodyText: Career opportunities include Digital Content Creators, Social Media Executives, Video/Audio Producers, Influencers or Brand Ambassadors, YouTubers, Podcasters, PR Executives, Content Writers or Editors, Branding Strategists, Creative Directors and Freelance Content Consultants.

contentBlocks.blockquote: Studying at Arts University Plymouth gave me the opportunity to grow both creatively and personally in a way I wouldn’t have done anywhere else.
contentBlocks.attribution: Maia Cazzani, BA (Hons) Commercial Photography graduate

contentBlocks.heading: Integrated Foundation Year
contentBlocks.bodyText: This degree is also available as a four-year Integrated Foundation option. Our Integrated Foundation provides you with a preparatory year that will support your creative development, through a broad understanding of art, design and media skills relevant to your chosen degree subject. Learning through experimentation, exploration and discovery will support you in progressing to the next level of your degree at Arts University Plymouth.

contentBlocks.heading: Support while you study
contentBlocks.bodyText:
All students at Arts University Plymouth can access specialist support via our Student Support Team. Our trained advisers offer information and guidance on student finance and funding, disability support, counselling and more.

Click here to read more about the support we offer.

contentBlocks.heading: Get in touch
contentBlocks.bodyText: • Email: admissions@aup.ac.uk

contentBlocks.heading: What are my options after completing this degree?

contentBlocks.bodyText: After successful completion of BA (Hons) Content Creation, your progression options at Arts University Plymouth could include some of the postgraduate courses listed below. As a graduate of the university, you will be entitled to a discount of 15% on postgraduate study fees if you choose to progress onto one of our MA programmes.

pages.text: Arts University Plymouth Logo Skip to Content Our Courses Open Days Apply Now Menu Apply Now Our Courses Open Days Chevron Down About Us Chevron Down Study Chevron Down International Chevron Down Student Life Alumni Chevron Down Visit Resources Chevron Down Research & Innovation Prospectus Latest News What's On Established 1856 Student Login Staff Login Contact Us Explore our Undergraduate courses BA (Hons) Craft & Material Practices Course Duration Full-time: 3 years / Part-time: 6 years Integrated Foundation: Full-time: 4 years / Part-time: 7 years Course Contact hello@aup.ac.uk Admissions Contact admissions@aup.ac.uk +44 (0)1752 203434 UCAS Code Course: 67T2 Institution: P65 Apply Now Register your interest Overview Course & Units Entry Requirements Staff Student Work Careers & Alumni Ask a Student Resources Fees & Funding Overview Prepare for success in the contemporary craft industry With almost 150,000 people employed in the UK’s craft industry, skilled craftspeople are putting the country on the map for original, forward-thinking contemporary design. The relationship between thinking and making is constantly evolving, with experimentation and innovation driving a new wave of craftspeople to explore original directions. On BA (Hons) Craft & Material Practices at Arts University Plymouth, you’ll often explore methods in which we can live harmoniously within natural and fabricated environments while supporting a healthy ecosystem, developing your practice through materials, processes and making. Find out more about BA (Hons) Craft & Material Practices at Arts University Plymouth. At a glance Degree: BA (Hons) Craft & Material Practices UCAS codes: 3-year degree 67T2 / 4-year Integrated Foundation 69K5 Typical UCAS points: 104–120 Facilities, studios and resources Our spacious Materials Lab includes specialist facilities for ceramics, glass, metal and wood, encouraging you to explore traditional making. It is complemented by the rapid digital prototyping facilities within Fab Lab South West, giving you the opportunity to reinvent craft for the 21st century. However, learning isn’t limited to our studios and workshops. You will meet some of the UK’s most inventive and entrepreneurial contemporary makers and thinkers through gallery visits, demonstrations and presentations. From collective installations to traditional making and digital fabrication - your experience will be filled with opportunities to diversify and try new processes. I knew I needed to see the university in person, and the facilities were just unbeatable. That was when I realised how much the course had to offer. I was unsure which creative route to follow, so I took the opportunities offered to learn as much as possible across a number of disciplines, and I found my specialism. Caroline Barr, BA (Hons) Craft & Material Practices student What you’ll learn and how you’ll study On this course you will have the opportunity to explore a wide range of techniques and processes across materials and making: Ceramics: throwing, slip casting, slab building, coiling, glazing and raku firing Glass: hot glassmaking, kiln-formed glass, coldworking and lampworking Metals: casting, welding and grinding Woodworking: woodturning, joinery and CNC routing (if you choose to specialise) Fab Lab South West: laser cutting, CNC milling and 3D printing Jason Mcanuff working in the glass-blowing house within our £8m funded Craft, Design and Fabrication workshops. Enterprise, entrepreneurship and live experience As a student, you will learn about enterprise and entrepreneurship, and how to price, display and promote work for a range of different markets. This includes large-scale site-specific work, individual exhibition pieces and domestic products, all based on knowledge of your customers and the experience gained by working on live briefs, pitching to clients and entering competitions. Student work by Ben Kew Why choose this course? Explore an expansive range of material practices, including glassblowing and kiln-formed glass, ceramics, large and small scale metals, woodworking, concrete, plastics and textiles, in our industry-standard workshops. Engage with live briefs and real clients: students have worked with Tate Exchange, The Box, MAKE Southwest, Mount Edgcumbe Estate, Eden Project and New Designers among others. Become part of the international maker community by participating in our renowned, biennial Making Futures™ conference, a research platform exploring contemporary craft and maker movements as ‘change agents’ in 21st-century society. Careers and future opportunities Career opportunities include: Designer/Makers, Ceramicists, Glass Artists, Wearables Designers, Sculptors, Architectural Surface Designers, Mixed Media Artists, Fine Artists, Gallery and Museum Professionals, Teachers, Technicians, Material Restoration Technicians and Conservators, and Prop Designers. Frequently asked questions What is BA (Hons) Craft & Material Practices about? It’s about contemporary craft and the evolving relationship between thinking and making, shaped by experimentation and innovation in materials, processes and making. What kinds of projects could I be ready for? You’ll be supported to enter industry as a well-rounded interiors specialist, ready to work on projects from super yachts to magazine photoshoots. What environments will I design for? You’ll design for environments from residential and commercial spaces to the public realm and even transport. What themes are emphasised in your studies? Your studies place special emphasis on trends, colour, materiality, sustainability and accessibility in interior contexts, both public and private. Will I develop styling and curation skills? Yes. You’ll develop your own distinct taste in style curation, exploring lighting, furnishing, surface and textural finishes to make your design concepts a reality. Does the course cover consumer trends and market levels? Yes. You’ll develop a keen understanding of consumer trends and learn how to design for different levels of the market. What specialist modules and technical skills are covered? Specialist modules cover interior project management, materials and regulations in design, event planning and live design briefs, and you’ll develop skills including technical drawing, visualisation, editorial photography and industry-standard CAD software. Who will I learn from on the course? You’ll be taught by industry-active academics and specialist technicians whose combined client list includes the National Trust, the BBC, Royal Caribbean Cruises and Sheraton, and who have delivered multi-million-pound commissions in New York and Barbados. Postgraduate progression with the Royal College of Art Graduates of this course can access application guidance, portfolio preparation and progression planning for relevant taught postgraduate programmes at the Royal College of Art through our progression agreement. Your undergraduate degree is taught and awarded by Arts University Plymouth. Applications to the RCA follow its normal admissions process, and applicants must meet the entry requirements for their chosen programme. Explore the RCA progression route and scholarships for 2027/28 entry . Integrated Foundation Year This degree is also available as a four-year Integrated Foundation option. Our Integrated Foundation provides you with a preparatory year that will support your creative development, through a broad understanding of art, design and media skills relevant to your chosen degree subject. Learning through experimentation, exploration and discovery will support you in progressing to the next level of your degree at Arts University Plymouth. Support while you study All students at Arts University Plymouth can access specialist support via our Student Support Team. Our trained advisers offer information and guidance on student finance and funding, disability support, counselling and more. Click here to read more about the support we offer. Get in touch Email: admissions@aup.ac.uk Instagram: @aup_craft What are my options after completing this degree? After graduating from BA (Hons) Film & Screen Arts, you could continue your studies at Arts University Plymouth on one of the postgraduate courses listed below. Our graduates are entitled to a 15% discount on tuition fees for our MA programmes. Through our partnership with the Royal College of Art , graduates of this course can also access application guidance and portfolio preparation for relevant RCA postgraduate programmes. MA Craft & Material Practices Develop a future-oriented professional practice through material-led research processes, supported by specialist studios, digital fabrication in Fab Lab South West, and an interdisciplinary postgraduate structure. MA Glass Study the unique art and refined techniques of studio glassmaking on a course dedicated to the history, material and culture of glass, learning in world-class hot glass and kiln-formed studios. MA Fine Art Deepen your studio practice, within critical and contemporary contexts, develop your ideas and work in a practice-led, interdisciplinary environment. MA Museum Studies This postgraduate course offers a unique opportunity to reimagine the role of the museum within contemporary socio-political debates Next Open Day: 14 Nov Discover our state-of-the-art facilities, talk to expert staff and tour local affordable accommodation at our next Open Day. On BA (Hons) Craft & Material Practices at Arts University Plymouth, you’ll often explore methods in which we can live harmoniously within natural and fabricated environments while supporting a healthy ecosystem, developing your practice through materials, processes and making.

Facilities, studios and resources

Our spacious Materials Lab includes specialist facilities for ceramics, glass, metal and wood, encouraging you to explore traditional making. It is complemented by the rapid digital prototyping facilities within Fab Lab South West, giving you the opportunity to reinvent craft for the 21st century.

Caroline Barr, BA (Hons) Craft & Material Practices student What you’ll learn and how you’ll study

On this course you will have the opportunity to explore a wide range of techniques and processes across materials and making:

  • Ceramics: throwing, slip casting, slab building, coiling, glazing and raku firing

This includes large-scale site-specific work, individual exhibition pieces and domestic products, all based on knowledge of your customers and the experience gained by working on live briefs, pitching to clients and entering competitions.

Frequently asked questions What is BA (Hons) Craft & Material Practices about?

It’s about contemporary craft and the evolving relationship between thinking and making, shaped by experimentation and innovation in materials, processes and making.

What kinds of projects could I be ready for?

You’ll be supported to enter industry as a well-rounded interiors specialist, ready to work on projects from super yachts to magazine photoshoots.

What environments will I design for?

You’ll design for environments from residential and commercial spaces to the public realm and even transport.

Your studies place special emphasis on trends, colour, materiality, sustainability and accessibility in interior contexts, both public and private.

contentBlocks.heading: Prepare for success in the contemporary craft industry

contentBlocks.text: With almost 150,000 people employed in the UK’s craft industry, skilled craftspeople are putting the country on the map for original, forward-thinking contemporary design. The relationship between thinking and making is constantly evolving, with experimentation and innovation driving a new wave of craftspeople to explore original directions.

contentBlocks.bodyText: On BA (Hons) Craft & Material Practices at Arts University Plymouth, you’ll often explore methods in which we can live harmoniously within natural and fabricated environments while supporting a healthy ecosystem, developing your practice through materials, processes and making.

contentBlocks.caption: Find out more about BA (Hons) Craft & Material Practices at Arts University Plymouth.

contentBlocks.heading: At a glance
contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Degree: BA (Hons) Craft & Material Practices

  • UCAS codes: 3-year degree 67T2 / 4-year Integrated Foundation 69K5

  • Typical UCAS points: 104–120

Our spacious Materials Lab includes specialist facilities for ceramics, glass, metal and wood, encouraging you to explore traditional making. It is complemented by the rapid digital prototyping facilities within Fab Lab South West, giving you the opportunity to reinvent craft for the 21st century.

However, learning isn’t limited to our studios and workshops. You will meet some of the UK’s most inventive and entrepreneurial contemporary makers and thinkers through gallery visits, demonstrations and presentations.

images.title: Web res Melting Pot Hot Glass Gathering March 2022 78
22 For Crafts Sake22 Picket Line at Tate Exchange

contentBlocks.caption: From collective installations to traditional making and digital fabrication - your experience will be filled with opportunities to diversify and try new processes.

contentBlocks.blockquote: I knew I needed to see the university in person, and the facilities were just unbeatable. That was when I realised how much the course had to offer. I was unsure which creative route to follow, so I took the opportunities offered to learn as much as possible across a number of disciplines, and I found my specialism.
contentBlocks.attribution: Caroline Barr, BA (Hons) Craft & Material Practices student

contentBlocks.heading: What you’ll learn and how you’ll study

contentBlocks.bodyText:
On this course you will have the opportunity to explore a wide range of techniques and processes across materials and making:

  • Ceramics: throwing, slip casting, slab building, coiling, glazing and raku firing

  • Glass: hot glassmaking, kiln-formed glass, coldworking and lampworking

  • Metals: casting, welding and grinding

  • Woodworking: woodturning, joinery and CNC routing (if you choose to specialise)

  • Fab Lab South West: laser cutting, CNC milling and 3D printing

contentBlocks.caption: Jason Mcanuff working in the glass-blowing house within our £8m funded Craft, Design and Fabrication workshops.

contentBlocks.bodyText: As a student, you will learn about enterprise and entrepreneurship, and how to price, display and promote work for a range of different markets. This includes large-scale site-specific work, individual exhibition pieces and domestic products, all based on knowledge of your customers and the experience gained by working on live briefs, pitching to clients and entering competitions.

contentBlocks.caption: Student work by Ben Kew

contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Explore an expansive range of material practices, including glassblowing and kiln-formed glass, ceramics, large and small scale metals, woodworking, concrete, plastics and textiles, in our industry-standard workshops.

  • Engage with live briefs and real clients: students have worked with Tate Exchange, The Box, MAKE Southwest, Mount Edgcumbe Estate, Eden Project and New Designers among others.

  • Become part of the international maker community by participating in our renowned, biennial Making Futures™ conference, a research platform exploring contemporary craft and maker movements as ‘change agents’ in 21st-century society.

Career opportunities include: Designer/Makers, Ceramicists, Glass Artists, Wearables Designers, Sculptors, Architectural Surface Designers, Mixed Media Artists, Fine Artists, Gallery and Museum Professionals, Teachers, Technicians, Material Restoration Technicians and Conservators, and Prop Designers.

items.heading: What is BA (Hons) Craft & Material Practices about?
items.bodyText: It’s about contemporary craft and the evolving relationship between thinking and making, shaped by experimentation and innovation in materials, processes and making.

items.heading: What kinds of projects could I be ready for?
items.bodyText: You’ll be supported to enter industry as a well-rounded interiors specialist, ready to work on projects from super yachts to magazine photoshoots.

items.heading: What environments will I design for?
items.bodyText: You’ll design for environments from residential and commercial spaces to the public realm and even transport.

items.heading: What themes are emphasised in your studies?
items.bodyText: Your studies place special emphasis on trends, colour, materiality, sustainability and accessibility in interior contexts, both public and private.

items.heading: Will I develop styling and curation skills?
items.bodyText: Yes. You’ll develop your own distinct taste in style curation, exploring lighting, furnishing, surface and textural finishes to make your design concepts a reality.

items.heading: Does the course cover consumer trends and market levels?
items.bodyText: Yes. You’ll develop a keen understanding of consumer trends and learn how to design for different levels of the market.

items.heading: What specialist modules and technical skills are covered?
items.bodyText: Specialist modules cover interior project management, materials and regulations in design, event planning and live design briefs, and you’ll develop skills including technical drawing, visualisation, editorial photography and industry-standard CAD software.

items.heading: Who will I learn from on the course?
items.bodyText: You’ll be taught by industry-active academics and specialist technicians whose combined client list includes the National Trust, the BBC, Royal Caribbean Cruises and Sheraton, and who have delivered multi-million-pound commissions in New York and Barbados.

contentBlocks.heading: Postgraduate progression with the Royal College of Art
contentBlocks.bodyText:
Graduates of this course can access application guidance, portfolio preparation and progression planning for relevant taught postgraduate programmes at the Royal College of Art through our progression agreement.

Your undergraduate degree is taught and awarded by Arts University Plymouth. Applications to the RCA follow its normal admissions process, and applicants must meet the entry requirements for their chosen programme.

Explore the RCA progression route and scholarships for 2027/28 entry.

contentBlocks.heading: Integrated Foundation Year
contentBlocks.bodyText: This degree is also available as a four-year Integrated Foundation option. Our Integrated Foundation provides you with a preparatory year that will support your creative development, through a broad understanding of art, design and media skills relevant to your chosen degree subject. Learning through experimentation, exploration and discovery will support you in progressing to the next level of your degree at Arts University Plymouth.

contentBlocks.heading: Support while you study
contentBlocks.bodyText:
All students at Arts University Plymouth can access specialist support via our Student Support Team. Our trained advisers offer information and guidance on student finance and funding, disability support, counselling and more.

Click here to read more about the support we offer.

Instagram: @aup_craft

contentBlocks.heading: What are my options after completing this degree?

contentBlocks.bodyText:
After graduating from BA (Hons) Film & Screen Arts, you could continue your studies at Arts University Plymouth on one of the postgraduate courses listed below. Our graduates are entitled to a 15% discount on tuition fees for our MA programmes.

Through our partnership with the Royal College of Art, graduates of this course can also access application guidance and portfolio preparation for relevant RCA postgraduate programmes.

You’ll combine authentic image-making with real-world commercial practices to build a robust, fulfilling and lifelong illustration career. On this course, you’ll cultivate a variety of conceptual and image-making methods by dissecting and tackling the essential ‘ingredients’ of illustration and how you might apply them to your own creative practice. You’ll be challenged to cultivate a culturally curious attitude while being mindful of the ethical responsibilities that accompany the field of illustration. What stood out for me at Arts University Plymouth is the fact that it’s a dedicated art university. In other universities that I looked at, the arts were really pushed to the side – but here it was really inspiring to see that the whole university is dedicated to creativity and creative subjects. Another big selling point was the high contact time with tutors, which I really took advantage of. Throughout my course, there was never a point where there were long waits to speak to tutors or get feedback on work, which was so valuable. You’ll approach independent projects with a critical mindset, considering the purpose, rationale, production and application of your own original work. Helena Dore, BA (Hons) Illustration Studio culture and community You will be based in a spacious and naturally lit studio in the heart of our seaside city, where you’ll build your own unique blend of skills and attributes and grow into a well-rounded practitioner. Within this supportive studio environment, you’ll delve into your subject both individually and as part of collaborative, interdisciplinary teams. We’ll inspire you to engage with our nurturing, student-led communities across the university, showcasing your final outputs as part of enterprising collectives, pop-up shops and curated exhibitions. Industry partners and professional insight During your time on the course you’ll engage with input from industry partners from around the world, including experienced illustrators Molly Mendoza, Roman Muradov and Tommy Parker, plus art directors, agents and project leaders from Profile Books, Airbnb, The National Trust and NoBrow. Why choose this course? Creative empowerment: You will learn how to make great work, developing your ability to express powerful ideas, evoke emotions, and communicate propositions through illustration. You will create artwork that exceeds what you think you’re capable of. Professional empowerment: You will learn how to find and get work, building the refined set of skills needed to operate as a practising illustrator. You will become comfortable working with real clients, dealing with money, and maintaining professional relationships. Personal empowerment: You will learn how to enjoy your work, nurturing your independent creativity, confidence, and fulfilment. Across your time on the course, through compassionate teaching and a studio of peers, you will become more than an illustrator. You could work in freelance commercial illustration, in-house illustration, graphic design, studio management and art direction, or progress to further study and qualifications. Creative empowerment: You will learn how to make great work, developing your ability to express powerful ideas, evoke emotions, and communicate propositions through illustration. You will create artwork that exceeds what you think you’re capable of.

Professional empowerment: You will learn how to find and get work, building the refined set of skills needed to operate as a practising illustrator. You will become comfortable working with real clients, dealing with money, and maintaining professional relationships.

Personal empowerment: You will learn how to enjoy your work, nurturing your independent creativity, confidence, and fulfilment. Across your time on the course, through compassionate teaching and a studio of peers, you will become more than an illustrator.

Student work by Grace Betteridge Careers and next steps

Career opportunities include:

  • Freelance commercial illustration, focused in, or moving between, areas such as editorial (newspapers and magazines), picture books, branding, technology or advertising

  • In-house illustration in areas such as packaging, technology or retail

  • Graphic design within an agency, studio or as a freelancer

  • Studio management and art direction within an agency, studio, or larger creative organisation

Further study and qualifications, with options to move into creative education or a more specific creative niche

Frequently asked questions What is BA (Hons) Illustration about?

It’s an industry-informed degree that explores and defines what it means to be an illustrator today, combining authentic image-making with real-world commercial practices.

What areas of illustration can I focus on?

You can become an effective practitioner in the areas you feel most connected to, including editorial, advertising, narrative, books and research.

How will I develop my own creative practice?

You’ll dissect and tackle the essential ‘ingredients’ of illustration and apply them to your own creative practice, cultivating conceptual and image-making methods.

Will the course support independent ways of working?

Yes. You’ll be challenged to develop authentic ways of working, assuming agency and autonomy as an image-maker.

How will I approach projects on the course?

You’ll approach independent projects with a critical mindset, considering the purpose, rationale, production and application of your own original work.

What is the studio environment like?

You’ll be based in a spacious and naturally lit studio in the heart of our seaside city, within a supportive studio environment.

Will I work collaboratively?

Yes. You’ll delve into your subject both individually and as part of collaborative, interdisciplinary teams.

Will I have opportunities to showcase work while I study?

Yes. You’ll showcase final outputs as part of enterprising collectives, pop-up shops and curated exhibitions, engaging with nurturing, student-led communities across the university.

Will I learn from visiting illustrators and industry partners?

Yes. You’ll engage with input from industry partners from around the world, including illustrators Molly Mendoza, Roman Muradov and Tommy Parker, and art directors, agents and project leaders from Profile Books, Airbnb, The National Trust and NoBrow.

What can I do after graduating?

You could work in freelance commercial illustration, in-house illustration, graphic design, studio management and art direction, or progress to further study and qualifications.

Student work by Amy Ottley Student satisfaction

BA (Hons) Illustration students responded especially positively in the National Student Survey 2026 to questions around creative exploration, teaching and timely feedback.

In the NSS 2026, 95.7% of responding students answered positively to the question “To what extent have you had the chance to explore ideas and concepts in depth?” and 95.7% answered positively to “How often have you received assessment feedback on time?”

91.3% of responding students answered positively to the question “How good are teaching staff at explaining things?”

Postgraduate progression with the Royal College of Art

Graduates of this course can access application guidance, portfolio preparation and progression planning for relevant taught postgraduate programmes at the Royal College of Art through our progression agreement.

Your undergraduate degree is taught and awarded by Arts University Plymouth. Applications to the RCA follow its normal admissions process, and applicants must meet the entry requirements for their chosen programme.

Explore the RCA progression route and scholarships for 2027/28 entry.

Integrated Foundation Year

This degree is also available as a four-year Integrated Foundation option. Our Integrated Foundation provides you with a preparatory year that will support your creative development, through a broad understanding of art, design and media skills relevant to your chosen degree subject. Learning through experimentation, exploration and discovery will support you in progressing to the next level of your degree at Arts University Plymouth.

Support while you study

All students at Arts University Plymouth can access specialist support via our Student Support Team. Our trained advisers offer information and guidance on student finance and funding, disability support, counselling and more.

Click here to read more about the support we offer.

Get in touch

Email: illustration@aup.ac.uk

Instagram: @aup_illustration

What are my options after completing this degree?

After graduating from BA (Hons) Film & Screen Arts, you could continue your studies at Arts University Plymouth on one of the postgraduate courses listed below. Our graduates are entitled to a 15% discount on tuition fees for our MA programmes.

Through our partnership with the Royal College of Art, graduates of this course can also access application guidance and portfolio preparation for relevant RCA postgraduate programmes.

MA Design (Communication) Explore how current social, critical and technological paradigms are changing how designers create and distribute narrative-driven artefacts and campaigns. MA Design Develop products, practices and applications for contemporary society and imagine design beyond the status quo of production and consumption. MA Fine Art Deepen your studio practice, within critical and contemporary contexts, develop your ideas and work in a practice-led, interdisciplinary environment. contentBlocks.heading: Prepare for success in the illustration industry

contentBlocks.text:
This industry-informed degree explores and defines what it means to be an illustrator today. You’ll combine authentic image-making with real-world commercial practices to build a robust, fulfilling and lifelong illustration career.

On this course, you’ll cultivate a variety of conceptual and image-making methods by dissecting and tackling the essential ‘ingredients’ of illustration and how you might apply them to your own creative practice. You’ll be challenged to cultivate a culturally curious attitude while being mindful of the ethical responsibilities that accompany the field of illustration.

You’ll be challenged to cultivate a culturally curious attitude while being mindful of the ethical responsibilities that accompany the field of illustration.

contentBlocks.caption: Find out more about BA (Hons) Illustration at Arts University Plymouth.

contentBlocks.heading: At a glance
contentBlocks.bodyText:

  • Typical UCAS points: 104–120

You’ll become an effective practitioner in the areas you feel most connected to, informed by the expert experience of your tutors, who work in those fields:

  • Editorial

  • Advertising

  • Narrative

  • Books

  • Research

You will be challenged to develop authentic ways of working, assuming agency and autonomy as an image-maker and learning what this means to you as a practitioner.

contentBlocks.blockquote: What stood out for me at Arts University Plymouth is the fact that it’s a dedicated art university. In other universities that I looked at, the arts were really pushed to the side – but here it was really inspiring to see that the whole university is dedicated to creativity and creative subjects. Another big selling point was the high contact time with tutors, which I really took advantage of. Throughout my course, there was never a point where there were long waits to speak to tutors or get feedback on work, which was so valuable.

Through our partnership with the Royal College of Art, graduates of this course can also access application guidance and portfolio preparation for relevant RCA postgraduate programmes.
