We promote an interdisciplinary exploration of contemporary art, where you will gain skills to critically question and actively create. The course provides opportunities for working collaboratively, deepening cultural understanding and exploring new processes in workshops, within a learning environment that provides a meaningful link between your studio practice and contemporary art theory. Find out more about BA (Hons) Fine Art at Arts University Plymouth. At a glance Degree: BA (Hons) Fine Art UCAS codes: 3-year degree W101 / 4-year Integrated Foundation W103 Typical UCAS points: 104–120 Course overview This is a dynamic course that supports ambitious, interdisciplinary contemporary art practice, encouraging you to critically question and actively create. You’ll be supported to develop your individual practice-based study through exposure to a wide variety of material methods and modes of art practice. I wouldn’t change any of the decisions that led me here. I’m so glad that I quit my job in London and came back to the South West to study Fine Art at Arts University Plymouth. That was the best decision I’ve ever made. MOLLY ERIN MCCARTHY, BA (HONS) FINE ART GRADUATE Students exhibit work throughout the year – including at the university's annual Graduate Shows. What you’ll learn and how you’ll study You’ll participate in workshops that allow you to explore new processes while connecting studio practice with contemporary art theory. Workshops include opportunities across drawing, sound, glass, installation, video, clay, performance, painting, scale and sculpture, projection mapping, wood, printmaking and critical writing. You can also explore 3D casting in plaster, alginate and rubber, alongside traditional sculptural practices. From forming international artist collectives, winning awards, exhibiting at Art Weekenders and securing places on the prestigious Venice Biennale Fellowship - our students regularly engage with the public, and gain vital artist exposure. Your studio practice and creative community The course is led and supported by a stimulating community of creative practitioners. The core academic team are experienced artists who are active makers, writers and researchers in contemporary fine art practice. We encourage diversity in thinking and making through material exploration, collaborative working, cross-fertilisation of ideas, and the exploration of new concepts and materials. Partnerships, exhibitions and the professional art world As a student you will develop an unrivalled understanding of the professional art world through ongoing partnerships with emerging and established galleries, museums, creative organisations and practising artists. You will gain a deep understanding of the professional landscape through these partnerships, preparing you effectively for a career in the creative sector upon graduation. BA (Hons) Fine Art students enjoy access to dedicated workspaces, and award-winning facilities. Why choose this course? Our course prioritises contemporary art practice and critical enquiry. As a studio-centred, interdisciplinary programme, it allows you the freedom to work in any medium at any stage, offering the flexibility to shape your own professional journey. Partnerships with ambitious and contemporary art spaces, such as our on-site gallery, MIRROR, and our neighbours, The Box. We think beyond our walls and you will get to test, experiment and exhibit work in real-life professional art settings. Access to industry connections including: KARST, The Box, Sprite Arts Collective, Plymouth Culture, RAAM, Heart for Art, Stoke Village Hub, MIRROR gallery, WonderZoo, Yourway Project and Make Tank. Will I have opportunities to exhibit work in professional settings? Yes. Through partnerships with ambitious and contemporary art spaces such as MIRROR and The Box, you will get to test, experiment and exhibit work in real-life professional art settings. We promote an interdisciplinary exploration of contemporary art, where you will gain skills to critically question and actively create.

The course provides opportunities for working collaboratively, deepening cultural understanding and exploring new processes in workshops, within a learning environment that provides a meaningful link between your studio practice and contemporary art theory.

Find out more about BA (Hons) Fine Art at Arts University Plymouth. At a glance

  • Degree: BA (Hons) Fine Art

  • UCAS codes: 3-year degree W101 / 4-year Integrated Foundation W103

  • Typical UCAS points: 104–120

Course overview

This is a dynamic course that supports ambitious, interdisciplinary contemporary art practice, encouraging you to critically question and actively create.

You’ll be supported to develop your individual practice-based study through exposure to a wide variety of material methods and modes of art practice.

I wouldn’t change any of the decisions that led me here. I’m so glad that I quit my job in London and came back to the South West to study Fine Art at Arts University Plymouth. That was the best decision I’ve ever made. MOLLY ERIN MCCARTHY, BA (HONS) FINE ART GRADUATE Students exhibit work throughout the year – including at the university's annual Graduate Shows. What you’ll learn and how you’ll study

You’ll participate in workshops that allow you to explore new processes while connecting studio practice with contemporary art theory.

Workshops include opportunities across drawing, sound, glass, installation, video, clay, performance, painting, scale and sculpture, projection mapping, wood, printmaking and critical writing.

You can also explore 3D casting in plaster, alginate and rubber, alongside traditional sculptural practices.

From forming international artist collectives, winning awards, exhibiting at Art Weekenders and securing places on the prestigious Venice Biennale Fellowship - our students regularly engage with the public, and gain vital artist exposure. Your studio practice and creative community

The course is led and supported by a stimulating community of creative practitioners. The core academic team are experienced artists who are active makers, writers and researchers in contemporary fine art practice.

We encourage diversity in thinking and making through material exploration, collaborative working, cross-fertilisation of ideas, and the exploration of new concepts and materials.

Partnerships, exhibitions and the professional art world

As a student you will develop an unrivalled understanding of the professional art world through ongoing partnerships with emerging and established galleries, museums, creative organisations and practising artists.

You will gain a deep understanding of the professional landscape through these partnerships, preparing you effectively for a career in the creative sector upon graduation.

BA (Hons) Fine Art students enjoy access to dedicated workspaces, and award-winning facilities. Why choose this course?

  • Our course prioritises contemporary art practice and critical enquiry. As a studio-centred, interdisciplinary programme, it allows you the freedom to work in any medium at any stage, offering the flexibility to shape your own professional journey.

  • Partnerships with ambitious and contemporary art spaces, such as our on-site gallery, MIRROR, and our neighbours, The Box. We think beyond our walls and you will get to test, experiment and exhibit work in real-life professional art settings.

  • Access to industry connections including: KARST, The Box, Sprite Arts Collective, Plymouth Culture, RAAM, Heart for Art, Stoke Village Hub, MIRROR gallery, WonderZoo, Yourway Project and Make Tank.

Careers and future opportunities

Career opportunities include: Professional Artists, Curators, Producers, Arts Facilitators, Exhibition Organisers, Digital Content Creators, Art Therapists, Researchers, Photographers, Lecturers and Teachers, Art Conservators and Framers, Art Handlers, Gallery Owners or Curators, Studio Assistants, Technicians, Directors, Printmakers, Writers and Directors of Artist-run Spaces.

Frequently asked questions What kind of course is BA (Hons) Fine Art?

It is a rigorous and questioning course that encourages an ambitious diversity of approaches in thinking and making, with an interdisciplinary exploration of contemporary art.

How does the course connect studio practice and theory?

You’ll study in a learning environment that provides a meaningful link between your studio practice and contemporary art theory.

What workshops and processes can I explore?

You can participate in workshops for drawing, sound, glass, installation, video, clay, performance, painting, scale and sculpture, projection mapping, wood, printmaking, critical writing, and 3D casting in plaster, alginate and rubber, alongside traditional sculptural practices.

Will I be supported to develop my own individual practice?

Yes. The course focuses on the development of individual practice-based study through exposure to a wide variety of material methods and modes of art practice.

Who will I learn from?

You’ll be led and supported by a stimulating community of creative practitioners, with a core academic team of experienced artists who are active makers, writers and researchers in contemporary fine art practice.

Will I have opportunities to collaborate and experiment?

Yes. The course provides opportunities for working collaboratively, encouraging diversity through material exploration, collaborative working and cross-fertilisation of ideas.

How will the course help me understand the professional art world?

You will develop an unrivalled understanding of the professional art world through ongoing partnerships with emerging and established galleries, museums, creative organisations and practising artists.

Will I have opportunities to exhibit work in professional settings?

Yes. Through partnerships with ambitious and contemporary art spaces such as MIRROR and The Box, you will get to test, experiment and exhibit work in real-life professional art settings.

What careers could this degree support?

Career opportunities include Professional Artists, Curators, Producers, Arts Facilitators, Exhibition Organisers, Digital Content Creators, Art Therapists, Researchers, Photographers, Lecturers and Teachers, Art Conservators and Framers, Art Handlers, Gallery Owners or Curators, Studio Assistants, Technicians, Directors, Printmakers, Writers and Directors of Artist-run Spaces.

Student work by Miranda Hallett-Pullen, BA (Hons) Fine Art, at our 2024 Graduate Shows. Student satisfaction

BA (Hons) Fine Art students gave very strong feedback in the National Student Survey (NSS) 2026, with 100% positive responses to 12 of the 27 individual questions. Students responded positively at 90% or above to 20 of the 27 questions.

Fine Art also received 100% positive responses to both questions in the NSS scale ‘Academic support’: “How easy was it to contact teaching staff when you needed to?” and “How well have teaching staff supported your learning?”

Responding BA (Hons) Fine Art students gave 100% positive responses to questions including:

Learning opportunities

“To what extent have you had the chance to explore ideas and concepts in depth?”
“To what extent have you had the chance to bring together information and ideas from different topics?”

Assessment and feedback

“How clear were the marking criteria used to assess your work?”
“How fair has the marking and assessment been on your course?”
“How often have you received assessment feedback on time?”
“How often does feedback help you to improve your work?”

Academic support, organisation and student voice

“How easy was it to contact teaching staff when you needed to?”
“How well have teaching staff supported your learning?”
“How well organised is your course?”
“How well have the library resources (e.g., books, online services and learning spaces) supported your learning?”
“To what extent do you get the right opportunities to give feedback on your course?”
“How well communicated was information about your university/college’s mental wellbeing support services?”

Postgraduate progression with the Royal College of Art

Graduates of this course can access application guidance, portfolio preparation and progression planning for relevant taught postgraduate programmes at the Royal College of Art through our progression agreement.

Your undergraduate degree is taught and awarded by Arts University Plymouth. Applications to the RCA follow its normal admissions process, and applicants must meet the entry requirements for their chosen programme.

Explore the RCA progression route and scholarships for 2027/28 entry.

Integrated Foundation Year

This degree is also available as a four-year Integrated Foundation option. Our Integrated Foundation provides you with a preparatory year that will support your creative development, through a broad understanding of art, design and media skills relevant to your chosen degree subject. Learning through experimentation, exploration and discovery will support you in progressing to the next level of your degree at Arts University Plymouth.

Support while you study

All students at Arts University Plymouth can access specialist support via our Student Support Team. Our trained advisers offer information and guidance on student finance and funding, disability support, counselling and more.

Click here to read more about the support we offer.

course.revalidationMessage:
Applying to study with us in 2021?

We are excited to relaunch this course with a new title for 2021 as we enhance our well-established undergraduate curriculum.

Degrees listed as subject to validation are in the final stage of our rigorous approval process, designed to ensure they accurately reflect course content and employment opportunities for students. Through close consultation with industry professionals, academics, students and alumni we can ensure that your learning prepares you for a dynamic and ever-changing future job market.

contentBlocks.heading: Prepare for success in Fine Art

contentBlocks.text: Our BA (Hons) Fine Art course is rigorous and questioning, encouraging an ambitious diversity of approaches in thinking and making. We promote an interdisciplinary exploration of contemporary art, where you will gain skills to critically question and actively create.

contentBlocks.bodyText: The course provides opportunities for working collaboratively, deepening cultural understanding and exploring new processes in workshops, within a learning environment that provides a meaningful link between your studio practice and contemporary art theory.

contentBlocks.caption: Find out more about BA (Hons) Fine Art at Arts University Plymouth.

contentBlocks.heading: At a glance
contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Degree: BA (Hons) Fine Art

  • UCAS codes: 3-year degree W101 / 4-year Integrated Foundation W103

  • Typical UCAS points: 104–120

This is a dynamic course that supports ambitious, interdisciplinary contemporary art practice, encouraging you to critically question and actively create.

You’ll be supported to develop your individual practice-based study through exposure to a wide variety of material methods and modes of art practice.

contentBlocks.blockquote: I wouldn’t change any of the decisions that led me here. I’m so glad that I quit my job in London and came back to the South West to study Fine Art at Arts University Plymouth. That was the best decision I’ve ever made.
contentBlocks.attribution: MOLLY ERIN MCCARTHY, BA (HONS) FINE ART GRADUATE

image.title: Colourful guests chatting next to work by Rebecca Alford at BA Hons Fine Art Grad Shows Summer 2025

contentBlocks.caption: Students exhibit work throughout the year – including at the university's annual Graduate Shows.

contentBlocks.heading: What you’ll learn and how you’ll study

contentBlocks.bodyText:
You’ll participate in workshops that allow you to explore new processes while connecting studio practice with contemporary art theory.

Workshops include opportunities across drawing, sound, glass, installation, video, clay, performance, painting, scale and sculpture, projection mapping, wood, printmaking and critical writing.

You can also explore 3D casting in plaster, alginate and rubber, alongside traditional sculptural practices.

Guests looking at work at BA Hons Fine Art Summer Shows 2022
BA Hons Fine Art Graduate Show Summer 2026 The Mythcorrhizal Tree by Vanessa Crosse
BA Hons Fine Art Summer Show 2022
BA Hons Fine Art cohort winners of The Deans Award at the 2024 Grad Shows

contentBlocks.caption: From forming international artist collectives, winning awards, exhibiting at Art Weekenders and securing places on the prestigious Venice Biennale Fellowship - our students regularly engage with the public, and gain vital artist exposure.

contentBlocks.heading: Your studio practice and creative community

contentBlocks.bodyText:
The course is led and supported by a stimulating community of creative practitioners. The core academic team are experienced artists who are active makers, writers and researchers in contemporary fine art practice.

We encourage diversity in thinking and making through material exploration, collaborative working, cross-fertilisation of ideas, and the exploration of new concepts and materials.

contentBlocks.heading: Partnerships, exhibitions and the professional art world

contentBlocks.bodyText:
As a student you will develop an unrivalled understanding of the professional art world through ongoing partnerships with emerging and established galleries, museums, creative organisations and practising artists.

You will gain a deep understanding of the professional landscape through these partnerships, preparing you effectively for a career in the creative sector upon graduation.

image.title: Guests and students at BA Hons Fine Art Grad Shows Summer 2024 work by Dezeta Fantie

contentBlocks.caption: BA (Hons) Fine Art students enjoy access to dedicated workspaces, and award-winning facilities.

contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Our course prioritises contemporary art practice and critical enquiry. As a studio-centred, interdisciplinary programme, it allows you the freedom to work in any medium at any stage, offering the flexibility to shape your own professional journey.

  • Partnerships with ambitious and contemporary art spaces, such as our on-site gallery, MIRROR, and our neighbours, The Box. We think beyond our walls and you will get to test, experiment and exhibit work in real-life professional art settings.

  • Access to industry connections including: KARST, The Box, Sprite Arts Collective, Plymouth Culture, RAAM, Heart for Art, Stoke Village Hub, MIRROR gallery, WonderZoo, Yourway Project and Make Tank.

Career opportunities include: Professional Artists, Curators, Producers, Arts Facilitators, Exhibition Organisers, Digital Content Creators, Art Therapists, Researchers, Photographers, Lecturers and Teachers, Art Conservators and Framers, Art Handlers, Gallery Owners or Curators, Studio Assistants, Technicians, Directors, Printmakers, Writers and Directors of Artist-run Spaces.

items.heading: What kind of course is BA (Hons) Fine Art?
items.bodyText: It is a rigorous and questioning course that encourages an ambitious diversity of approaches in thinking and making, with an interdisciplinary exploration of contemporary art.

items.heading: How does the course connect studio practice and theory?
items.bodyText: You’ll study in a learning environment that provides a meaningful link between your studio practice and contemporary art theory.

items.heading: What workshops and processes can I explore?
items.bodyText: You can participate in workshops for drawing, sound, glass, installation, video, clay, performance, painting, scale and sculpture, projection mapping, wood, printmaking, critical writing, and 3D casting in plaster, alginate and rubber, alongside traditional sculptural practices.

items.heading: Will I be supported to develop my own individual practice?
items.bodyText: Yes. The course focuses on the development of individual practice-based study through exposure to a wide variety of material methods and modes of art practice.

items.heading: Who will I learn from?
items.bodyText: You’ll be led and supported by a stimulating community of creative practitioners, with a core academic team of experienced artists who are active makers, writers and researchers in contemporary fine art practice.

items.heading: Will I have opportunities to collaborate and experiment?
items.bodyText: Yes. The course provides opportunities for working collaboratively, encouraging diversity through material exploration, collaborative working and cross-fertilisation of ideas.

items.heading: How will the course help me understand the professional art world?
items.bodyText: You will develop an unrivalled understanding of the professional art world through ongoing partnerships with emerging and established galleries, museums, creative organisations and practising artists.

items.heading: Will I have opportunities to exhibit work in professional settings?
items.bodyText: Yes. Through partnerships with ambitious and contemporary art spaces such as MIRROR and The Box, you will get to test, experiment and exhibit work in real-life professional art settings.

items.heading: What careers could this degree support?
items.bodyText: Career opportunities include Professional Artists, Curators, Producers, Arts Facilitators, Exhibition Organisers, Digital Content Creators, Art Therapists, Researchers, Photographers, Lecturers and Teachers, Art Conservators and Framers, Art Handlers, Gallery Owners or Curators, Studio Assistants, Technicians, Directors, Printmakers, Writers and Directors of Artist-run Spaces.

image.title: BA Hons Fine Art Grad Shows Summer 2024 colourful installation in white room with various household artefacts piled in centre

contentBlocks.caption: Student work by Miranda Hallett-Pullen, BA (Hons) Fine Art, at our 2024 Graduate Shows.

contentBlocks.bodyText:
BA (Hons) Fine Art students gave very strong feedback in the National Student Survey (NSS) 2026, with 100% positive responses to 12 of the 27 individual questions. Students responded positively at 90% or above to 20 of the 27 questions.

Fine Art also received 100% positive responses to both questions in the NSS scale ‘Academic support’: “How easy was it to contact teaching staff when you needed to?” and “How well have teaching staff supported your learning?”

Responding BA (Hons) Fine Art students gave 100% positive responses to questions including:

Learning opportunities

“To what extent have you had the chance to explore ideas and concepts in depth?”
“To what extent have you had the chance to bring together information and ideas from different topics?”

Assessment and feedback

“How clear were the marking criteria used to assess your work?”
“How fair has the marking and assessment been on your course?”
“How often have you received assessment feedback on time?”
“How often does feedback help you to improve your work?”

Academic support, organisation and student voice

“How easy was it to contact teaching staff when you needed to?”
“How well have teaching staff supported your learning?”
“How well organised is your course?”
“How well have the library resources (e.g., books, online services and learning spaces) supported your learning?”
“To what extent do you get the right opportunities to give feedback on your course?”
“How well communicated was information about your university/college’s mental wellbeing support services?”

contentBlocks.heading: Postgraduate progression with the Royal College of Art
contentBlocks.bodyText:
Graduates of this course can access application guidance, portfolio preparation and progression planning for relevant taught postgraduate programmes at the Royal College of Art through our progression agreement.

Your undergraduate degree is taught and awarded by Arts University Plymouth. Applications to the RCA follow its normal admissions process, and applicants must meet the entry requirements for their chosen programme.

Explore the RCA progression route and scholarships for 2027/28 entry.

contentBlocks.heading: Integrated Foundation Year
contentBlocks.bodyText: This degree is also available as a four-year Integrated Foundation option. Our Integrated Foundation provides you with a preparatory year that will support your creative development, through a broad understanding of art, design and media skills relevant to your chosen degree subject. Learning through experimentation, exploration and discovery will support you in progressing to the next level of your degree at Arts University Plymouth.

contentBlocks.heading: Support while you study
contentBlocks.bodyText:
All students at Arts University Plymouth can access specialist support via our Student Support Team. Our trained advisers offer information and guidance on student finance and funding, disability support, counselling and more.

Click here to read more about the support we offer.

contentBlocks.heading: What are my options after completing this degree?

contentBlocks.bodyText:
After graduating from BA (Hons) Film & Screen Arts, you could continue your studies at Arts University Plymouth on one of the postgraduate courses listed below. Our graduates are entitled to a 15% discount on tuition fees for our MA programmes.

Through our partnership with the Royal College of Art, graduates of this course can also access application guidance and portfolio preparation for relevant RCA postgraduate programmes.

We see this as an exciting opportunity to nurture independently minded designers ready to meet the demands of a dynamic, forward-thinking industry. Blending traditional, digital and experimental practices, this course is built around innovation and sustainable thinking, combining craftsmanship and precision through hands-on making, colour and material development, and emerging technologies that amplify your ideas. Find out more about BA (Hons) Textile Design at Arts University Plymouth. At a glance Degree: BA (Hons) Textile Design UCAS codes: 3-year degree WYC2 / 4-year Integrated Foundation J400 Typical UCAS points: 104–120 Course approach: project-based, student-led and collaborative Sustainable thinking, colour and material innovation You will explore regenerative and circular design through hands-on, non-toxic processes, alongside the creative science of colour and material development. This includes experimenting with natural dyes, responding to projects that explore biomaterials, and developing innovative applications that shape the future of textiles. You will also work with our natural dye garden and locally sourced materials, supporting an ethos of environmentally responsible design. Resources in the Textile Design studio include knitting machines, a natural dye lab where locally grown plants are used to make vibrant colours for fabric dyeing, a tufting room where students can learn how to make rugs and other textured textiles, and a screenprinting area with large tables, screen coating and washing areas, drying racks and exposure units. Digital tools, AI and prototyping Engage critically and creatively with emerging technologies that provide new ways to amplify your ideas, using AI, 3D modelling and digital prototyping to strike a balance between craftsmanship and precision. It is rare to see such a wealth of facilities as you have in Arts University Plymouth. It is an incredible site. DANIEL HEATH, AWARD-WINNING TEXTILE & SURFACE PATTERN DESIGNER, ON A VISIT TO THE CAMPUS IN 2023 Facilities, studios and resources Our industry-standard facilities include a dedicated textile print room and knit, dye, stitch and tufting studios, alongside access to Fab Lab South West tools such as laser cutters, CNC machines and 3D printers. Inspired by place in Britain’s Ocean City Studying in Britain’s Ocean City, you will draw inspiration from the dramatic coastlines of Devon and Cornwall and the raw textures of Dartmoor. You’ll ground global ideas in the hyperlocal through briefs, materials and partnerships. Industry software and trend awareness Use software trusted across the industry, AVA, Adobe Creative Cloud, WGSN and The Future Laboratory, helping you build the trend awareness and technical fluency needed to respond to global markets. Live projects and international opportunities This course is project-based, student-led and collaborative. You’ll work on live projects and gain industry insight through guest lectures with organisations such as Finisterre, National Trust, Mercedes, Princess Yachts, Red and RAMM. International opportunities typically include visits to leading trade shows such as Première Vision, Maison&Objet and Heimtextil, with recent trips to Milan, Paris, Amsterdam, St Ives and London. Why choose this course? Create with purpose: explore non-toxic processes, natural dyes and future-facing sustainable design. Get hands-on: access specialist textile studios and cutting-edge digital tools in our Fab Lab. Be inspired by place: work with materials and ideas rooted in our coast, moors and natural dye garden. Connect with industry: collaborate on live projects and gain experience through global trips and events. Shape your future: graduate with the skills, mindset and adaptability to thrive across fashion, interiors and material innovation. BA (Hons) Textile Design students in our Biomaterials Lab, learning about algae-based biomaterials for textiles, led by Yan Feng, Biomaterial Researcher and Textile Designer. Careers and future opportunities Career opportunities include: Textile Designers, Surface Pattern Designers, Design Stylists, Trend Forecasters, Materials Researchers, Textile Buyers and Sustainable Design Consultants. Our graduates leave with an interdisciplinary mindset. They are adaptable, critical thinkers ready to innovate across the design industries, from fashion and interiors to material research and beyond. Frequently asked questions What is BA (Hons) Textile Design built around? It blends traditional, digital and experimental practices and is built around innovation and sustainable thinking. What sustainable approaches will I explore? You will explore regenerative and circular design through hands-on, non-toxic processes, including natural dyes, biomaterials projects, locally sourced materials and work connected to the natural dye garden. Will I use digital tools and emerging technologies? Yes. You will use AI, 3D modelling and digital prototyping to amplify your ideas and balance craftsmanship with precision. What facilities will I have access to? You’ll have access to a dedicated textile print room, knit, dye, stitch and tufting studios, and Fab Lab South West tools such as laser cutters, CNC machines and 3D printers. What software will I use? You’ll use AVA, Adobe Creative Cloud, WGSN and The Future Laboratory to build trend awareness and technical fluency for global markets. Will I work on live projects and hear from industry? Yes. You’ll work on live projects and gain industry insight through guest lectures with organisations such as Finisterre, National Trust, Mercedes, Princess Yachts, Red and RAMM. Are there international opportunities? Yes. International opportunities typically include visits to trade shows such as Première Vision, Maison&Objet and Heimtextil, with recent trips to Milan, Paris, Amsterdam, St Ives and London. What careers could this degree lead to? Career opportunities include Textile Designers, Surface Pattern Designers, Design Stylists, Trend Forecasters, Materials Researchers, Textile Buyers and Sustainable Design Consultants. “I definitely feel like our individuality was nurtured, and although hard work, the programme and tutors have given me the confidence I need to now start setting up my own business. The facilities are second to none, and if I had to re-do my degree, I would still choose Arts University Plymouth.” Winona Flay, BA (Hons) Printed Textile Design & Surface Pattern Postgraduate progression with the Royal College of Art Graduates of this course can access application guidance, portfolio preparation and progression planning for relevant taught postgraduate programmes at the Royal College of Art through our progression agreement. This includes experimenting with natural dyes, responding to projects that explore biomaterials, and developing innovative applications that shape the future of textiles.

You will also work with our natural dye garden and locally sourced materials, supporting an ethos of environmentally responsible design.

Resources in the Textile Design studio include knitting machines, a natural dye lab where locally grown plants are used to make vibrant colours for fabric dyeing, a tufting room where students can learn how to make rugs and other textured textiles, and a screenprinting area with large tables, screen coating and washing areas, drying racks and exposure units. Digital tools, AI and prototyping

Engage critically and creatively with emerging technologies that provide new ways to amplify your ideas, using AI, 3D modelling and digital prototyping to strike a balance between craftsmanship and precision.

It is rare to see such a wealth of facilities as you have in Arts University Plymouth. It is an incredible site. DANIEL HEATH, AWARD-WINNING TEXTILE & SURFACE PATTERN DESIGNER, ON A VISIT TO THE CAMPUS IN 2023 Facilities, studios and resources

Our industry-standard facilities include a dedicated textile print room and knit, dye, stitch and tufting studios, alongside access to Fab Lab South West tools such as laser cutters, CNC machines and 3D printers.

Inspired by place in Britain’s Ocean City

Studying in Britain’s Ocean City, you will draw inspiration from the dramatic coastlines of Devon and Cornwall and the raw textures of Dartmoor.

You’ll ground global ideas in the hyperlocal through briefs, materials and partnerships.

Industry software and trend awareness

Use software trusted across the industry, AVA, Adobe Creative Cloud, WGSN and The Future Laboratory, helping you build the trend awareness and technical fluency needed to respond to global markets.

Live projects and international opportunities

This course is project-based, student-led and collaborative. You’ll work on live projects and gain industry insight through guest lectures with organisations such as Finisterre, National Trust, Mercedes, Princess Yachts, Red and RAMM.

International opportunities typically include visits to leading trade shows such as Première Vision, Maison&Objet and Heimtextil, with recent trips to Milan, Paris, Amsterdam, St Ives and London.

Why choose this course?

  • Create with purpose: explore non-toxic processes, natural dyes and future-facing sustainable design.

  • Get hands-on: access specialist textile studios and cutting-edge digital tools in our Fab Lab.

  • Be inspired by place: work with materials and ideas rooted in our coast, moors and natural dye garden.

  • Connect with industry: collaborate on live projects and gain experience through global trips and events.

  • Shape your future: graduate with the skills, mindset and adaptability to thrive across fashion, interiors and material innovation.

BA (Hons) Textile Design students in our Biomaterials Lab, learning about algae-based biomaterials for textiles, led by Yan Feng, Biomaterial Researcher and Textile Designer. Careers and future opportunities

Career opportunities include: Textile Designers, Surface Pattern Designers, Design Stylists, Trend Forecasters, Materials Researchers, Textile Buyers and Sustainable Design Consultants.

Our graduates leave with an interdisciplinary mindset. They are adaptable, critical thinkers ready to innovate across the design industries, from fashion and interiors to material research and beyond.

Frequently asked questions What is BA (Hons) Textile Design built around?

It blends traditional, digital and experimental practices and is built around innovation and sustainable thinking.

What sustainable approaches will I explore?

You will explore regenerative and circular design through hands-on, non-toxic processes, including natural dyes, biomaterials projects, locally sourced materials and work connected to the natural dye garden.

Will I use digital tools and emerging technologies?

Yes. You will use AI, 3D modelling and digital prototyping to amplify your ideas and balance craftsmanship with precision.

What facilities will I have access to?

You’ll have access to a dedicated textile print room, knit, dye, stitch and tufting studios, and Fab Lab South West tools such as laser cutters, CNC machines and 3D printers.

What software will I use?

You’ll use AVA, Adobe Creative Cloud, WGSN and The Future Laboratory to build trend awareness and technical fluency for global markets.

Will I work on live projects and hear from industry?

Yes. You’ll work on live projects and gain industry insight through guest lectures with organisations such as Finisterre, National Trust, Mercedes, Princess Yachts, Red and RAMM.

Are there international opportunities?

Yes. International opportunities typically include visits to trade shows such as Première Vision, Maison&Objet and Heimtextil, with recent trips to Milan, Paris, Amsterdam, St Ives and London.

What careers could this degree lead to?

Career opportunities include Textile Designers, Surface Pattern Designers, Design Stylists, Trend Forecasters, Materials Researchers, Textile Buyers and Sustainable Design Consultants.

“I definitely feel like our individuality was nurtured, and although hard work, the programme and tutors have given me the confidence I need to now start setting up my own business. The facilities are second to none, and if I had to re-do my degree, I would still choose Arts University Plymouth.” Winona Flay, BA (Hons) Printed Textile Design & Surface Pattern Postgraduate progression with the Royal College of Art

Graduates of this course can access application guidance, portfolio preparation and progression planning for relevant taught postgraduate programmes at the Royal College of Art through our progression agreement.

Your undergraduate degree is taught and awarded by Arts University Plymouth. Applications to the RCA follow its normal admissions process, and applicants must meet the entry requirements for their chosen programme.

Explore the RCA progression route and scholarships for 2027/28 entry.

Integrated Foundation Year

This degree is also available as a four-year Integrated Foundation option. Our Integrated Foundation provides you with a preparatory year that will support your creative development, through a broad understanding of art, design and media skills relevant to your chosen degree subject. Learning through experimentation, exploration and discovery will support you in progressing to the next level of your degree at Arts University Plymouth.

Support while you study

All students at Arts University Plymouth can access specialist support via our Student Support Team. Our trained advisers offer information and guidance on student finance and funding, disability support, counselling and more.

Click here to read more about the support we offer.

Get in touch

Email: admissions@aup.ac.uk / textiledesign@aup.ac.uk

Instagram: @aup_textiledesign

After graduating from BA (Hons) Film & Screen Arts, you could continue your studies at Arts University Plymouth on one of the postgraduate courses listed below. Our graduates are entitled to a 15% discount on tuition fees for our MA programmes.

contentBlocks.text: The textile industry is evolving rapidly. We see this as an exciting opportunity to nurture independently minded designers ready to meet the demands of a dynamic, forward-thinking industry.

contentBlocks.blockquote: “I definitely feel like our individuality was nurtured, and although hard work, the programme and tutors have given me the confidence I need to now start setting up my own business. The facilities are second to none, and if I had to re-do my degree, I would still choose Arts University Plymouth.”

contentBlocks.heading: Postgraduate progression with the Royal College of Art
contentBlocks.bodyText:
Graduates of this course can access application guidance, portfolio preparation and progression planning for relevant taught postgraduate programmes at the Royal College of Art through our progression agreement.

Your undergraduate degree is taught and awarded by Arts University Plymouth. Applications to the RCA follow its normal admissions process, and applicants must meet the entry requirements for their chosen programme.

Explore the RCA progression route and scholarships for 2027/28 entry.

contentBlocks.heading: Integrated Foundation Year
contentBlocks.bodyText: This degree is also available as a four-year Integrated Foundation option. Our Integrated Foundation provides you with a preparatory year that will support your creative development, through a broad understanding of art, design and media skills relevant to your chosen degree subject. Learning through experimentation, exploration and discovery will support you in progressing to the next level of your degree at Arts University Plymouth.

contentBlocks.heading: Support while you study
contentBlocks.bodyText:
All students at Arts University Plymouth can access specialist support via our Student Support Team. Our trained advisers offer information and guidance on student finance and funding, disability support, counselling and more.

Click here to read more about the support we offer.

contentBlocks.heading: What are my options after completing this degree?

contentBlocks.bodyText:
After graduating from BA (Hons) Film & Screen Arts, you could continue your studies at Arts University Plymouth on one of the postgraduate courses listed below. Our graduates are entitled to a 15% discount on tuition fees for our MA programmes.

Through our partnership with the Royal College of Art, graduates of this course can also access application guidance and portfolio preparation for relevant RCA postgraduate programmes.

With a focus on cinematic storytelling, the course allows you to design and create storyworlds for a range of audiences, and to gain real insight into the global filmmaking industries. Within this course you will explore the practical craft skills necessary to succeed as a practical filmmaker or content producer, while being guided from the initial idea to shooting and screening. Find out more about BA (Hons) Film & Screen Arts at Arts University Plymouth. At a glance Degree: BA (Hons) Film & Screen Arts UCAS codes: 3-year degree W692 / 4-year Integrated Foundation P311 UCAS points: 104–120 What you’ll learn and how you’ll study You’ll explore the practical craft skills necessary to succeed as a practical filmmaker or content producer, including: Cinematography and lighting design Directing and camera operation Sound design and mixing Production design and art direction Editing and post-production In addition to practical skills, you’ll be challenged to consider the societal role of film, the effect of online streaming on cinema, and effective strategies to showcase your work. From the initial idea, to shooting and screening, you’ll be guided to think critically about your creative techniques in the context of culture, society and the broader world. There’s so much freedom on the film course to try anything you want, I definitely enjoyed being encouraged to get out of my comfort zone and try new things. Lucie Eckersley Creative collaboration and contemporary forms Studying filmmaking in an arts university fosters creative collaborations, leading to the creation of unique works that go beyond traditional film forms, such as screen-based installations, music videos, and site-specific cinema. Led by a team of practising filmmakers, sound artists and film writers, all areas of your learning are underpinned by critical thinking and cultural enquiry to encourage understanding of how film functions in its many contemporary forms. Facilities, studios and professional equipment Our experienced technicians support your practical learning, and you’ll have access to outstanding facilities, including film and media studios, sound recording and post-production studios, vocal recording booths and foley studio space. Our Multimedia Studio is stocked with specialist media equipment, including Arri Alexa, Black Magic Ursa, 8mm film cameras, Arri Super 16mm cinema cameras and a Blackmagic Cintel film scanner, camera rigs, specialist lighting kit, sound-recording kit and much more. Why choose this course? Practical filmmaking is at the heart of what and how we study. Expect practical skills and workshops covering all filmmaking roles. Access to professional filmmaking equipment, from motion-picture film cameras to industry-standard digital cinema cameras. Studio facilities include an infinity green screen cove, sound-recording studio and editing workstations in class. Filmmaking is at the centre of every unit and you will be asked to experiment and develop methods of practice that match your creative intentions. Whether on location or in the studio, you will be confidently in control of the work you make. Encouragement to enter film festivals in the UK, Europe and beyond, as well as the opportunity to showcase work in an on-site independent cinema. Students benefit from our partnership with Real Ideas, which provides opportunities to create and screen 360-degree content in Europe’s first-of-its-kind immersive dome, also compatible with VR, augmented reality and mixed reality. Arts University Plymouth Logo Skip to Content Our Courses Open Days Apply Now Menu Apply Now Our Courses Open Days Chevron Down About Us Chevron Down Study Chevron Down International Chevron Down Student Life Alumni Chevron Down Visit Resources Chevron Down Research & Innovation Prospectus Latest News What's On Established 1856 Student Login Staff Login Contact Us Explore our Undergraduate courses BA (Hons) Film & Screen Arts Course Duration Full-time: 3 years / Part-time: 6 years Integrated Foundation: Full-time 4 years / Part-time: 7 years Course Contact film@aup.ac.uk Admissions Contact admissions@aup.ac.uk +44 (0)1752 203434 UCAS Code Course: W692 Institution: P65 Apply Now Register Your Interest Overview Course & Units Entry Requirements Staff Careers & Alumni Ask a Student Resources Fees & Funding Overview Prepare for success in film and screen arts BA (Hons) Film & Screen Arts is a practical filmmaking course that focuses on the craft and aesthetics of contemporary filmmaking. With a focus on cinematic storytelling, the course allows you to design and create storyworlds for a range of audiences, and to gain real insight into the global filmmaking industries.

Within this course you will explore the practical craft skills necessary to succeed as a practical filmmaker or content producer, while being guided from the initial idea to shooting and screening.

Find out more about BA (Hons) Film & Screen Arts at Arts University Plymouth. At a glance

  • Degree: BA (Hons) Film & Screen Arts

  • UCAS codes: 3-year degree W692 / 4-year Integrated Foundation P311

  • UCAS points: 104–120

What you’ll learn and how you’ll study

You’ll explore the practical craft skills necessary to succeed as a practical filmmaker or content producer, including:

  • Cinematography and lighting design

  • Directing and camera operation

  • Sound design and mixing

  • Production design and art direction

  • Editing and post-production

In addition to practical skills, you’ll be challenged to consider the societal role of film, the effect of online streaming on cinema, and effective strategies to showcase your work. From the initial idea, to shooting and screening, you’ll be guided to think critically about your creative techniques in the context of culture, society and the broader world.

There’s so much freedom on the film course to try anything you want, I definitely enjoyed being encouraged to get out of my comfort zone and try new things. Lucie Eckersley Creative collaboration and contemporary forms

Studying filmmaking in an arts university fosters creative collaborations, leading to the creation of unique works that go beyond traditional film forms, such as screen-based installations, music videos, and site-specific cinema.

Led by a team of practising filmmakers, sound artists and film writers, all areas of your learning are underpinned by critical thinking and cultural enquiry to encourage understanding of how film functions in its many contemporary forms.

Facilities, studios and professional equipment

Our experienced technicians support your practical learning, and you’ll have access to outstanding facilities, including film and media studios, sound recording and post-production studios, vocal recording booths and foley studio space.

Our Multimedia Studio is stocked with specialist media equipment, including Arri Alexa, Black Magic Ursa, 8mm film cameras, Arri Super 16mm cinema cameras and a Blackmagic Cintel film scanner, camera rigs, specialist lighting kit, sound-recording kit and much more.

Why choose this course?

  • Practical filmmaking is at the heart of what and how we study. Expect practical skills and workshops covering all filmmaking roles.

  • Access to professional filmmaking equipment, from motion-picture film cameras to industry-standard digital cinema cameras. Studio facilities include an infinity green screen cove, sound-recording studio and editing workstations in class.

  • Filmmaking is at the centre of every unit and you will be asked to experiment and develop methods of practice that match your creative intentions. Whether on location or in the studio, you will be confidently in control of the work you make.

  • Encouragement to enter film festivals in the UK, Europe and beyond, as well as the opportunity to showcase work in an on-site independent cinema.

  • Students benefit from our partnership with Real Ideas, which provides opportunities to create and screen 360-degree content in Europe’s first-of-its-kind immersive dome, also compatible with VR, augmented reality and mixed reality.

Careers and future opportunities

Career opportunities include: Independent Filmmakers, Commercial Filmmakers, Documentary Filmmakers, Artist Filmmakers, Directors, Producers, Production Designers, Cinematographers, Scriptwriters, Editors, Location Managers, Researchers, Post-Production Specialists and Sound Designers.

Frequently asked questions What is BA (Hons) Film & Screen Arts focused on?

It’s a practical filmmaking course focused on the craft and aesthetics of contemporary filmmaking, with cinematic storytelling at its core.

What practical filmmaking skills will I develop?

You’ll develop practical craft skills including cinematography and lighting design, directing and camera operation, sound design and mixing, production design and art direction, and editing and post-production.

Does the course cover the wider context of film today?

Yes. Alongside practical skills, you’ll be challenged to consider the societal role of film, the effect of online streaming on cinema, and effective strategies to showcase your work.

Will I be supported from idea to screening?

Yes. From the initial idea to shooting and screening, you’ll be guided to think critically about your creative techniques in the context of culture, society and the broader world.

What kinds of creative outcomes could I make?

Studying filmmaking in an arts university fosters creative collaborations that can lead to unique works beyond traditional film forms, such as screen-based installations, music videos and site-specific cinema.

What facilities and studios will I have access to?

You’ll have access to film and media studios, sound recording and post-production studios, vocal recording booths and foley studio space, supported by experienced technicians.

What equipment is available in the Multimedia Studio?

The Multimedia Studio includes specialist equipment such as Arri Alexa, Black Magic Ursa, 8mm film cameras, Arri Super 16mm cinema cameras, a Blackmagic Cintel film scanner, camera rigs, specialist lighting kit and sound-recording kit.

Will I be encouraged to enter film festivals and showcase my work?

Yes. You’ll be encouraged to enter film festivals in the UK, Europe and beyond, and to showcase work in an on-site independent cinema.

What is the partnership with Real Ideas?

Through a partnership with Real Ideas, you can create and screen 360-degree content in Europe’s first-of-its-kind immersive dome, compatible with VR, augmented reality and mixed reality.

What careers could this degree lead to?

Career opportunities include Independent Filmmakers, Commercial Filmmakers, Documentary Filmmakers, Artist Filmmakers, Directors, Producers, Production Designers, Cinematographers, Scriptwriters, Editors, Location Managers, Researchers, Post-Production Specialists and Sound Designers.

Student satisfaction

BA (Hons) Film & Screen Arts students responded especially positively to National Student Survey (NSS) 2026 questions about teaching, assessment feedback, academic support and library resources. Responding students gave 100% positive responses to 3 of the 27 individual questions and responded positively at 90% or above to 13 of the 27 questions.

Film & Screen Arts students gave 100% positive responses to the questions:

“How good are teaching staff at explaining things?”
“How often have you received assessment feedback on time?”
“How well have the library resources (e.g., books, online services and learning spaces) supported your learning?”

Students also responded positively at 91.7% to questions including “How often do teaching staff make the subject engaging?”, “To what extent have you had the chance to explore ideas and concepts in depth?”, “How fair has the marking and assessment been on your course?”, “How easy was it to contact teaching staff when you needed to?” and “How well have teaching staff supported your learning?”

Jack Kruyswijk, Impact Film Postgraduate progression with the Royal College of Art

contentBlocks.heading: Prepare for success in film and screen arts

contentBlocks.text: BA (Hons) Film & Screen Arts is a practical filmmaking course that focuses on the craft and aesthetics of contemporary filmmaking. With a focus on cinematic storytelling, the course allows you to design and create storyworlds for a range of audiences, and to gain real insight into the global filmmaking industries.

contentBlocks.bodyText: Within this course you will explore the practical craft skills necessary to succeed as a practical filmmaker or content producer, while being guided from the initial idea to shooting and screening.

contentBlocks.caption: Find out more about BA (Hons) Film & Screen Arts at Arts University Plymouth.

contentBlocks.heading: At a glance
contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Degree: BA (Hons) Film & Screen Arts

  • UCAS codes: 3-year degree W692 / 4-year Integrated Foundation P311

  • UCAS points: 104–120

contentBlocks.heading: What you’ll learn and how you’ll study

contentBlocks.bodyText:
You’ll explore the practical craft skills necessary to succeed as a practical filmmaker or content producer, including:

  • Cinematography and lighting design

  • Directing and camera operation

  • Sound design and mixing

  • Production design and art direction

  • Editing and post-production

In addition to practical skills, you’ll be challenged to consider the societal role of film, the effect of online streaming on cinema, and effective strategies to showcase your work. From the initial idea, to shooting and screening, you’ll be guided to think critically about your creative techniques in the context of culture, society and the broader world.

contentBlocks.blockquote: There’s so much freedom on the film course to try anything you want, I definitely enjoyed being encouraged to get out of my comfort zone and try new things.
contentBlocks.attribution: Lucie Eckersley

contentBlocks.bodyText:
Studying filmmaking in an arts university fosters creative collaborations, leading to the creation of unique works that go beyond traditional film forms, such as screen-based installations, music videos, and site-specific cinema.

Led by a team of practising filmmakers, sound artists and film writers, all areas of your learning are underpinned by critical thinking and cultural enquiry to encourage understanding of how film functions in its many contemporary forms.

Our experienced technicians support your practical learning, and you’ll have access to outstanding facilities, including film and media studios, sound recording and post-production studios, vocal recording booths and foley studio space.

Our Multimedia Studio is stocked with specialist media equipment, including Arri Alexa, Black Magic Ursa, 8mm film cameras, Arri Super 16mm cinema cameras and a Blackmagic Cintel film scanner, camera rigs, specialist lighting kit, sound-recording kit and much more.

• Practical filmmaking is at the heart of what and how we study. Expect practical skills and workshops covering all filmmaking roles.

  • Access to professional filmmaking equipment, from motion-picture film cameras to industry-standard digital cinema cameras. Studio facilities include an infinity green screen cove, sound-recording studio and editing workstations in class.

  • Filmmaking is at the centre of every unit and you will be asked to experiment and develop methods of practice that match your creative intentions. Whether on location or in the studio, you will be confidently in control of the work you make.

  • Encouragement to enter film festivals in the UK, Europe and beyond, as well as the opportunity to showcase work in an on-site independent cinema.

  • Students benefit from our partnership with Real Ideas, which provides opportunities to create and screen 360-degree content in Europe’s first-of-its-kind immersive dome, also compatible with VR, augmented reality and mixed reality.

Career opportunities include: Independent Filmmakers, Commercial Filmmakers, Documentary Filmmakers, Artist Filmmakers, Directors, Producers, Production Designers, Cinematographers, Scriptwriters, Editors, Location Managers, Researchers, Post-Production Specialists and Sound Designers.

items.heading: What is BA (Hons) Film & Screen Arts focused on?
items.bodyText: It’s a practical filmmaking course focused on the craft and aesthetics of contemporary filmmaking, with cinematic storytelling at its core.

items.heading: What practical filmmaking skills will I develop?
items.bodyText: You’ll develop practical craft skills including cinematography and lighting design, directing and camera operation, sound design and mixing, production design and art direction, and editing and post-production.

items.heading: Does the course cover the wider context of film today?
items.bodyText: Yes. Alongside practical skills, you’ll be challenged to consider the societal role of film, the effect of online streaming on cinema, and effective strategies to showcase your work.

items.heading: Will I be supported from idea to screening?
items.bodyText: Yes. From the initial idea to shooting and screening, you’ll be guided to think critically about your creative techniques in the context of culture, society and the broader world.

items.heading: What kinds of creative outcomes could I make?
items.bodyText: Studying filmmaking in an arts university fosters creative collaborations that can lead to unique works beyond traditional film forms, such as screen-based installations, music videos and site-specific cinema.

items.heading: What facilities and studios will I have access to?
items.bodyText: You’ll have access to film and media studios, sound recording and post-production studios, vocal recording booths and foley studio space, supported by experienced technicians.

items.heading: What equipment is available in the Multimedia Studio?
items.bodyText: The Multimedia Studio includes specialist equipment such as Arri Alexa, Black Magic Ursa, 8mm film cameras, Arri Super 16mm cinema cameras, a Blackmagic Cintel film scanner, camera rigs, specialist lighting kit and sound-recording kit.

items.heading: Will I be encouraged to enter film festivals and showcase my work?
items.bodyText: Yes. You’ll be encouraged to enter film festivals in the UK, Europe and beyond, and to showcase work in an on-site independent cinema.

items.heading: What is the partnership with Real Ideas?
items.bodyText: Through a partnership with Real Ideas, you can create and screen 360-degree content in Europe’s first-of-its-kind immersive dome, compatible with VR, augmented reality and mixed reality.

items.heading: What careers could this degree lead to?
items.bodyText: Career opportunities include Independent Filmmakers, Commercial Filmmakers, Documentary Filmmakers, Artist Filmmakers, Directors, Producers, Production Designers, Cinematographers, Scriptwriters, Editors, Location Managers, Researchers, Post-Production Specialists and Sound Designers.

BA (Hons) Film & Screen Arts students responded especially positively to National Student Survey (NSS) 2026 questions about teaching, assessment feedback, academic support and library resources. Responding students gave 100% positive responses to 3 of the 27 individual questions and responded positively at 90% or above to 13 of the 27 questions.

Film & Screen Arts students gave 100% positive responses to the questions:

“How good are teaching staff at explaining things?”
“How often have you received assessment feedback on time?”
“How well have the library resources (e.g., books, online services and learning spaces) supported your learning?”

Students also responded positively at 91.7% to questions including “How often do teaching staff make the subject engaging?”, “To what extent have you had the chance to explore ideas and concepts in depth?”, “How fair has the marking and assessment been on your course?”, “How easy was it to contact teaching staff when you needed to?” and “How well have teaching staff supported your learning?”

contentBlocks.heading: Postgraduate progression with the Royal College of Art
contentBlocks.bodyText:
If you’re considering postgraduate study after your degree, our partnership with the Royal College of Art supports graduates of this course with application guidance and portfolio preparation for relevant RCA programmes.

Your undergraduate degree is taught and awarded by Arts University Plymouth. Applications to the RCA follow its normal admissions process, and applicants must meet the entry requirements for their chosen programme.

Explore the RCA progression route and scholarships for 2027/28 entry.

contentBlocks.heading: Integrated Foundation Year
contentBlocks.bodyText: This degree is also available as a four-year Integrated Foundation option. Our Integrated Foundation provides you with a preparatory year that will support your creative development, through a broad understanding of art, design and media skills relevant to your chosen degree subject. Learning through experimentation, exploration and discovery will support you in progressing to the next level of your degree at Arts University Plymouth.

contentBlocks.heading: Support while you study
contentBlocks.bodyText:
All students at Arts University Plymouth can access specialist support via our Student Support Team. Our trained advisers offer information and guidance on student finance and funding, disability support, counselling and more.

Click here to read more about the support we offer.

contentBlocks.heading: Get in touch
contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Email: admissions@aup.ac.uk / film@aup.ac.uk
  • Tel: +44 (0)1752 203434
  • Instagram: @aup_filmandscreenarts

contentBlocks.heading: What are my options after completing this degree?

contentBlocks.bodyText:
After graduating from BA (Hons) Film & Screen Arts, you could continue your studies at Arts University Plymouth on one of the postgraduate courses listed below. Our graduates are entitled to a 15% discount on tuition fees for our MA programmes.

Through our partnership with the Royal College of Art, graduates of this course can also access application guidance and portfolio preparation for relevant RCA postgraduate programmes.

Arts University Plymouth Logo Skip to Content Our Courses Open Days Apply Now Menu Apply Now Our Courses Open Days Chevron Down About Us Chevron Down Study Chevron Down International Chevron Down Student Life Alumni Chevron Down Visit Resources Chevron Down Research & Innovation Prospectus Latest News What's On Established 1856 Student Login Staff Login Contact Us Explore our Undergraduate courses BA (Hons) Graphic Design Course Duration Full-time: 3 years / Part-time: 6 years Integrated Foundation: Full-time 4 years / Part-time: 7 years Course Contact graphics@aup.ac.uk Admissions Contact admissions@aup.ac.uk +44 (0)1752 203434 UCAS Code Course: W214 Institution: P65 Apply Now Register your interest Overview Course & Units Entry Requirements Staff Student Work Careers & Alumni Ask a Student Resources Fees & Funding Overview Get ready to thrive at the forefront of the graphic design industry Join the graphic design programme at Arts University Plymouth, where you will experiment and push boundaries to create design that matters. From bold branding to socially responsible campaigns, you’ll master the universal language of design while developing versatile skills that open doors worldwide. With innovation, sustainability and real-world impact at the core of this course, this is your chance to design with purpose and shape a more responsible future. Find out more about BA (Hons) Graphic Design at Arts University Plymouth. At a glance

  • Degree: BA (Hons) Graphic Design

  • UCAS codes: 3-year degree W214 / 4-year Integrated Foundation W211

  • Typical UCAS points: 104–120

Design that matters

From bold branding to socially responsible campaigns, you’ll master the universal language of design while developing versatile skills that open doors worldwide. With innovation, sustainability and real-world impact at the core, you’ll design with purpose and shape a more responsible future.

Student work by Simon Langer We had great opportunities and a great course leader. The team were extremely supportive especially when I started my first graphic design job whilst still studying in the final year. I met a lot of great friends and some amazing contacts. The course allowed me to get my first job as a graphic designer and I am still using skills today. Laura Scott Award-winning creativity and inspiration

Our BA (Hons) Graphic Design course invites you to join award-winning students, recognised by D&AD Best in Show, Creative Conscience, JDO Raw and more. You’ll stay sharp by exploring current trends, culture, and global events, turning everyday inspiration into powerful design.

By promoting self-expression alongside communication for the greater good, you’ll develop the skills to thrive in a fast-moving creative industry.

Skills for a fast-changing industry

These skills, from traditional print practices to brand development and immersive technologies, will enable you to thrive in this ever-changing landscape. Learn to bring your ideas to life both online and offline.

With the support of our expert academics, your studies will instil professional confidence, enriching you personally as you graduate as a progressive problem-solver and effective communicator, equipped with knowledge of ecological sustainability, emerging technologies and user-centred design.

Why choose this course?

  • Build essential skills: from core design and research techniques to creative problem-solving, you’ll develop the foundation to thrive as a designer.

  • Learn by doing: work on real client briefs and projects that connect you directly to the creative industries.

  • Network like a pro: access local and national events such as Plymouth Design Forum, Plymouth Art Weekender, D&AD New Blood Festival, New Designers, and more.

  • Be inspired to lead change: our course pushes you to think differently, innovate, and use design as a tool for impact.

  • Industry connections that matter: gain insight from your own mentor and meet visiting lecturers from leading names like Pentagram Design, Mother London, Getty Images, G.F Smith, Fiasco Design, and Anthony Burrill.
Trevi and BA (Hons) Graphic Design students host event, photography by Codie Hobbs Student satisfaction

BA (Hons) Graphic Design students gave strong National Student Survey 2026 feedback across teaching, creative development, assessment, learning resources and student voice. Responding students gave 100% positive responses to 5 of the 27 individual questions and responded positively at 90% or above to 20 of the 27 questions.

Graphic Design students gave 100% positive responses to the questions:

“To what extent have you had the chance to bring together information and ideas from different topics?”
“How fair has the marking and assessment been on your course?”
“How well have assessments allowed you to demonstrate what you have learned?”
“To what extent do you get the right opportunities to give feedback on your course?”
“How well communicated was information about your university/college’s mental wellbeing support services?”

Students also responded positively at 90.9% to questions about teaching, creative challenge, feedback, learning resources, student voice and freedom of expression.

Careers and future opportunities

Career opportunities include: Graphic Designers, Marketing Managers, Letterpress Designers, Web Designers, Web Coders, Brand Managers, Print Designers, Design Managers, Digital Designers, Motion Graphic Designers, UX Designers, Advertisers, App Designers, Content Producers, Studio Managers, Educators, Editors and Creative Directors.

Student work by Anastasiia Derepa Frequently asked questions What will I do on BA (Hons) Graphic Design?

You’ll experiment and push boundaries to create design that matters, mastering the universal language of design through work ranging from bold branding to socially responsible campaigns.

What is at the core of this course?

Innovation, sustainability and real-world impact are at the core of the course, supporting you to design with purpose and shape a more responsible future.

What kinds of skills will I develop?

You’ll develop versatile skills that open doors worldwide, including skills spanning traditional print practices, brand development and immersive technologies.

Will I work on real client briefs?

Yes. You’ll learn by doing, working on real client briefs and projects that connect you directly to the creative industries.

How will the course help me stay current as a designer?

You’ll stay sharp by exploring current trends, culture and global events, turning everyday inspiration into powerful design.

Will I have opportunities to network and meet industry professionals?

Yes. You’ll access local and national events including Plymouth Design Forum, Plymouth Art Weekender, D&AD New Blood Festival and New Designers, and meet visiting lecturers from leading names such as Pentagram Design, Mother London, Getty Images, G.F Smith, Fiasco Design and Anthony Burrill.

Will I have a mentor?

Yes. You’ll gain insight from your own mentor as part of your industry connections.

How satisfied are students on the course?

In the National Student Survey 2026, students gave 100% positive responses to 5 of the 27 individual questions and responded positively at 90% or above to 20 of the 27 questions.

What careers could this degree lead to?

Career opportunities include Graphic Designers, Letterpress Designers, Web Designers, Brand Managers, Print Designers, Design Managers, Digital Designers, Motion Graphic Designers, UX Designers, Advertisers, App Designers, Content Producers, Studio Managers, Educators, Editors and Creative Directors.

Postgraduate progression with the Royal College of Art

Graduates of this course can access application guidance, portfolio preparation and progression planning for relevant taught postgraduate programmes at the Royal College of Art through our progression agreement.

Your undergraduate degree is taught and awarded by Arts University Plymouth. Applications to the RCA follow its normal admissions process, and applicants must meet the entry requirements for their chosen programme.

Explore the RCA progression route and scholarships for 2027/28 entry.

Integrated Foundation Year

This degree is also available as a four-year Integrated Foundation option. Our Integrated Foundation provides you with a preparatory year that will support your creative development, through a broad understanding of art, design and media skills relevant to your chosen degree subject. Learning through experimentation, exploration and discovery will support you in progressing to the next level of your degree at Arts University Plymouth.

Support while you study

All students at Arts University Plymouth can access specialist support via our Student Support Team. Our trained advisers offer information and guidance on student finance and funding, disability support, counselling and more.

Click here to read more about the support we offer.

Get in touch
  • Email: graphics@aup.ac.uk
  • Tel: +44 (0)1752 203434
  • Instagram: @aup_graphics
What are my options after completing this degree?

After graduating from BA (Hons) Film & Screen Arts, you could continue your studies at Arts University Plymouth on one of the postgraduate courses listed below. Our graduates are entitled to a 15% discount on tuition fees for our MA programmes.

Through our partnership with the Royal College of Art, graduates of this course can also access application guidance and portfolio preparation for relevant RCA postgraduate programmes.

MA Design (Communication) Explore how current social, critical and technological paradigms are changing how designers create and distribute narrative-driven artefacts and campaigns. MA Design Develop products, practices and applications for contemporary society and imagine design beyond the status quo of production and consumption. MA Immersive Media Translate your creative knowledge and digital skills into engaging immersive content and public media experiences for diverse audiences in this exciting and rapidly growing sector. Integrated Foundation Year This degree is also available as a four-year Integrated Foundation option, with a preparatory first year that will support your creative development. items.heading: What will I do on BA (Hons) Graphic Design?
items.bodyText: You’ll experiment and push boundaries to create design that matters, mastering the universal language of design through work ranging from bold branding to socially responsible campaigns.

items.heading: What is at the core of this course?
items.bodyText: Innovation, sustainability and real-world impact are at the core of the course, supporting you to design with purpose and shape a more responsible future.

items.heading: What kinds of skills will I develop?
items.bodyText: You’ll develop versatile skills that open doors worldwide, including skills spanning traditional print practices, brand development and immersive technologies.

items.heading: Will I work on real client briefs?
items.bodyText: Yes. You’ll learn by doing, working on real client briefs and projects that connect you directly to the creative industries.

items.heading: How will the course help me stay current as a designer?
items.bodyText: You’ll stay sharp by exploring current trends, culture and global events, turning everyday inspiration into powerful design.

items.heading: Will I have opportunities to network and meet industry professionals?
items.bodyText: Yes. You’ll access local and national events including Plymouth Design Forum, Plymouth Art Weekender, D&AD New Blood Festival and New Designers, and meet visiting lecturers from leading names such as Pentagram Design, Mother London, Getty Images, G.F Smith, Fiasco Design and Anthony Burrill.

items.heading: Will I have a mentor?
items.bodyText: Yes. You’ll gain insight from your own mentor as part of your industry connections.

items.heading: How satisfied are students on the course?
items.bodyText: In the National Student Survey 2026, students gave 100% positive responses to 5 of the 27 individual questions and responded positively at 90% or above to 20 of the 27 questions.

items.heading: What careers could this degree lead to?
items.bodyText: Career opportunities include Graphic Designers, Letterpress Designers, Web Designers, Brand Managers, Print Designers, Design Managers, Digital Designers, Motion Graphic Designers, UX Designers, Advertisers, App Designers, Content Producers, Studio Managers, Educators, Editors and Creative Directors.

contentBlocks.heading: Postgraduate progression with the Royal College of Art
contentBlocks.bodyText:
Graduates of this course can access application guidance, portfolio preparation and progression planning for relevant taught postgraduate programmes at the Royal College of Art through our progression agreement.

Your undergraduate degree is taught and awarded by Arts University Plymouth. Applications to the RCA follow its normal admissions process, and applicants must meet the entry requirements for their chosen programme.

Explore the RCA progression route and scholarships for 2027/28 entry.

contentBlocks.heading: Integrated Foundation Year
contentBlocks.bodyText: This degree is also available as a four-year Integrated Foundation option. Our Integrated Foundation provides you with a preparatory year that will support your creative development, through a broad understanding of art, design and media skills relevant to your chosen degree subject. Learning through experimentation, exploration and discovery will support you in progressing to the next level of your degree at Arts University Plymouth.

contentBlocks.heading: Support while you study
contentBlocks.bodyText:
All students at Arts University Plymouth can access specialist support via our Student Support Team. Our trained advisers offer information and guidance on student finance and funding, disability support, counselling and more.

Click here to read more about the support we offer.

contentBlocks.bodyText:
After graduating from BA (Hons) Film & Screen Arts, you could continue your studies at Arts University Plymouth on one of the postgraduate courses listed below. Our graduates are entitled to a 15% discount on tuition fees for our MA programmes.

Through our partnership with the Royal College of Art, graduates of this course can also access application guidance and portfolio preparation for relevant RCA postgraduate programmes.
