From fashion media and fashion marketing, through to discussions exploring disruptive technology and changing consumer behaviour, this course will place you at the forefront of fashion communication.

This creative and hands-on degree is for students who aspire to work in fashion imaging, styling, social media and marketing. We encourage innovative experimentation in all areas of fashion communication and promotion.

Fran Summers and Mona Tougaard outside the Paco Rabanne show, photographed by BA (Hons) Fashion Media & Marketing student Georgia Ley. At a glance

  • Degree: BA (Hons) Fashion Media & Marketing

  • UCAS codes: 3-year degree NW52 / 4-year Integrated Foundation 7BD5

  • Typical UCAS points: 104–120

Course overview

This practice-based, multidisciplinary programme nurtures talented, self-motivated students, enabling you to strategically engage with fashion while focusing on experiential and digital futures.

Our comprehensive Fashion Media & Marketing course enables students to cultivate strong conceptual, visual and communication skills.

I feel really proud to have been part of the community at Arts University Plymouth – there have been so many talented people who have studied here, and it does feel like you’re part of a family. Penny Chan, Original Film Publicity Coordinator (Europe, Middle East, and Africa) for Netflix, Extended Diploma in Fashion & Textiles and BA (Hons) Fashion Media & Marketing graduate What you’ll learn and how you’ll study

You will explore a broad range of techniques, including photography and moving image, analytics and market research, art direction and styling, social media strategies and trend forecasting.

Strictly for the fashion curious, this course trains students to gather intelligence and insight from the cultural and economic landscape, turning it into exciting multimedia communications for print, digital and campaign design.

Poppy Stroud Developing your creative practice in fashion communication

With support from experienced industry professionals and expert technicians, students will transform contextual sources into broadcast media, observing themes such as culture and appropriation, customer behaviour and commodity and business strategies.

Whether aspiring to work in fashion media, fashion marketing, fashion promotion, styling and art direction, print journalism, visual merchandising, visual influencing or roles that have yet to be created, this course will futureproof students for success and adaptability in the ever-changing global fashion, lifestyle and beauty industries.

Why choose this course?

  • Drive innovation by exploring future fashion trends, products and their potential impact on consumers.

  • Acquire skills that are applicable across various industries, expanding your job opportunities.

  • Develop specialist knowledge and a deep understanding of the fashion industry, allowing for better targeting of potential customers and identification of new trends.

  • Produce your own fashion publications and industry reports based on the latest insights, exploring opportunities to distribute over digital and print media.

  • Learn how to study trend forecasting, develop media campaigns, plan product launches, and implement effective marketing and advertising campaigns.

Student satisfaction

BA (Hons) Fashion Media & Marketing students gave very strong feedback in the National Student Survey 2026, with 100% positive responses to 7 of the 27 individual questions. Students responded positively at 90% or above to 17 of the 27 questions.

Responding BA (Hons) Fashion Media & Marketing students gave 100% positive responses to questions including:

Teaching, assessment and feedback

“How often does your course challenge you to achieve your best work?”
“How well have assessments allowed you to demonstrate what you have learned?”
“How often have you received assessment feedback on time?”
“How often does feedback help you to improve your work?”

Student voice, support and creative freedom

“To what extent are students’ opinions about the course valued by staff?”
“How well communicated was information about your university/college’s mental wellbeing support services?”
“During your studies, how free did you feel to express your ideas, opinions, and beliefs?”

100% of BA (Hons) Fashion Media & Marketing students agreed that “the students’ opinions about the course were valued by staff. - NATIONAL STUDENT SURVEY 2023 Careers and future opportunities

Career opportunities include: Creative Directors, Art Directors, Fashion Filmmakers, Fashion Photographers, Journalists, Stylists, Content Producers, Social Media Managers, Visual Merchandisers, Trend Forecasters, Buyers, PR and Marketing Coordinators, Brand Managers and Event Managers.

Frequently asked questions What is BA (Hons) Fashion Media & Marketing about?

It places you at the forefront of fashion communication, exploring fashion media and fashion marketing alongside disruptive technology and changing consumer behaviour.

Who is this degree for?

It’s a creative and hands-on degree for students who aspire to work in fashion imaging, styling, social media and marketing, encouraging innovative experimentation in fashion communication and promotion.

What techniques will I explore on the course?

You will explore photography and moving image, analytics and market research, art direction and styling, social media strategies and trend forecasting.

How will the course help me create fashion communications for different platforms?

You’ll gather intelligence and insight from the cultural and economic landscape and turn it into exciting multimedia communications for print, digital and campaign design.

Will I be supported by industry professionals and technicians?

Yes. With support from experienced industry professionals and expert technicians, you’ll transform contextual sources into broadcast media while observing themes such as culture and appropriation, customer behaviour and commodity and business strategies.

What kinds of roles can this degree prepare me for?

It can support aspirations including fashion media, fashion marketing, fashion promotion, styling and art direction, print journalism, visual merchandising, visual influencing, and roles that have yet to be created.

How satisfied are students on the course?

100% of BA (Hons) Fashion Media & Marketing students gave the best possible response to 16 of the 27 questions in the National Student Survey 2024, and a responding student said it was “the best three years of my life”.

What careers could this degree lead to?

Career opportunities include Creative Directors, Art Directors, Fashion Filmmakers, Fashion Photographers, Journalists, Stylists, Content Producers, Social Media Managers, Visual Merchandisers, Trend Forecasters, Buyers, PR and Marketing Coordinators, Brand Managers and Event Managers.

Postgraduate progression with the Royal College of Art

Graduates of this course can access application guidance, portfolio preparation and progression planning for relevant taught postgraduate programmes at the Royal College of Art through our progression agreement.

Your undergraduate degree is taught and awarded by Arts University Plymouth. Applications to the RCA follow its normal admissions process, and applicants must meet the entry requirements for their chosen programme.

Explore the RCA progression route and scholarships for 2027/28 entry.

Integrated Foundation Year

This degree is also available as a four-year Integrated Foundation option. Our Integrated Foundation provides you with a preparatory year that will support your creative development, through a broad understanding of art, design and media skills relevant to your chosen degree subject. Learning through experimentation, exploration and discovery will support you in progressing to the next level of your degree at Arts University Plymouth.

Support while you study

All students at Arts University Plymouth can access specialist support via our Student Support Team. Our trained advisers offer information and guidance on student finance and funding, disability support, counselling and more.

Click here to read more about the support we offer.

contentBlocks.heading: Prepare for success in the fashion industry

contentBlocks.text: Fashion is an evolutionary and multifaceted industry that takes innovations in technology and culture as inspiration. From fashion media and fashion marketing, through to discussions exploring disruptive technology and changing consumer behaviour, this course will place you at the forefront of fashion communication.

contentBlocks.bodyText: This creative and hands-on degree is for students who aspire to work in fashion imaging, styling, social media and marketing. We encourage innovative experimentation in all areas of fashion communication and promotion.

image.title: Fran Summers and Mona Tougaard outside the Paco Rabanne show by BA (Hons) Fashion Media & Marketing student Georgia Ley
image.caption: Fran Summers and Mona Tougaard outside the Paco Rabanne show by BA (Hons) Fashion Media & Marketing student Georgia Ley.

contentBlocks.caption: Fran Summers and Mona Tougaard outside the Paco Rabanne show, photographed by BA (Hons) Fashion Media & Marketing student Georgia Ley.

contentBlocks.heading: At a glance
contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Degree: BA (Hons) Fashion Media & Marketing

  • UCAS codes: 3-year degree NW52 / 4-year Integrated Foundation 7BD5

  • Typical UCAS points: 104–120

This practice-based, multidisciplinary programme nurtures talented, self-motivated students, enabling you to strategically engage with fashion while focusing on experiential and digital futures.

Our comprehensive Fashion Media & Marketing course enables students to cultivate strong conceptual, visual and communication skills.

contentBlocks.blockquote: I feel really proud to have been part of the community at Arts University Plymouth – there have been so many talented people who have studied here, and it does feel like you’re part of a family.
contentBlocks.attribution: Penny Chan, Original Film Publicity Coordinator (Europe, Middle East, and Africa) for Netflix, Extended Diploma in Fashion & Textiles and BA (Hons) Fashion Media & Marketing graduate

contentBlocks.heading: What you’ll learn and how you’ll study

contentBlocks.bodyText:
You will explore a broad range of techniques, including photography and moving image, analytics and market research, art direction and styling, social media strategies and trend forecasting.

Strictly for the fashion curious, this course trains students to gather intelligence and insight from the cultural and economic landscape, turning it into exciting multimedia communications for print, digital and campaign design.

contentBlocks.caption: Poppy Stroud

contentBlocks.heading: Developing your creative practice in fashion communication

contentBlocks.bodyText:
With support from experienced industry professionals and expert technicians, students will transform contextual sources into broadcast media, observing themes such as culture and appropriation, customer behaviour and commodity and business strategies.

Whether aspiring to work in fashion media, fashion marketing, fashion promotion, styling and art direction, print journalism, visual merchandising, visual influencing or roles that have yet to be created, this course will futureproof students for success and adaptability in the ever-changing global fashion, lifestyle and beauty industries.

• Drive innovation by exploring future fashion trends, products and their potential impact on consumers.

  • Acquire skills that are applicable across various industries, expanding your job opportunities.

  • Develop specialist knowledge and a deep understanding of the fashion industry, allowing for better targeting of potential customers and identification of new trends.

  • Produce your own fashion publications and industry reports based on the latest insights, exploring opportunities to distribute over digital and print media.

  • Learn how to study trend forecasting, develop media campaigns, plan product launches, and implement effective marketing and advertising campaigns.

contentBlocks.bodyText:

Responding BA (Hons) Fashion Media & Marketing students gave 100% positive responses to questions including:

Teaching, assessment and feedback

“How often does your course challenge you to achieve your best work?”
“How well have assessments allowed you to demonstrate what you have learned?”
“How often have you received assessment feedback on time?”
“How often does feedback help you to improve your work?”

Student voice, support and creative freedom

“To what extent are students’ opinions about the course valued by staff?”
“How well communicated was information about your university/college’s mental wellbeing support services?”
“During your studies, how free did you feel to express your ideas, opinions, and beliefs?”

contentBlocks.blockquote: 100% of BA (Hons) Fashion Media & Marketing students agreed that “the students’ opinions about the course were valued by staff.
contentBlocks.attribution: - NATIONAL STUDENT SURVEY 2023

contentBlocks.bodyText: Career opportunities include: Creative Directors, Art Directors, Fashion Filmmakers, Fashion Photographers, Journalists, Stylists, Content Producers, Social Media Managers, Visual Merchandisers, Trend Forecasters, Buyers, PR and Marketing Coordinators, Brand Managers and Event Managers.

items.heading: What is BA (Hons) Fashion Media & Marketing about?
items.bodyText: It places you at the forefront of fashion communication, exploring fashion media and fashion marketing alongside disruptive technology and changing consumer behaviour.

items.heading: Who is this degree for?
items.bodyText: It’s a creative and hands-on degree for students who aspire to work in fashion imaging, styling, social media and marketing, encouraging innovative experimentation in fashion communication and promotion.

items.heading: What techniques will I explore on the course?
items.bodyText: You will explore photography and moving image, analytics and market research, art direction and styling, social media strategies and trend forecasting.

items.heading: How will the course help me create fashion communications for different platforms?
items.bodyText: You’ll gather intelligence and insight from the cultural and economic landscape and turn it into exciting multimedia communications for print, digital and campaign design.

items.heading: Will I be supported by industry professionals and technicians?
items.bodyText: Yes. With support from experienced industry professionals and expert technicians, you’ll transform contextual sources into broadcast media while observing themes such as culture and appropriation, customer behaviour and commodity and business strategies.

items.heading: What kinds of roles can this degree prepare me for?
items.bodyText: It can support aspirations including fashion media, fashion marketing, fashion promotion, styling and art direction, print journalism, visual merchandising, visual influencing, and roles that have yet to be created.

items.heading: How satisfied are students on the course?
items.bodyText: 100% of BA (Hons) Fashion Media & Marketing students gave the best possible response to 16 of the 27 questions in the National Student Survey 2024, and a responding student said it was “the best three years of my life”.

items.heading: What careers could this degree lead to?
items.bodyText: Career opportunities include Creative Directors, Art Directors, Fashion Filmmakers, Fashion Photographers, Journalists, Stylists, Content Producers, Social Media Managers, Visual Merchandisers, Trend Forecasters, Buyers, PR and Marketing Coordinators, Brand Managers and Event Managers.

contentBlocks.heading: Postgraduate progression with the Royal College of Art
contentBlocks.bodyText:
Graduates of this course can access application guidance, portfolio preparation and progression planning for relevant taught postgraduate programmes at the Royal College of Art through our progression agreement.

Your undergraduate degree is taught and awarded by Arts University Plymouth. Applications to the RCA follow its normal admissions process, and applicants must meet the entry requirements for their chosen programme.

Explore the RCA progression route and scholarships for 2027/28 entry.

contentBlocks.heading: Integrated Foundation Year
contentBlocks.bodyText: This degree is also available as a four-year Integrated Foundation option. Our Integrated Foundation provides you with a preparatory year that will support your creative development, through a broad understanding of art, design and media skills relevant to your chosen degree subject. Learning through experimentation, exploration and discovery will support you in progressing to the next level of your degree at Arts University Plymouth.

contentBlocks.heading: Support while you study
contentBlocks.bodyText:
All students at Arts University Plymouth can access specialist support via our Student Support Team. Our trained advisers offer information and guidance on student finance and funding, disability support, counselling and more.

Click here to read more about the support we offer.

contentBlocks.heading: Get in touch
contentBlocks.bodyText:

  • Instagram: @aup_fmm

contentBlocks.heading: What are my options after completing this degree?

contentBlocks.bodyText: After successful completion of BA (Hons) Fashion Media & Marketing, your progression options at Arts University Plymouth could include some of the postgraduate courses listed below. As a graduate of the university, you will be entitled to a discount of 15% on postgraduate study fees if you choose to progress onto one of our MA programmes.

We will ensure you enter industry as a well-rounded interiors specialist, ready to work on a range of projects, from super yachts to magazine photoshoots. You’ll gain a great introduction to designing interiors for a variety of environments, from residential and commercial spaces to the public realm and even transport. Find out more about BA (Hons) Interior Design & Styling at Arts University Plymouth. At a glance Degree: BA (Hons) Interior Design & Styling UCAS codes: 3-year degree 5LWB / 4-year Integrated Foundation B68G Typical UCAS points: 104–120 Designing for a range of environments You’ll design interiors for a variety of environments, from residential and commercial spaces to the public realm and even transport. Your studies place special emphasis on trends, colour, materiality, sustainability and accessibility in a range of interior contexts, both public and private. Ranked 3rd in the UK - BA (Hons) Interior Design & Styling at Arts University Plymouth came 3rd out of all UK universities offering Interior Design degrees. The Guardian University Guide 2025 Styling, materiality and making concepts real You’ll develop your own distinct taste in style curation, exploring lighting, furnishing, and surface and textural finishes to make your design concepts a reality. You’ll also develop a keen understanding of consumer trends and learn how to design for different levels of the market. Specialist modules and technical skills Specialist modules cover interior project management, materials and regulations in design, event planning and live design briefs. You’ll also develop skills including technical drawing, visualisation, editorial photography and industry-standard CAD software. Student work by Lydia Hughes Who you’ll learn from You’ll be taught by industry-active academics and specialist technicians who are responsible for some of the world’s most impressive design and styling choices in hotels, restaurants and private residences. Our team’s combined client list includes the National Trust, the BBC, Royal Caribbean Cruises and Sheraton. They have also delivered multi-million-pound commissions in New York and Barbados, and are well connected and at the forefront of their field. Why choose this course? #3 in the UK for Interior Design (The Guardian University Guide 2025). Industry-facing course with strong connections resulting in outstanding levels of progression into professional employment. We nurture you to find your own individual style and career. Vibrant focus on materiality, colour and styling as well as technical skills you’ll learn with our specialist resources in an industry-standard workspace. Student satisfaction BA (Hons) Interior Design & Styling students responded strongly in the National Student Survey 2026 to creative exploration, assessment, teaching and student voice. Responding students gave 100% positive responses to 4 of the 27 individual questions and responded positively at 90% or above to 11 of the 27 questions . It develops your skills in interior design and styling, emphasising the impact of colour, texture, materials, surface and ambience in a range of environments. What kinds of projects could I be ready for? You’ll be supported to enter industry as a well-rounded interiors specialist, ready to work on projects from super yachts to magazine photoshoots. What environments will I design for? You’ll design for environments from residential and commercial spaces to the public realm and even transport. What themes are emphasised in your studies? Your studies place special emphasis on trends, colour, materiality, sustainability and accessibility in interior contexts, both public and private. Will I develop styling and curation skills? Yes. You’ll develop your own distinct taste in style curation, exploring lighting, furnishing, surface and textural finishes to make your design concepts a reality. Does the course cover consumer trends and market levels? Yes. You’ll develop a keen understanding of consumer trends and learn how to design for different levels of the market. What specialist modules and technical skills are covered? Specialist modules cover interior project management, materials and regulations in design, event planning and live design briefs, and you’ll develop skills including technical drawing, visualisation, editorial photography and industry-standard CAD software. Who will I learn from on the course? You’ll be taught by industry-active academics and specialist technicians whose combined client list includes the National Trust, the BBC, Royal Caribbean Cruises and Sheraton, and who have delivered multi-million-pound commissions in New York and Barbados. Why choose this course?

  • #3 in the UK for Interior Design (The Guardian University Guide 2025).

  • Industry-facing course with strong connections resulting in outstanding levels of progression into professional employment.

  • We nurture you to find your own individual style and career.

  • Vibrant focus on materiality, colour and styling as well as technical skills you’ll learn with our specialist resources in an industry-standard workspace.

Student satisfaction

BA (Hons) Interior Design & Styling students responded strongly in the National Student Survey 2026 to creative exploration, assessment, teaching and student voice. Responding students gave 100% positive responses to 4 of the 27 individual questions and responded positively at 90% or above to 11 of the 27 questions.

Interior Design & Styling students gave 100% positive responses to the questions:

“To what extent have you had the chance to explore ideas and concepts in depth?”
“How fair has the marking and assessment been on your course?”
“How well have assessments allowed you to demonstrate what you have learned?”
“How well communicated was information about your university/college’s mental wellbeing support services?”

Students also responded positively at 94% to the questions “How good are teaching staff at explaining things?”, “How often do teaching staff make the subject engaging?”, “How often does your course challenge you to achieve your best work?” and “To what extent are students’ opinions about the course valued by staff?”

Careers and future opportunities

Career opportunities include:

  • Interior & Spatial Designers
  • Interior Stylists
  • Art Directors
  • Set Designers
  • Exhibition Designers
  • Product Stylists
  • Trend Forecasters
  • Retail Buyers
  • Merchandisers
  • Magazine Stylists
  • 3D Designers
  • Visualisers
  • Freelance Artists and Designers
Frequently asked questions What is BA (Hons) Interior Design & Styling focused on?

It develops your skills in interior design and styling, emphasising the impact of colour, texture, materials, surface and ambience in a range of environments.

What kinds of projects could I be ready for?

You’ll be supported to enter industry as a well-rounded interiors specialist, ready to work on projects from super yachts to magazine photoshoots.

What environments will I design for?

You’ll design for environments from residential and commercial spaces to the public realm and even transport.

What themes are emphasised in your studies?

Your studies place special emphasis on trends, colour, materiality, sustainability and accessibility in interior contexts, both public and private.

Will I develop styling and curation skills?

Yes. You’ll develop your own distinct taste in style curation, exploring lighting, furnishing, surface and textural finishes to make your design concepts a reality.

Does the course cover consumer trends and market levels?

Yes. You’ll develop a keen understanding of consumer trends and learn how to design for different levels of the market.

What specialist modules and technical skills are covered?

Specialist modules cover interior project management, materials and regulations in design, event planning and live design briefs, and you’ll develop skills including technical drawing, visualisation, editorial photography and industry-standard CAD software.

Who will I learn from on the course?

You’ll be taught by industry-active academics and specialist technicians whose combined client list includes the National Trust, the BBC, Royal Caribbean Cruises and Sheraton, and who have delivered multi-million-pound commissions in New York and Barbados.

I am from Wales and did some scouring before I chose which university to go to. Arts University Plymouth’s facilities and opportunities looked amazing and after having my interview and talking to Course Leader Cathryn Bishop it confirmed my decision as the correct one. I have had the most amazing three years at Arts University Plymouth and wouldn’t change anything about it. The staff are so supportive. BA (Hons) Interior Design & Styling student Caitlin Evans Postgraduate progression with the Royal College of Art

Graduates of this course can access application guidance, portfolio preparation and progression planning for relevant taught postgraduate programmes at the Royal College of Art through our progression agreement.

Your undergraduate degree is taught and awarded by Arts University Plymouth. Applications to the RCA follow its normal admissions process, and applicants must meet the entry requirements for their chosen programme.

Explore the RCA progression route and scholarships for 2027/28 entry.

Integrated Foundation Year

This degree is also available as a four-year Integrated Foundation option. Our Integrated Foundation provides you with a preparatory year that will support your creative development, through a broad understanding of art, design and media skills relevant to your chosen degree subject. Learning through experimentation, exploration and discovery will support you in progressing to the next level of your degree at Arts University Plymouth.

Support while you study

All students at Arts University Plymouth can access specialist support via our Student Support Team. Our trained advisers offer information and guidance on student finance and funding, disability support, counselling and more.

Click here to read more about the support we offer.

Get in touch
  • Email: interior@aup.ac.uk
  • Instagram: @aup_interiors
What are my options after completing this degree?

After graduating from BA (Hons) Film & Screen Arts, you could continue your studies at Arts University Plymouth on one of the postgraduate courses listed below. Our graduates are entitled to a 15% discount on tuition fees for our MA programmes.

Through our partnership with the Royal College of Art, graduates of this course can also access application guidance and portfolio preparation for relevant RCA postgraduate programmes.

MA Design (Built Environment) Use methods of co-design and practice-led research to transform the spaces people inhabit for increased wellbeing, social agency and sense of place. MA Design Develop products, practices and applications for contemporary society and imagine design beyond the status quo of production and consumption. MA Immersive Media Translate your creative knowledge and digital skills into engaging immersive content and public media experiences for diverse audiences in this exciting and rapidly growing sector. MA Design (Communication) Explore how current social, critical and technological paradigms are changing how designers create and distribute narrative-driven artefacts and campaigns. contentBlocks.heading: Prepare for success in interior design and styling

contentBlocks.text: This course has been devised to develop your skills in interior design and styling, emphasising the impact of colour, texture, materials, surface and ambience in a range of environments. We will ensure you enter industry as a well-rounded interiors specialist, ready to work on a range of projects, from super yachts to magazine photoshoots.

contentBlocks.bodyText: You’ll gain a great introduction to designing interiors for a variety of environments, from residential and commercial spaces to the public realm and even transport.

contentBlocks.caption: Find out more about BA (Hons) Interior Design & Styling at Arts University Plymouth.

contentBlocks.heading: At a glance
contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Degree: BA (Hons) Interior Design & Styling
  • UCAS codes: 3-year degree 5LWB / 4-year Integrated Foundation B68G
  • Typical UCAS points: 104–120

contentBlocks.heading: Designing for a range of environments

contentBlocks.bodyText:
You’ll design interiors for a variety of environments, from residential and commercial spaces to the public realm and even transport.

Your studies place special emphasis on trends, colour, materiality, sustainability and accessibility in a range of interior contexts, both public and private.

contentBlocks.blockquote: Ranked 3rd in the UK - BA (Hons) Interior Design & Styling at Arts University Plymouth came 3rd out of all UK universities offering Interior Design degrees.
contentBlocks.attribution: The Guardian University Guide 2025

contentBlocks.heading: Styling, materiality and making concepts real

contentBlocks.bodyText:
You’ll develop your own distinct taste in style curation, exploring lighting, furnishing, and surface and textural finishes to make your design concepts a reality.

You’ll also develop a keen understanding of consumer trends and learn how to design for different levels of the market.

Specialist modules cover interior project management, materials and regulations in design, event planning and live design briefs.

You’ll also develop skills including technical drawing, visualisation, editorial photography and industry-standard CAD software.

contentBlocks.caption: Student work by Lydia Hughes

contentBlocks.bodyText:
You’ll be taught by industry-active academics and specialist technicians who are responsible for some of the world’s most impressive design and styling choices in hotels, restaurants and private residences.

Our team’s combined client list includes the National Trust, the BBC, Royal Caribbean Cruises and Sheraton.

They have also delivered multi-million-pound commissions in New York and Barbados, and are well connected and at the forefront of their field.

• #3 in the UK for Interior Design (The Guardian University Guide 2025).

  • Industry-facing course with strong connections resulting in outstanding levels of progression into professional employment.

  • We nurture you to find your own individual style and career.

  • Vibrant focus on materiality, colour and styling as well as technical skills you’ll learn with our specialist resources in an industry-standard workspace.

Our comprehensive curriculum equips you with the skills and knowledge essential for influencing change within the fashion industry. With a focus on creativity, innovation, and practical application, our program prepares you for a rewarding career in fashion design. At a glance Degree: BA (Hons) Fashion Design UCAS codes: 3-year degree W290 / 4-year Integrated Foundation W234 Typical UCAS points: 104–120 Why choose this fashion design degree at Arts University Plymouth? Our philosophy is to develop students as independently-minded fashion thinkers and skilled makers who can confidently challenge the conventions of a rapidly changing fashion industry. An innovative curriculum supported by an actively engaged and diverse team of tutors and professionals. Pro Entrepreneurship with well established local, national & international industry links , creating a broad range of opportunities for students with embedded business training and live opportunities. I am impressed by the flexibility and encouragement that the Fashion programme offers students to explore their personal creativity. It is a real strength that students are empowered to explore the varied specialities within fashion design, without being limited. It allows them to make decisions, grow in confidence and understand their own opinion and taste level, learning to adapt to different markets and customers – a vital skill set in industry. Becky French, Accessories Designer, Marwood Fashion students debut their final collections at our annual Graduate Shows. Unlock your creative potential in fashion design At Arts University Plymouth, we foster a culture of independence within our vibrant fashion program. We empower aspiring fashion thinkers, makers, and designers to embrace their creative journey and carve their path in the ever-evolving fashion landscape. By seamlessly blending traditional craft techniques with cutting-edge digital technologies, you'll transcend your ideas from mere concepts to tangible, three-dimensional creations. Our curriculum encourages innovation and individualism, preparing you for success in the dynamic world of fashion. Join us as we redefine design, take creative risks, and communicate your unique style through your craft. Explore our fashion studio and beyond Step into our expansive Fashion Studio, bathed in natural light and offering breathtaking panoramic views. Equipped with cutting-edge industry-standard technologies, this space serves as your creative sanctuary. But your journey at Arts University Plymouth extends far beyond the confines of our Fashion Studio. Embrace a culture of cross-disciplinary collaboration, where you'll hone your skills in our professional textile print studios, jewellery and ceramics workshops, and our innovative Fab Lab. Here, you'll have access to the latest in laser cutting, 3D printing, and design technology, expanding your horizons and unleashing your creativity to its fullest potential. Develop your unique style You'll have the freedom to refine your signature aesthetic without the constraints of a predefined house style. Our comprehensive program covers every facet of the design process, including trend analysis, research, design development, drawing, and illustration. Dive into the realms of colour and fabric development, and immerse yourself in historical and cultural studies that inform your creative vision. From translating ideas from 2D to 3D to mastering the art of presentation and marketing, our curriculum prepares you for every aspect of the industry. Embrace the business side of fashion as you delve into business development, equipping yourself with the skills needed to thrive in the competitive fashion landscape. Student work by Molly Adlington. Access cutting-edge facilities At Arts University Plymouth, you'll have access to cutting-edge facilities and invaluable industry partnerships. Utilise global trend forecasting tools like WGSN and The Future Laboratory, and master software such as Adobe Creative Suite and Gerber Accumark for CAD pattern cutting. Our curriculum covers every aspect of the design process, from future forecasting to concept and design development, and from creative pattern cutting to the leadership of compelling marketing campaigns. Fashion is one of the largest employers in the UK’s creative industries, offering boundless opportunities for forward-thinking individuals. At our university, you'll be encouraged to challenge assumptions, take creative risks, and communicate your individual style through your work. Whether you're interested in menswear, womenswear, lingerie, knitwear, performance, sportswear, or other technical routes, we provide the tools and support for you to realise your ideas and develop specialised skills. Gain real-world experience and fashion industry exposure Acquire a comprehensive understanding of sustainable design and ethical manufacturing, gaining insight into every step of the commercial supply chain. Develop entrepreneurial skills through collaborative projects and live briefs, becoming industry-ready for the competitive fashion landscape. Engage with expert industry speakers and collaborate with renowned brands like Finisterre and Hiut Denim to enhance your market awareness, project management, and communication skills. Explore the factors influencing design, development, and production while participating in industry events worldwide, including London, Paris, New York, and Berlin. Showcase your work at prestigious events like Graduate Fashion Week and leverage our extensive professional network to secure placements with leading fashion houses like Alexander McQueen, Vivienne Westwood, and more. Learning through experimentation, exploration and discovery will support you in progressing to the next level of your degree at Arts University Plymouth. contentBlocks.heading: Prepare for success in the fashion industry

contentBlocks.text: Join our dynamic BA (Hons) Fashion Design program, tailored to nurture independently-minded fashion thinkers and makers poised to lead change in the industry. Our comprehensive curriculum equips you with the skills and knowledge essential for influencing change within the fashion industry. With a focus on creativity, innovation, and practical application, our program prepares you for a rewarding career in fashion design.

contentBlocks.heading: At a glance
contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Degree: BA (Hons) Fashion Design

  • UCAS codes: 3-year degree W290 / 4-year Integrated Foundation W234

  • Typical UCAS points: 104–120

contentBlocks.heading: Why choose this fashion design degree at Arts University Plymouth?

contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Our philosophy is to develop students as independently-minded fashion thinkers and skilled makers who can confidently challenge the conventions of a rapidly changing fashion industry.

  • An innovative curriculum supported by an actively engaged and diverse team of tutors and professionals.

  • Pro Entrepreneurship with well established local, national & international industry links, creating a broad range of opportunities for students with embedded business training and live opportunities.

contentBlocks.blockquote: I am impressed by the flexibility and encouragement that the Fashion programme offers students to explore their personal creativity. It is a real strength that students are empowered to explore the varied specialities within fashion design, without being limited. It allows them to make decisions, grow in confidence and understand their own opinion and taste level, learning to adapt to different markets and customers – a vital skill set in industry.
contentBlocks.attribution: Becky French, Accessories Designer, Marwood

contentBlocks.heading: Unlock your creative potential in fashion design

contentBlocks.bodyText: At Arts University Plymouth, we foster a culture of independence within our vibrant fashion program. We empower aspiring fashion thinkers, makers, and designers to embrace their creative journey and carve their path in the ever-evolving fashion landscape. By seamlessly blending traditional craft techniques with cutting-edge digital technologies, you'll transcend your ideas from mere concepts to tangible, three-dimensional creations. Our curriculum encourages innovation and individualism, preparing you for success in the dynamic world of fashion. Join us as we redefine design, take creative risks, and communicate your unique style through your craft.

contentBlocks.heading: Explore our fashion studio and beyond

contentBlocks.bodyText: Step into our expansive Fashion Studio, bathed in natural light and offering breathtaking panoramic views. Equipped with cutting-edge industry-standard technologies, this space serves as your creative sanctuary. But your journey at Arts University Plymouth extends far beyond the confines of our Fashion Studio. Embrace a culture of cross-disciplinary collaboration, where you'll hone your skills in our professional textile print studios, jewellery and ceramics workshops, and our innovative Fab Lab. Here, you'll have access to the latest in laser cutting, 3D printing, and design technology, expanding your horizons and unleashing your creativity to its fullest potential.

You'll have the freedom to refine your signature aesthetic without the constraints of a predefined house style. Our comprehensive program covers every facet of the design process, including trend analysis, research, design development, drawing, and illustration. Dive into the realms of colour and fabric development, and immerse yourself in historical and cultural studies that inform your creative vision.

From translating ideas from 2D to 3D to mastering the art of presentation and marketing, our curriculum prepares you for every aspect of the industry. Embrace the business side of fashion as you delve into business development, equipping yourself with the skills needed to thrive in the competitive fashion landscape.

image.title: Work by Molly Adlington BA Hons Fashion Design

contentBlocks.caption: Student work by Molly Adlington.

contentBlocks.bodyText:
At Arts University Plymouth, you'll have access to cutting-edge facilities and invaluable industry partnerships. Utilise global trend forecasting tools like WGSN and The Future Laboratory, and master software such as Adobe Creative Suite and Gerber Accumark for CAD pattern cutting. Our curriculum covers every aspect of the design process, from future forecasting to concept and design development, and from creative pattern cutting to the leadership of compelling marketing campaigns.

Fashion is one of the largest employers in the UK’s creative industries, offering boundless opportunities for forward-thinking individuals. At our university, you'll be encouraged to challenge assumptions, take creative risks, and communicate your individual style through your work. Whether you're interested in menswear, womenswear, lingerie, knitwear, performance, sportswear, or other technical routes, we provide the tools and support for you to realise your ideas and develop specialised skills.

contentBlocks.heading: Gain real-world experience and fashion industry exposure

contentBlocks.bodyText:
Acquire a comprehensive understanding of sustainable design and ethical manufacturing, gaining insight into every step of the commercial supply chain. Develop entrepreneurial skills through collaborative projects and live briefs, becoming industry-ready for the competitive fashion landscape.

Engage with expert industry speakers and collaborate with renowned brands like Finisterre and Hiut Denim to enhance your market awareness, project management, and communication skills. Explore the factors influencing design, development, and production while participating in industry events worldwide, including London, Paris, New York, and Berlin. Showcase your work at prestigious events like Graduate Fashion Week and leverage our extensive professional network to secure placements with leading fashion houses like Alexander McQueen, Vivienne Westwood, and more.
Phoebe English, Mend Assembly, Davy J Swimwear, Mae’s Luxury Manufacturing, WGSN, Real Ideas, Studio PL1, Peclers Paris Trend Forecasting, FACE

contentBlocks.bodyText:
BA (Hons) Fashion Design students gave particularly positive feedback on assessment questions in the National Student Survey (NSS) 2026.

In the NSS 2026, 92.3% of responding students answered positively to the question “How fair has the marking and assessment been on your course?” and 92.3% answered positively to “How well have assessments allowed you to demonstrate what you have learned?”

Students also responded positively at 84.6% to questions including “To what extent have you had the chance to explore ideas and concepts in depth?”, “To what extent have you had the chance to bring together information and ideas from different topics?” and “How well has your course developed your knowledge and skills that you think you will need for your future?”

contentBlocks.heading: Postgraduate progression with the Royal College of Art
contentBlocks.bodyText:
Graduates of this course can access application guidance, portfolio preparation and progression planning for relevant taught postgraduate programmes at the Royal College of Art through our progression agreement.

Your undergraduate degree is taught and awarded by Arts University Plymouth. Applications to the RCA follow its normal admissions process, and applicants must meet the entry requirements for their chosen programme.

Explore the RCA progression route and scholarships for 2027/28 entry.

contentBlocks.heading: Integrated Foundation Year
contentBlocks.bodyText: This degree is also available as a four-year Integrated Foundation option. Our Integrated Foundation provides you with a preparatory year that will support your creative development, through a broad understanding of art, design and media skills relevant to your chosen degree subject. Learning through experimentation, exploration and discovery will support you in progressing to the next level of your degree at Arts University Plymouth.

contentBlocks.heading: Support while you study
contentBlocks.bodyText:
All students at Arts University Plymouth can access specialist support via our Student Support Team. Our trained advisers offer information and guidance on student finance and funding, disability support, counselling and more.

Click here to read more about the support we offer.

contentBlocks.bodyText:
Email: fashion@aup.ac.uk

Instagram: @aup_bafashiondesign

contentBlocks.heading: What are my options after completing this degree?

contentBlocks.bodyText:
After graduating from BA (Hons) Film & Screen Arts, you could continue your studies at Arts University Plymouth on one of the postgraduate courses listed below. Our graduates are entitled to a 15% discount on tuition fees for our MA programmes.

Through our partnership with the Royal College of Art, graduates of this course can also access application guidance and portfolio preparation for relevant RCA postgraduate programmes.

Alongside the teaching of other content linked to entertainment designs, integrated studies and the humanities and arts, you will develop a comprehensive and sustainable approach for creating dynamic and engaging games and animations. At a glance Degree: BA (Hons) Game Arts & Animation UCAS codes: 3-year degree W61M / 4-year Integrated Foundation W618 Typical UCAS points: 104–120 Course overview The objective of the course is to prepare each student to join a studio, having observed and practised the numerous phases required in the production of game design and animated features, including: Writing Concept art Storyboarding Art direction Animation Editing Arts University Plymouth gave me the opportunity to spend my days studying art, improving my skills, and honing my thinking for the creative industries. I was surrounded by extremely inspiring people, and being able to bounce concepts around and share skills was an essential part of my learning. I soon came to realise that being an artist really is a viable career path. - Leon Tyler, Creative Director for award-winning global EdTech company Macademia and former BAFTA juror | BA (Hons) Animation graduate What you’ll learn and how you’ll study During the first year, a significant part of the course is devoted to fundamental drawing practice, such as anatomy, characters, posing and animation. Following on from this, your skills will be developed further through working with the digital tools that are widely used within the industries. As a student you will focus on concept art and visual development towards outputs such as characters, worldbuilding and asset creation. Choose your specialism in year two During your second year you will be able to select either a games or animation career development specialism. Game arts path: prepares students to create and communicate visual concepts through 3D and 2D prototyping, iteration and production. Animation path: develops students in the disciplines of character animation, storyboarding, modelling, art direction and the principles of 2D and 3D lighting. Student work by Nathan Hardy Why choose this course? Industry-ready expertise: graduates emerge with expertise in storytelling, prototyping and problem-solving, perfectly primed for fulfilling roles in the dynamic and demanding entertainment industry. Real Ideas partnership: opportunities to develop and screen 360-degree content in Europe’s first-of-its-kind immersive dome, compatible with VR, AR, mixed reality, games and animation software. Specialised career paths: choose between game arts and animation, tailoring your education to your entertainment-sector career goals. Unreal Academic Partner recognition for BA (Hons) Game Arts & Animation Recognised as an Unreal Academic Partner BA (Hons) Game Arts & Animation at Arts University Plymouth has been recognised as an Unreal Academic Partner by Epic Games. The recognition reflects a course where students build strong visual foundations in drawing, concept art and worldbuilding, then develop digital production skills using tools such as Unreal Engine, Autodesk's 3D studio max and Maya, ZBrush and Substance Painter. On the game arts pathway, you will apply those skills to environments, blockouts and game-ready assets, preparing for contemporary practice across games and animation. Unreal Academic Partner badge used under licence from Epic Games. Arts University Plymouth is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Epic Games. Real Ideas' immersive dome at Market Hall in Plymouth is the first of its type in Europe. Student satisfaction BA (Hons) Game Arts & Animation students responded especially positively in the National Student Survey 2026 to assessment, academic support, IT resources and freedom of expression. Students responded positively at 90% or above to 9 of the 27 individual questions . Students responded particularly strongly to questions including: 97% for “How fair has the marking and assessment been on your course?” 97% for “How often have you received assessment feedback on time?” 97% for “During your studies, how free did you feel to express your ideas, opinions, and beliefs?” 97% for “How well have the IT resources and facilities supported your learning?” 94% for “How good are teaching staff at explaining things?” 94% for “To what extent does your course have the right balance of directed and independent study?” 94% for “How well have teaching staff supported your learning?” Careers and future opportunities Career opportunities include: 2D Texture Artists, 3D CGI Animators, 3D Modellers, Print Artists (stop-motion production), Animators, Art Directors, Character Designers, Compositors, Concept Artists, Illustrators, Set and Prop Designers and Storyboard Artists. Frequently asked questions What is BA (Hons) Game Arts & Animation designed to prepare me for? It prepares you for today’s highly competitive market and the rapidly expanding entertainment and media industry, which is forecast to reach $3.5 trillion globally by 2029. What is the objective of the course? The objective is to prepare each student to join a studio, having observed and practised the numerous phases required in the production of game design and animated features. Which production phases will I observe and practise? You will observe and practise phases including writing, concept art, storyboarding, art direction, animation and editing. What will I focus on in the first year? In the first year, a significant part of the course is devoted to fundamental drawing practice, such as anatomy, characters, posing and animation. Will I develop digital skills as well as drawing? Yes. Following the drawing foundations, your skills will be developed further through working with the digital tools that are widely used within the industries. What kinds of outputs will I develop? You will focus on concept art and visual development towards outputs such as characters, worldbuilding and asset creation. Can I specialise in games or animation? Yes. During your second year you will be able to select either a games or animation career development specialism. What is the difference between the game arts and animation paths? The game arts path prepares students to create and communicate visual concepts through 3D and 2D prototyping, iteration and production, while the animation path develops students in character animation, storyboarding, modelling, art direction and the principles of 2D and 3D lighting. How satisfied are students on the course? In NSS 2025, students recorded 94% positive responses to “Teaching staff are good at explaining things” and 97% positive responses to “I have the right IT resources for my studies”, and the course achieved 94% positive responses in the academic support theme.   • Real Ideas partnership: opportunities to develop and screen 360-degree content in Europe’s first-of-its-kind immersive dome, compatible with VR, AR, mixed reality, games and animation software.

  • Specialised career paths: choose between game arts and animation, tailoring your education to your entertainment-sector career goals.

Unreal Academic Partner recognition for BA (Hons) Game Arts & Animation Recognised as an Unreal Academic Partner

BA (Hons) Game Arts & Animation at Arts University Plymouth has been recognised as an Unreal Academic Partner by Epic Games. The recognition reflects a course where students build strong visual foundations in drawing, concept art and worldbuilding, then develop digital production skills using tools such as Unreal Engine, Autodesk's 3D studio max and Maya, ZBrush and Substance Painter. On the game arts pathway, you will apply those skills to environments, blockouts and game-ready assets, preparing for contemporary practice across games and animation.

Unreal Academic Partner badge used under licence from Epic Games. Arts University Plymouth is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Epic Games.

Real Ideas' immersive dome at Market Hall in Plymouth is the first of its type in Europe. Student satisfaction

BA (Hons) Game Arts & Animation students responded especially positively in the National Student Survey 2026 to assessment, academic support, IT resources and freedom of expression. Students responded positively at 90% or above to 9 of the 27 individual questions.

Students responded particularly strongly to questions including:

97% for “How fair has the marking and assessment been on your course?”
97% for “How often have you received assessment feedback on time?”
97% for “During your studies, how free did you feel to express your ideas, opinions, and beliefs?”
97% for “How well have the IT resources and facilities supported your learning?”
94% for “How good are teaching staff at explaining things?”
94% for “To what extent does your course have the right balance of directed and independent study?”
94% for “How well have teaching staff supported your learning?”

Careers and future opportunities

Career opportunities include: 2D Texture Artists, 3D CGI Animators, 3D Modellers, Print Artists (stop-motion production), Animators, Art Directors, Character Designers, Compositors, Concept Artists, Illustrators, Set and Prop Designers and Storyboard Artists.

Frequently asked questions What is BA (Hons) Game Arts & Animation designed to prepare me for?

It prepares you for today’s highly competitive market and the rapidly expanding entertainment and media industry, which is forecast to reach $3.5 trillion globally by 2029.

What is the objective of the course?

The objective is to prepare each student to join a studio, having observed and practised the numerous phases required in the production of game design and animated features.

Which production phases will I observe and practise?

You will observe and practise phases including writing, concept art, storyboarding, art direction, animation and editing.

What will I focus on in the first year?

In the first year, a significant part of the course is devoted to fundamental drawing practice, such as anatomy, characters, posing and animation.

Will I develop digital skills as well as drawing?

Yes. Following the drawing foundations, your skills will be developed further through working with the digital tools that are widely used within the industries.

What kinds of outputs will I develop?

You will focus on concept art and visual development towards outputs such as characters, worldbuilding and asset creation.

Can I specialise in games or animation?

Yes. During your second year you will be able to select either a games or animation career development specialism.

What is the difference between the game arts and animation paths?

The game arts path prepares students to create and communicate visual concepts through 3D and 2D prototyping, iteration and production, while the animation path develops students in character animation, storyboarding, modelling, art direction and the principles of 2D and 3D lighting.

How satisfied are students on the course?

In NSS 2025, students recorded 94% positive responses to “Teaching staff are good at explaining things” and 97% positive responses to “I have the right IT resources for my studies”, and the course achieved 94% positive responses in the academic support theme.

Postgraduate progression with the Royal College of Art

Graduates of this course can access application guidance, portfolio preparation and progression planning for relevant taught postgraduate programmes at the Royal College of Art through our progression agreement.

Your undergraduate degree is taught and awarded by Arts University Plymouth. Applications to the RCA follow its normal admissions process, and applicants must meet the entry requirements for their chosen programme.

Explore the RCA progression route and scholarships for 2027/28 entry.

Integrated Foundation Year

This degree is also available as a four-year Integrated Foundation option. Our Integrated Foundation provides you with a preparatory year that will support your creative development, through a broad understanding of art, design and media skills relevant to your chosen degree subject. Learning through experimentation, exploration and discovery will support you in progressing to the next level of your degree at Arts University Plymouth.

Support while you study

All students at Arts University Plymouth can access specialist support via our Student Support Team. Our trained advisers offer information and guidance on student finance and funding, disability support, counselling and more.

Click here to read more about the support we offer.

Get in touch
  • Email: admissions@aup.ac.uk
  • Instagram: @animation_gameart_aup

After graduating from BA (Hons) Film & Screen Arts, you could continue your studies at Arts University Plymouth on one of the postgraduate courses listed below. Our graduates are entitled to a 15% discount on tuition fees for our MA programmes.

Through our partnership with the Royal College of Art, graduates of this course can also access application guidance and portfolio preparation for relevant RCA postgraduate programmes.

contentBlocks.heading: Prepare for success in the game arts and animation industries

contentBlocks.text: Our BA (Hons) Game Arts & Animation degree prepares you for today’s highly competitive market and rapidly expanding entertainment and media industry, which is forecast to reach $3.5 trillion globally by 2029.

contentBlocks.bodyText: Through storytelling, prototyping and problem-solving, you will develop projects and lead in interdisciplinary contexts, gaining knowledge that will be valuable whether you work for a multinational organisation or a small studio. Alongside the teaching of other content linked to entertainment designs, integrated studies and the humanities and arts, you will develop a comprehensive and sustainable approach for creating dynamic and engaging games and animations.

contentBlocks.caption: Find out more about BA (Hons) Game Arts & Animation at Arts University Plymouth.

contentBlocks.heading: At a glance
contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Degree: BA (Hons) Game Arts & Animation

  • UCAS codes: 3-year degree W61M / 4-year Integrated Foundation W618

  • Typical UCAS points: 104–120

The objective of the course is to prepare each student to join a studio, having observed and practised the numerous phases required in the production of game design and animated features, including:

  • Writing
  • Concept art
  • Storyboarding
  • Art direction
  • Animation
  • Editing

contentBlocks.blockquote: Arts University Plymouth gave me the opportunity to spend my days studying art, improving my skills, and honing my thinking for the creative industries. I was surrounded by extremely inspiring people, and being able to bounce concepts around and share skills was an essential part of my learning. I soon came to realise that being an artist really is a viable career path.

Find out more about BA (Hons) Photography at Arts University Plymouth. At a glance

  • Degree: BA (Hons) Photography

  • UCAS codes: 3-year degree W645 / 4-year Integrated Foundation W600

  • Typical UCAS points: 104–120

What you’ll learn and how you’ll study

You will develop your practical and creative skills in studio and location practice, covering image production, lighting, styling, creative direction, retouching and post-production.

You’ll master a wide range of techniques and technologies to produce innovative photographic and multimedia content, supported by industry-standard equipment and resources.

Students access high quality resources – including a darkroom, photographic cove, studios, a digital darkroom, the Digital Print Bureau, and a range of industry-standard kit, all free to hire. From being an un-confident student, my time at Arts University Plymouth has moulded me into a bold and powerful artist and human! Presenting in front of the class for three years improved my fear of public speaking. The tutors were always supportive and encouraged me to experiment and to think outside of the box. Rose Mary, BA (Hons) Photography 2020 and MA Photography 2024 graduate Storytelling, identity and culture

You’ll be encouraged to develop your own distinctive visual practice while investigating photography’s role in storytelling, identity and culture.

From editorial advocacy, concerned with how image-making can respond to debates around social justice and climate change, to fashion, advertising and commercial production, you’ll learn how images can inform, inspire and connect with audiences.

Informed by research and engagement with contemporary thinking, your studies will include the exploration of historical and cultural contexts, enabling you to become an ethically aware and critically informed practitioner.

Women's football team, by Lucy Arscott, BA (Hons) Photography 2025 Industry readiness, live briefs and placements

Industry readiness is a core theme of our curriculum. Throughout the course you’ll have opportunities to meet industry professionals and present your work.

You’ll be supported to undertake industry placements with photographers, creative agencies, brands, publishers and cultural organisations.

You’ll work on live briefs, developing your professional skills and confidence in responding to commissions, while cultivating transferable skills to succeed in the workplace.

Students exhibit their work at our annual Graduate Shows. Why choose this course?

  • Explore diverse practices including fashion, editorial, advocacy, heritage and culture, and commercial production.

  • Access our Equipment Resource Centre, with specialist photography, film and lighting equipment, and industry-standard photographic studios.

  • Experiment with a wide range of traditional, digital and emerging technologies.

  • Learn from experienced industry professionals, academics and technical tutors.

  • Acquire a breadth of practical, creative and professional skills to enable you to succeed in the creative industries.

  • Participate in our Photography Festival and symposium events, with exhibitions, talks, workshops, portfolio reviews and panel discussions.

Photo by Evaliina Vuorma, BA (Hons) Photography 2025 Student satisfaction

BA (Hons) Photography received particularly strong feedback in the National Student Survey (NSS) 2026, with responding students giving 100% positive responses to 18 of the 27 individual questions. Students responded positively at 90% or above to 25 of the 27 questions.

Photography also received 100% positive responses to both questions in the NSS scale ‘Academic support’: “How easy was it to contact teaching staff when you needed to?” and “How well have teaching staff supported your learning?”

Responding BA (Hons) Photography students gave 100% positive responses to questions including:

Teaching and creative challenge

“How good are teaching staff at explaining things?”
“How often do teaching staff make the subject engaging?”
“How often does your course challenge you to achieve your best work?”

Learning opportunities

“To what extent have you had the chance to explore ideas and concepts in depth?”
“To what extent does your course have the right balance of directed and independent study?”
“How well has your course developed your knowledge and skills that you think you will need for your future?”

Assessment, feedback and support

“How clear were the marking criteria used to assess your work?”
“How well have assessments allowed you to demonstrate what you have learned?”
“How often have you received assessment feedback on time?”
“How easy was it to contact teaching staff when you needed to?”
“How well have teaching staff supported your learning?”

Resources, student voice and freedom of expression

“How well were any changes to teaching on your course communicated?”
“How well have the IT resources and facilities supported your learning?”
“How easy is it to access subject specific resources (e.g., equipment, facilities, software) when you need them?”
“To what extent do you get the right opportunities to give feedback on your course?”
“To what extent are students’ opinions about the course valued by staff?”
“How well communicated was information about your university/college’s mental wellbeing support services?”
“During your studies, how free did you feel to express your ideas, opinions, and beliefs?”

It specialises in the creative and professional possibilities of lens-based image-making in the creative industries.

What areas of contemporary photography will I explore?

You’ll explore contemporary photography with a focus on fashion, editorial, heritage and culture, and commercial production.

What practical skills will I develop in studio and on location?

You will develop skills in studio and location practice covering image production, lighting, styling, creative direction, retouching and post-production.

Will I explore emerging technologies such as AI?

Yes. You’ll explore how emerging technologies such as AI are shaping the future of photography and the creative industries.

How does the course support ethical and critically informed practice?

Your studies include historical and cultural contexts, supporting you to become an ethically aware and critically informed practitioner.

What industry experience will I gain?

You’ll meet industry professionals, present your work, undertake industry placements, and work on live briefs to develop confidence in responding to commissions.

What facilities will I have access to?

You’ll have access to the Equipment Resource Centre with specialist photography, film and lighting equipment, and industry-standard photographic studios.

What are Photography Festival and symposium events?

They include exhibitions, talks, workshops, portfolio reviews and panel discussions.

What careers could this degree lead to?

Career opportunities include Photographers, Photographic Assistants, Creative Directors, Creative Producers, Digital Operators, Filmmakers, Museum/Archive Photographers, Content Creators and Curators.
