contentBlocks.text: BA (Hons) Photography specialises in the creative and professional possibilities of lens-based image-making in the creative industries. You’ll explore contemporary photography with a focus on fashion, editorial, heritage and culture, and commercial production.

contentBlocks.bodyText: Through our distinctive curriculum, using industry-standard equipment and resources, you’ll master a wide range of techniques and technologies to produce innovative photographic and multimedia content. You’ll also explore how emerging technologies such as AI are shaping the future of photography and the creative industries.

contentBlocks.caption: Find out more about BA (Hons) Photography at Arts University Plymouth.

contentBlocks.heading: At a glance
contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Degree: BA (Hons) Photography

  • UCAS codes: 3-year degree W645 / 4-year Integrated Foundation W600

  • Typical UCAS points: 104–120

contentBlocks.heading: What you’ll learn and how you’ll study

contentBlocks.bodyText:
You will develop your practical and creative skills in studio and location practice, covering image production, lighting, styling, creative direction, retouching and post-production.

You’ll master a wide range of techniques and technologies to produce innovative photographic and multimedia content, supported by industry-standard equipment and resources.

contentBlocks.caption: Students access high quality resources – including a darkroom, photographic cove, studios, a digital darkroom, the Digital Print Bureau, and a range of industry-standard kit, all free to hire.

contentBlocks.blockquote: From being an un-confident student, my time at Arts University Plymouth has moulded me into a bold and powerful artist and human! Presenting in front of the class for three years improved my fear of public speaking. The tutors were always supportive and encouraged me to experiment and to think outside of the box.
contentBlocks.attribution: Rose Mary, BA (Hons) Photography 2020 and MA Photography 2024 graduate

contentBlocks.bodyText:
You’ll be encouraged to develop your own distinctive visual practice while investigating photography’s role in storytelling, identity and culture.

From editorial advocacy, concerned with how image-making can respond to debates around social justice and climate change, to fashion, advertising and commercial production, you’ll learn how images can inform, inspire and connect with audiences.

Informed by research and engagement with contemporary thinking, your studies will include the exploration of historical and cultural contexts, enabling you to become an ethically aware and critically informed practitioner.

image.title: Photo of womens football team by Lucy Arscott BA Hons Photography graduate 2025

contentBlocks.caption: Women's football team, by Lucy Arscott, BA (Hons) Photography 2025

contentBlocks.heading: Industry readiness, live briefs and placements

contentBlocks.bodyText:
Industry readiness is a core theme of our curriculum. Throughout the course you’ll have opportunities to meet industry professionals and present your work.

You’ll be supported to undertake industry placements with photographers, creative agencies, brands, publishers and cultural organisations.

You’ll work on live briefs, developing your professional skills and confidence in responding to commissions, while cultivating transferable skills to succeed in the workplace.

contentBlocks.caption: Students exhibit their work at our annual Graduate Shows.

contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Explore diverse practices including fashion, editorial, advocacy, heritage and culture, and commercial production.

  • Access our Equipment Resource Centre, with specialist photography, film and lighting equipment, and industry-standard photographic studios.

  • Experiment with a wide range of traditional, digital and emerging technologies.

  • Learn from experienced industry professionals, academics and technical tutors.

  • Acquire a breadth of practical, creative and professional skills to enable you to succeed in the creative industries.

  • Participate in our Photography Festival and symposium events, with exhibitions, talks, workshops, portfolio reviews and panel discussions.

image.title: Photo by BA Hons Photography 2025 graduate Eveliina Vuorma

contentBlocks.caption: Photo by Evaliina Vuorma, BA (Hons) Photography 2025

contentBlocks.bodyText:
BA (Hons) Photography received particularly strong feedback in the National Student Survey (NSS) 2026, with responding students giving 100% positive responses to 18 of the 27 individual questions. Students responded positively at 90% or above to 25 of the 27 questions.

Photography also received 100% positive responses to both questions in the NSS scale ‘Academic support’: “How easy was it to contact teaching staff when you needed to?” and “How well have teaching staff supported your learning?”

Responding BA (Hons) Photography students gave 100% positive responses to questions including:

Teaching and creative challenge

“How good are teaching staff at explaining things?”
“How often do teaching staff make the subject engaging?”
“How often does your course challenge you to achieve your best work?”

Learning opportunities

“To what extent have you had the chance to explore ideas and concepts in depth?”
“To what extent does your course have the right balance of directed and independent study?”
“How well has your course developed your knowledge and skills that you think you will need for your future?”

Assessment, feedback and support

“How clear were the marking criteria used to assess your work?”
“How well have assessments allowed you to demonstrate what you have learned?”
“How often have you received assessment feedback on time?”
“How easy was it to contact teaching staff when you needed to?”
“How well have teaching staff supported your learning?”

Resources, student voice and freedom of expression

“How well were any changes to teaching on your course communicated?”
“How well have the IT resources and facilities supported your learning?”
“How easy is it to access subject specific resources (e.g., equipment, facilities, software) when you need them?”
“To what extent do you get the right opportunities to give feedback on your course?”
“To what extent are students’ opinions about the course valued by staff?”
“How well communicated was information about your university/college’s mental wellbeing support services?”
“During your studies, how free did you feel to express your ideas, opinions, and beliefs?”

items.heading: What does BA (Hons) Photography specialise in?
items.bodyText: It specialises in the creative and professional possibilities of lens-based image-making in the creative industries.

items.heading: What areas of contemporary photography will I explore?
items.bodyText: You’ll explore contemporary photography with a focus on fashion, editorial, heritage and culture, and commercial production.

items.heading: What practical skills will I develop in studio and on location?
items.bodyText: You will develop skills in studio and location practice covering image production, lighting, styling, creative direction, retouching and post-production.

items.heading: Will I explore emerging technologies such as AI?
items.bodyText: Yes. You’ll explore how emerging technologies such as AI are shaping the future of photography and the creative industries.

items.heading: How does the course support ethical and critically informed practice?
items.bodyText: Your studies include historical and cultural contexts, supporting you to become an ethically aware and critically informed practitioner.

items.heading: What industry experience will I gain?
items.bodyText: You’ll meet industry professionals, present your work, undertake industry placements, and work on live briefs to develop confidence in responding to commissions.

items.heading: What facilities will I have access to?
items.bodyText: You’ll have access to the Equipment Resource Centre with specialist photography, film and lighting equipment, and industry-standard photographic studios.

items.heading: What are Photography Festival and symposium events?
items.bodyText: They include exhibitions, talks, workshops, portfolio reviews and panel discussions.

items.heading: What careers could this degree lead to?
items.bodyText: Career opportunities include Photographers, Photographic Assistants, Creative Directors, Creative Producers, Digital Operators, Filmmakers, Museum/Archive Photographers, Content Creators and Curators.

contentBlocks.heading: Postgraduate progression with the Royal College of Art
contentBlocks.bodyText:
Graduates of this course can access application guidance, portfolio preparation and progression planning for relevant taught postgraduate programmes at the Royal College of Art through our progression agreement.

Your undergraduate degree is taught and awarded by Arts University Plymouth. Applications to the RCA follow its normal admissions process, and applicants must meet the entry requirements for their chosen programme.

Explore the RCA progression route and scholarships for 2027/28 entry.

contentBlocks.heading: Integrated Foundation Year
contentBlocks.bodyText: This degree is also available as a four-year Integrated Foundation option. Our Integrated Foundation provides you with a preparatory year that will support your creative development, through a broad understanding of art, design and media skills relevant to your chosen degree subject. Learning through experimentation, exploration and discovery will support you in progressing to the next level of your degree at Arts University Plymouth.

contentBlocks.heading: Support while you study
contentBlocks.bodyText:
All students at Arts University Plymouth can access specialist support via our Student Support Team. Our trained advisers offer information and guidance on student finance and funding, disability support, counselling and more.

Click here to read more about the support we offer.

contentBlocks.heading: Get in touch
contentBlocks.bodyText:
Email: admissions@aup.ac.uk

Instagram: @aup_photo

contentBlocks.heading: What are my options after completing this degree?

contentBlocks.bodyText:
After graduating from BA (Hons) Film & Screen Arts, you could continue your studies at Arts University Plymouth on one of the postgraduate courses listed below. Our graduates are entitled to a 15% discount on tuition fees for our MA programmes.

Through our partnership with the Royal College of Art, graduates of this course can also access application guidance and portfolio preparation for relevant RCA postgraduate programmes.

Working from classic and contemporary texts, music and storytelling, you’ll become skilled at producing bespoke costumes for a range of performance genres, whether for stage, screen or live-action events. Throughout the course, our dedicated Workshop Labs provide extensive resources and support from expert technicians, helping you explore skills including pattern cutting, tailoring, corsetry, costume props, and print and dyeing techniques. At a glance Degree: BA (Hons) Costume Production UCAS codes: 3-year degree PW34 / 4-year Integrated Foundation W451 UCAS points: 104–120 Course overview Our BA (Hons) Costume Production course offers a fresh approach to the study of design, realisation and construction for costume. Working from classic and contemporary texts, music and storytelling, you’ll produce bespoke costumes for a range of performance genres, whether for stage, screen or live-action events. Sophie Prings costume in action for 'The Actors Wheels' production of Faustus | Photo credit: Claire Tregaskis Workshop Labs and technical skills Throughout this course, our dedicated Workshop Labs will provide you with extensive resources, alongside support and guidance from expert technicians, allowing you to explore skills such as: Pattern cutting Tailoring Corsetry Costume props Print and dying techniques The things I loved best at university were the live briefs and outside collaborations. In my first year, I created a Victorian dress to go on display for the National Trust as part of a costume exhibition in Castle Drogo. We also worked on a theatre production with another local university, making and altering costumes backstage for the productions King Lear and Clockwork Orange, which taught me so much. Megan Proctor Live projects and professional practice You will work on live projects with professional designers and performers, providing essential experience of industry practices. This may take the form of heritage, stage or film work. Costume Production students have access to a wide range of facilities. Who you’ll learn from Your learning will be guided by a dedicated team of creative professionals who have worked for theatre and TV companies, including Netflix, the Royal Shakespeare Company, and West End productions. You will also gain valuable insight from visiting professionals such as Paul Farnsworth (Lend Me a Tenor), Lucinda Wright (The Witcher) and Michelle Carragher (Game of Thrones), as well as a close relationship with Theatre Royal Plymouth. Costume for screen, stage and heritage In TV and film, our students have contributed to Netflix’s Bridgerton series and the BBC’s EastEnders. They have also worked behind the scenes of smash-hit touring productions of Strictly Come Dancing, Matthew Bourne’s Sleeping Beauty, Wicked and The Lion King. This course encompasses cultural, social and political contexts for costume, enabling you to create costumes for public exhibitions and commissions from heritage societies, such as the National Trust and The Box, Plymouth. The Actors Wheel production of Faustus. Photo credit: Claire Tregaskis Student satisfaction In the National Student Survey (NSS) 2026, 94% of responding students answered positively to the question “How well have assessments allowed you to demonstrate what you have learned?” and 94% answered positively to “How often have you received assessment feedback on time?” Students also responded positively at 88% to “How often does your course challenge you to achieve your best work?” and “To what extent have you had the chance to explore ideas and concepts in depth?” Marie has such a passion for what she does, and the diversity of the modules provided so many opportunities to learn so many different skills to find what we really loved within our discipline. Zoe Brooks Why choose this course? Learn technical skills and acquire specialist knowledge of costume design and construction techniques used in the profession. Collaborate with other students across the university including Film & Screen Arts. Have opportunities to enter competitions, such as World of Wearable Art (New Zealand), and The Costume Society’s Patterns of Fashion Award. Gain a deep understanding of sustainable practices for both costume design and making. Benefit from opportunities to design and produce costumes for real clients in outward-facing projects. Frequently asked questions What is BA (Hons) Costume Production focused on? It offers a fresh approach to the study of design, realisation and construction for costume, producing bespoke costumes for stage, screen and live-action events. What will I work from when developing costume ideas? You’ll work from classic and contemporary texts, music and storytelling. What facilities and support will I have access to? You’ll work in dedicated Workshop Labs with extensive resources, supported by expert technicians. What technical skills will I explore? You’ll explore skills including pattern cutting, tailoring, corsetry, costume props, and print and dying techniques. Will I work on live projects? Yes. You will work on live projects with professional designers and performers, gaining essential experience of industry practices through heritage, stage or film work. Who will teach me on the course? Your learning is guided by a dedicated team of creative professionals with experience in theatre and TV companies including Netflix, the Royal Shakespeare Company, and West End productions. You’ll gain insight from visiting professionals including Paul Farnsworth (Lend Me a Tenor), Lucinda Wright (The Witcher) and Michelle Carragher (Game of Thrones), and benefit from a close relationship with Theatre Royal Plymouth. Does the course cover wider contexts for costume? Yes. The course encompasses cultural, social and political contexts for costume, including creating costumes for public exhibitions and commissions from heritage societies such as the National Trust and The Box, Plymouth. How satisfied are students on the course? 100% of BA (Hons) Costume Production students responded positively to the NSS 2025 questions “How often do teaching staff make the subject engaging?” and “How often does your course challenge you to achieve your best work?”. What career paths could this degree support? Career opportunities include Prop Makers, Costume Interpreters, Designers, Costume Assistants (Film & TV), Stylists, Buyers, Costume Supervisors, Theatrical Milliners and Heritage Professional. You will work on live projects with professional designers and performers, providing essential experience of industry practices. This may take the form of heritage, stage or film work.

Costume Production students have access to a wide range of facilities. Who you’ll learn from

Your learning will be guided by a dedicated team of creative professionals who have worked for theatre and TV companies, including Netflix, the Royal Shakespeare Company, and West End productions.

You will also gain valuable insight from visiting professionals such as Paul Farnsworth (Lend Me a Tenor), Lucinda Wright (The Witcher) and Michelle Carragher (Game of Thrones), as well as a close relationship with Theatre Royal Plymouth.

Costume for screen, stage and heritage

In TV and film, our students have contributed to Netflix’s Bridgerton series and the BBC’s EastEnders. They have also worked behind the scenes of smash-hit touring productions of Strictly Come Dancing, Matthew Bourne’s Sleeping Beauty, Wicked and The Lion King.

This course encompasses cultural, social and political contexts for costume, enabling you to create costumes for public exhibitions and commissions from heritage societies, such as the National Trust and The Box, Plymouth.

The Actors Wheel production of Faustus. Photo credit: Claire Tregaskis Student satisfaction

In the National Student Survey (NSS) 2026, 94% of responding students answered positively to the question “How well have assessments allowed you to demonstrate what you have learned?” and 94% answered positively to “How often have you received assessment feedback on time?”

Students also responded positively at 88% to “How often does your course challenge you to achieve your best work?” and “To what extent have you had the chance to explore ideas and concepts in depth?”

Marie has such a passion for what she does, and the diversity of the modules provided so many opportunities to learn so many different skills to find what we really loved within our discipline. Zoe Brooks Why choose this course?

  • Learn technical skills and acquire specialist knowledge of costume design and construction techniques used in the profession.

  • Collaborate with other students across the university including Film & Screen Arts.

  • Have opportunities to enter competitions, such as World of Wearable Art (New Zealand), and The Costume Society’s Patterns of Fashion Award.

  • Gain a deep understanding of sustainable practices for both costume design and making.

  • Benefit from opportunities to design and produce costumes for real clients in outward-facing projects.

Frequently asked questions What is BA (Hons) Costume Production focused on?

It offers a fresh approach to the study of design, realisation and construction for costume, producing bespoke costumes for stage, screen and live-action events.

What will I work from when developing costume ideas?

You’ll work from classic and contemporary texts, music and storytelling.

What facilities and support will I have access to?

You’ll work in dedicated Workshop Labs with extensive resources, supported by expert technicians.

What technical skills will I explore?

You’ll explore skills including pattern cutting, tailoring, corsetry, costume props, and print and dying techniques.

Will I work on live projects?

Yes. You will work on live projects with professional designers and performers, gaining essential experience of industry practices through heritage, stage or film work.

Who will teach me on the course?

Your learning is guided by a dedicated team of creative professionals with experience in theatre and TV companies including Netflix, the Royal Shakespeare Company, and West End productions.

Will I learn from visiting professionals and industry connections?

Yes. You’ll gain insight from visiting professionals including Paul Farnsworth (Lend Me a Tenor), Lucinda Wright (The Witcher) and Michelle Carragher (Game of Thrones), and benefit from a close relationship with Theatre Royal Plymouth.

What kinds of professional productions have students contributed to?

Students have contributed to Netflix’s Bridgerton series and the BBC’s EastEnders, and worked behind the scenes on touring productions including Strictly Come Dancing, Matthew Bourne’s Sleeping Beauty, Wicked and The Lion King.

Does the course cover wider contexts for costume?

Yes. The course encompasses cultural, social and political contexts for costume, including creating costumes for public exhibitions and commissions from heritage societies such as the National Trust and The Box, Plymouth.

How satisfied are students on the course?

100% of BA (Hons) Costume Production students responded positively to the NSS 2025 questions “How often do teaching staff make the subject engaging?” and “How often does your course challenge you to achieve your best work?”.

What career paths could this degree support?

Career opportunities include Prop Makers, Costume Interpreters, Designers, Costume Assistants (Film & TV), Stylists, Buyers, Costume Supervisors, Theatrical Milliners and Heritage Professional.

Postgraduate progression with the Royal College of Art

Our agreement with the Royal College of Art supports graduates from 13 Arts University Plymouth undergraduate courses who are considering relevant RCA postgraduate programmes.

The route provides application guidance, portfolio preparation and progression planning. Undergraduate degrees are taught and awarded by Arts University Plymouth, and admission to the RCA remains subject to its entry requirements.

Explore the eligible courses and RCA progression route, including scholarships for 2027/28 entry.

Integrated Foundation Year

This degree is also available as a four-year Integrated Foundation option. Our Integrated Foundation provides you with a preparatory year that will support your creative development, through a broad understanding of art, design and media skills relevant to your chosen degree subject. Learning through experimentation, exploration and discovery will support you in progressing to the next level of your degree at Arts University Plymouth.

Support while you study

All students at Arts University Plymouth can access specialist support via our Student Support Team. Our trained advisers offer information and guidance on student finance and funding, disability support, counselling and more.

Click here to read more about the support we offer.

Get in touch
  • Email: costume@aup.ac.uk
  • Instagram: @aup_costume
What are my options after completing this degree?

After graduating from BA (Hons) Film & Screen Arts, you could continue your studies at Arts University Plymouth on one of the postgraduate courses listed below. Our graduates are entitled to a 15% discount on tuition fees for our MA programmes.

Through our partnership with the Royal College of Art, graduates of this course can also access application guidance and portfolio preparation for relevant RCA postgraduate programmes.

MA Design (Fashion) Reimagine fashion design using research-led, practical exploration of materials, processes and technologies to propose new strategies for the industry. MA Design (Built Environment) Use methods of co-design and practice-led research to transform the spaces people inhabit for increased wellbeing, social agency and sense of place. MA Design Develop products, practices and applications for contemporary society and imagine design beyond the status quo of production and consumption. MA Design (Textiles) Immerse yourself in the research, application and production of textiles within the fashion design, interior design and craft industries. items.bodyText: Career opportunities include Prop Makers, Costume Interpreters, Designers, Costume Assistants (Film & TV), Stylists, Buyers, Costume Supervisors, Theatrical Milliners and Heritage Professional.

contentBlocks.heading: Postgraduate progression with the Royal College of Art
contentBlocks.bodyText:
Our agreement with the Royal College of Art supports graduates from 13 Arts University Plymouth undergraduate courses who are considering relevant RCA postgraduate programmes.

The route provides application guidance, portfolio preparation and progression planning. Undergraduate degrees are taught and awarded by Arts University Plymouth, and admission to the RCA remains subject to its entry requirements.

Explore the eligible courses and RCA progression route, including scholarships for 2027/28 entry.

contentBlocks.heading: Integrated Foundation Year
contentBlocks.bodyText: This degree is also available as a four-year Integrated Foundation option. Our Integrated Foundation provides you with a preparatory year that will support your creative development, through a broad understanding of art, design and media skills relevant to your chosen degree subject. Learning through experimentation, exploration and discovery will support you in progressing to the next level of your degree at Arts University Plymouth.

contentBlocks.heading: Support while you study
contentBlocks.bodyText:
All students at Arts University Plymouth can access specialist support via our Student Support Team. Our trained advisers offer information and guidance on student finance and funding, disability support, counselling and more.

Click here to read more about the support we offer.

contentBlocks.heading: Get in touch
contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Email: costume@aup.ac.uk
  • Instagram: @aup_costume

contentBlocks.heading: What are my options after completing this degree?

contentBlocks.bodyText:
After graduating from BA (Hons) Film & Screen Arts, you could continue your studies at Arts University Plymouth on one of the postgraduate courses listed below. Our graduates are entitled to a 15% discount on tuition fees for our MA programmes.

Through our partnership with the Royal College of Art, graduates of this course can also access application guidance and portfolio preparation for relevant RCA postgraduate programmes.

contentBlocks.heading: Craft meets technology, tradition, and design

contentBlocks.text:
Discover the beauty and versatility of ceramics and glass through a year of hands-on exploration. This course celebrates the material qualities of clay and glass, encouraging you to design through making while developing essential technical skills and creative confidence.

You’ll experiment with both functional and decorative forms, learning to transform raw materials into unique creative outcomes. Working within our nationally recognised Materials Lab, you’ll engage with both industrial and studio-based processes, gaining the foundations needed for a sustainable and expressive career as a designer/maker.

contentBlocks.heading: At a glance
contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Award: CertHE Ceramics & Glass

  • Course length and level: 1-year Level 4 course

  • UCAS code: G67W

  • UCAS points: 72–120

This course provides a comprehensive introduction to both ceramics and glass, allowing you to specialise or work across both disciplines.

You’ll experiment with both functional and decorative forms, learning to transform raw materials into unique creative outcomes as you develop technical skills and creative confidence.

image.title: A woman in blue dungarees makes a ceramic pot on a pottery wheel, she's located in our ceramics studio with fellow ceramicists also throwing pots on wheels next to her.

contentBlocks.bodyText: In ceramics, you’ll explore handbuilding techniques and production methods including mould-making, wheel-throwing and slip-casting.
In glass, you’ll gain experience in glassblowing, kiln-formed glass, coldworking and lampworking.

image.title: Finishing a piece of glass in the cold working area of the glass workshops at arts university plymouth

contentBlocks.heading: Combining traditional craft with digital tools

contentBlocks.bodyText:
You’ll be encouraged to combine traditional processes with new technologies, using digital tools in our Fab Lab South West to prototype and create moulds through CNC milling, laser cutting and 3D printing.

Learning is student-centred, shifting from lecturer-led briefs to self-initiated projects that reflect your developing interests.

As part of your professional development, you’ll learn how to communicate your creative ideas to different audiences, curate and present your work for exhibitions and fairs, and develop a personal creative identity and entrepreneurial mindset.

By the end of the course, you’ll have the technical skills, confidence and professional understanding to take your next steps in higher study or industry, joining a growing global network of makers and material innovators.

You’ll learn from experienced tutors and practising artists who are active in the fields of ceramics and glass, and be supported by our expert technical team and a programme of visiting lecturers.

The course sits within a wider community of designer/makers rooted in workshop culture, where collaboration, experimentation and material understanding come together.

Our teaching is informed by strong connections with industry and contemporary craft practice. You’ll be encouraged to exhibit your work, take part in craft fairs and engage with international forums and competitions to build your professional profile.

You’ll also benefit from our award-winning facilities, including Fab Lab South West, ceramics and hot glass studios, and open-access workshops, all part of one of the top 5 universities in the UK for creative facilities (Whatuni Student Choice Awards 2025).

Throughout your studies, you’ll develop entrepreneurial skills to help you market your work globally, understand creative audiences and contexts, and prepare for life as an independent designer/maker.

images.title: A handmade ceramic mug made by a student at arts university plymouth
Equipment in the glass studios at arts university plymouth
View of the cold finishing area in the glass workshops at arts university plymouth

contentBlocks.bodyText:
On completion, you can progress directly onto BA (Hons) Craft & Material Practices at Level 5, or apply to join Workroom Grow, our business incubator, designed to help graduates launch sustainable creative enterprises.

Career opportunities include:

  • Designer/Makers

  • Ceramicists

  • Glass Artists

  • Wearables Designers

  • Sculptors

  • Architectural Surface Designers

  • Mixed Media Artists

  • Fine Artists

  • Gallery and Museum Professionals

  • Teachers

  • Technicians

  • Material Restoration Technicians and Conservators

  • Prop Designers

items.heading: What will I explore on CertHE Ceramics & Glass?
items.bodyText: You’ll discover the beauty and versatility of ceramics and glass through a year of hands-on exploration, celebrating the material qualities of clay and glass and learning to design through making.

items.heading: Will I make both functional and decorative work?
items.bodyText: Yes. You’ll experiment with both functional and decorative forms, learning to transform raw materials into unique creative outcomes.

items.heading: Where will I study on the course?
items.bodyText: You’ll work within our nationally recognised Materials Lab, engaging with both industrial and studio-based processes.

items.heading: What ceramics techniques will I learn?
items.bodyText: In ceramics, you’ll explore handbuilding techniques and production methods including mould-making, wheel-throwing and slip-casting.

items.heading: What glass techniques will I learn?
items.bodyText: In glass, you’ll gain experience in glassblowing, kiln-formed glass, coldworking and lampworking.

items.heading: Will I use digital tools alongside traditional processes?
items.bodyText: Yes. You’ll be encouraged to combine traditional processes with new technologies, using digital tools in our Fab Lab South West to prototype and create moulds through CNC milling, laser cutting and 3D printing.

items.heading: How will learning be structured?
items.bodyText: Learning is student-centred, shifting from lecturer-led briefs to self-initiated projects that reflect your developing interests.

items.heading: How will the course support my professional development?
items.bodyText: You’ll learn how to communicate your creative ideas to different audiences, curate and present your work for exhibitions and fairs, and develop a personal creative identity and entrepreneurial mindset.

items.heading: Who will I learn from?
items.bodyText: You’ll learn from experienced tutors and practising artists, supported by an expert technical team and a programme of visiting lecturers.

items.heading: Will I have opportunities to exhibit and build my profile?
items.bodyText: Yes. You’ll be encouraged to exhibit your work, take part in craft fairs and engage with international forums and competitions to build your professional profile.

items.heading: What facilities will I have access to?
items.bodyText: You’ll benefit from award-winning facilities including Fab Lab South West, ceramics and hot glass studios, and open-access workshops, within one of the top 5 universities in the UK for creative facilities (Whatuni Student Choice Awards 2025).

items.heading: What can I do after completing the course?
items.bodyText: On completion, you can progress directly onto BA (Hons) Craft & Material Practices at Level 5, or apply to join Workroom Grow, our business incubator designed to help graduates launch sustainable creative enterprises.

contentBlocks.heading: Launch your career in business with a creative edge.

contentBlocks.text:
This one-year course is designed for students who want to combine business knowledge with creative thinking, developing the skills needed to succeed in today’s fast changing world of work.

With a focus on employability and enterprise, you will build skills in business thinking, creative problem solving and collaborative team working, while developing your understanding of social and ethical responsibility. In a world where technology and artificial intelligence are reshaping business practice, this blend of academic study and applied learning ensures you graduate ready to progress into employment, self-employed business or further study.

contentBlocks.heading: At a glance
contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Award: CertHE Business & Management for Creatives

  • Course length and level: 1-year Level 4 course

  • UCAS code: BY67

  • UCAS points: 72–120

The course draws on the skills identified by the Future Skills League Table as the most essential for the future, including problem-solving, critical thinking, communication, digital literacy, adaptability, resilience, creativity, teamwork and initiative.

image.title: Students at a networking event for Ignite Festival Launch photo by Sarah Packer

contentBlocks.bodyText: Students will gain a strong grounding in the principles of business and management, while applying this knowledge through live projects with local and national businesses, benefitting from citywide partnerships with cultural and enterprise organisations.

Our curriculum is continually informed by industry engagement and wider global developments in business education, including digital transformation, sustainability, entrepreneurship and internationalisation.

You will have access to sector insights and employability resources through our institutional membership of Creative UK, as well as expert talks and workshops delivered by industry professionals including Micronomy, Digital Remit, Maverick and PB Media.

contentBlocks.heading: A flexible foundation for your next steps

contentBlocks.bodyText: Whether you are aiming to launch your own creative business, enhance your management skills for industry, or continue your studies, our CertHE Business & Management for Creatives course offers a flexible and future-focused foundation.

• Learn the core principles of business and management with a creative focus, and gain skills in problem-solving, teamwork, communication and digital productivity.

  • Blend academic study with live industry projects, while building the skills to progress to employment, self-employment or further study.

  • Develop future-ready skills in creativity, adaptability and resilience, and learn how to think critically, analyse and evaluate complex challenges, and develop practical solutions that connect theory to real-world contexts.

  • Gain an understanding of social and ethical responsibility.

image.title: A female student speaks to guests about her work at London Design Fair 2018

contentBlocks.bodyText: Career opportunities: Graduate ready for entry-level business and management roles, build entrepreneurial skills to launch your own creative business, or progress to a full BA (Hons) degree.

items.heading: Who is this course designed for?
items.bodyText: This one-year course is designed for students who want to combine business knowledge with creative thinking, developing the skills needed to succeed in today’s fast changing world of work.

items.heading: Will I apply what I learn to real projects?

items.heading: How does the course support employability and enterprise?
items.bodyText: With a focus on employability and enterprise, you will build skills in business thinking, creative problem solving and collaborative team working, while developing your understanding of social and ethical responsibility.

items.heading: How does the course reflect changes in business, including AI?
items.bodyText: In a world where technology and artificial intelligence are reshaping business practice, the course blends academic study and applied learning to help ensure you graduate ready to progress into employment, self-employed business or further study.

items.heading: What themes inform the curriculum?
items.bodyText: The curriculum is informed by industry engagement and wider global developments in business education, including digital transformation, sustainability, entrepreneurship and internationalisation.

items.heading: What industry insight and professional input will I have access to?
items.bodyText: You will have access to sector insights and employability resources through our institutional membership of Creative UK, as well as expert talks and workshops delivered by industry professionals including Micronomy, Digital Remit, Maverick and PB Media.

items.heading: What can I do after completing this course?
items.bodyText: You can graduate ready for entry-level business and management roles, build entrepreneurial skills to launch your own creative business, or progress to a full BA (Hons) degree.

The Integrated Foundation will provide you with a preparatory year that will support your creative development, through a broad understanding of art, design and media skills relevant to your chosen degree subject. Learning through experimentation, exploration and discovery to support you in progressing to the next level of your degree at Arts University Plymouth. *This course was previously titled Extended BA. This course has been renamed in line with the university's ongoing commitment to offer courses that accurately reflect the needs of students. At a glance Route: Integrated Foundation (Year 1 of a 4-year degree) Availability: All 3-year undergraduate degrees are offered as a 4-year Integrated Foundation (see course page for UCAS code) UCAS code: See individual course page UCAS points: 104–120 A preparatory year The Integrated Foundation will provide you with a preparatory year that will support your creative development, through a broad understanding of art, design and media skills relevant to your chosen degree subject. The environment is dynamic and supportive, helping you discover your own particular passions and strengths within the creative arts, while building academic confidence, purpose and direction During this year, you will produce a body of work that will start to reveal your personal identity and approach to your chosen programme of study. I started the course wanting to be an artist. I left the course as an artist. This has been the most amazing formative year of my creative journey so far, I wish I had done it sooner. Joanne Nudd, BA (Hons) Textile Design with Integrated Foundation (previously Extended BA) graduate How you’ll learn Our Integrated Foundation year is intensive and challenging, taught through lectures, workshops and practical studio sessions, seminars and tutorials. You will have the freedom to take creative risks, generate ideas, experiment and develop a breadth of approaches to problem-solving. You will experiment with materials, processes, methodologies and practices. The time I spent on the [Integrated Foundation Year] is time that I wish I could repeat again and again. To say that the year was transformative is a considerable understatement. I came onto the course feeling slightly imposter-like and I left the course an artist, excited for my future. Michele Azzopardi, BA (Hons) Craft & Material Practices with Integrated Foundation (previously Extended BA) graduate Skills you’ll build for degree-level study You’ll develop a range of critical skills relevant to degree-level study, while broadening your use of drawing, visual research, contextual studies, digital imaging and art and design methods. This year primes you to become a confident, independent and creative artist, designer or maker, setting you on the path to excel in higher-level degree studies. Who the Integrated Foundation is for The course attracts a diverse age range, from school leavers to creative and experienced mature individuals. Some are returning to education after a break, while others are looking for a career change. Why choose this route? Immerse yourself in experimental and intense learning experiences that open up new avenues of exploration and discovery. This is done through research, making practical work, lively discussion and self-reflection. You will embark on a challenging, creative, academic and practical journey giving you the freedom to take risks, generate ideas and experiment with a variety of analogue and digital methods and materials. A transformative and exploratory year that increases knowledge, curiosity and confidence and is fantastic preparation for the following three years of degree-level study. “This course is an excellent chance to experiment with everything the university has to offer. The support from staff and use of the facilities helped me to determine the direction in which I wanted to take my career, as well as giving me a broad knowledge of art across a wide range of practices.” Taylor Harford, BA (Hons) Commercial Photography with Integrated Foundation (previously Extended BA) graduate Student work by Max Wilson Frequently asked questions What is an Integrated Foundation Year? It’s a four-year undergraduate degree course that includes a preparatory year supporting your creative development through a broad range of art, design and media skills, as the basis for continued study in your chosen specialist subject. Who is the Integrated Foundation for? It is for students who may be returning to education after a break or perhaps without formal qualifications to gain the necessary skills, knowledge and experience to succeed on an undergraduate course. Do all undergraduate degrees offer an Integrated Foundation option? Yes. All 3-year undergraduate degrees are offered as a 4-year Integrated Foundation, and you should see the individual course page for the UCAS code. What will I do in the first year? You’ll develop a broad understanding of art, design and media skills and approaches, and produce a body of work that starts to reveal your personal identity and approach to your chosen programme of study. How will I be taught? The Integrated Foundation Year is intensive and challenging, taught through lectures, workshops and practical studio sessions, seminars and tutorials. What skills will I build for degree-level study? You’ll develop critical skills relevant to degree-level study while broadening your use of drawing, visual research, contextual studies, digital imaging and art and design methods. Will I progress automatically to my chosen degree? Yes. Successfully completing the Integrated Foundation year allows automatic progression to your chosen degree at Arts University Plymouth. Students exhibit their work in their annual end of year show. Student Satisfaction Every single person you rub shoulders with is a creative, whether it's students, staff, housekeeping, front of house, everyone is here for one reason and one reason only, to make Arts University Plymouth a family community where you can truly be yourself, find your artistic voice, and become the artist that you had only dreamed about before. Arts University Plymouth genuinely makes dreams come true, it has for me! contentBlocks.heading: Prepare for Success with an Integrated Foundation*

contentBlocks.text:
Our four-year Integrated Foundation Degrees allow students who may be returning to education after a break or perhaps without formal qualifications to gain the necessary skills, knowledge and experience to succeed on an undergraduate course.

The Integrated Foundation will provide you with a preparatory year that will support your creative development, through a broad understanding of art, design and media skills relevant to your chosen degree subject. Learning through experimentation, exploration and discovery to support you in progressing to the next level of your degree at Arts University Plymouth.

contentBlocks.bodyText: *This course was previously titled Extended BA. This course has been renamed in line with the university's ongoing commitment to offer courses that accurately reflect the needs of students.

contentBlocks.heading: At a glance
contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Route: Integrated Foundation (Year 1 of a 4-year degree)

  • Availability: All 3-year undergraduate degrees are offered as a 4-year Integrated Foundation (see course page for UCAS code)

  • UCAS code: See individual course page

  • UCAS points: 104–120

The Integrated Foundation will provide you with a preparatory year that will support your creative development, through a broad understanding of art, design and media skills relevant to your chosen degree subject. The environment is dynamic and supportive, helping you discover your own particular passions and strengths within the creative arts, while building academic confidence, purpose and direction

During this year, you will produce a body of work that will start to reveal your personal identity and approach to your chosen programme of study.

contentBlocks.blockquote: I started the course wanting to be an artist. I left the course as an artist. This has been the most amazing formative year of my creative journey so far, I wish I had done it sooner.
contentBlocks.attribution: Joanne Nudd, BA (Hons) Textile Design with Integrated Foundation (previously Extended BA) graduate

contentBlocks.bodyText:
Our Integrated Foundation year is intensive and challenging, taught through lectures, workshops and practical studio sessions, seminars and tutorials.

You will have the freedom to take creative risks, generate ideas, experiment and develop a breadth of approaches to problem-solving. You will experiment with materials, processes, methodologies and practices.

image.title: A girl in a yellow top sits at a desk working on an art sculpture built from multicoloured strings.

contentBlocks.blockquote: The time I spent on the [Integrated Foundation Year] is time that I wish I could repeat again and again. To say that the year was transformative is a considerable understatement. I came onto the course feeling slightly imposter-like and I left the course an artist, excited for my future.
contentBlocks.attribution: Michele Azzopardi, BA (Hons) Craft & Material Practices with Integrated Foundation (previously Extended BA) graduate

contentBlocks.heading: Skills you’ll build for degree-level study

contentBlocks.bodyText:
You’ll develop a range of critical skills relevant to degree-level study, while broadening your use of drawing, visual research, contextual studies, digital imaging and art and design methods.

This year primes you to become a confident, independent and creative artist, designer or maker, setting you on the path to excel in higher-level degree studies.

contentBlocks.heading: Who the Integrated Foundation is for

contentBlocks.bodyText: The course attracts a diverse age range, from school leavers to creative and experienced mature individuals. Some are returning to education after a break, while others are looking for a career change.

Immerse yourself in experimental and intense learning experiences that open up new avenues of exploration and discovery. This is done through research, making practical work, lively discussion and self-reflection.

You will embark on a challenging, creative, academic and practical journey giving you the freedom to take risks, generate ideas and experiment with a variety of analogue and digital methods and materials.

A transformative and exploratory year that increases knowledge, curiosity and confidence and is fantastic preparation for the following three years of degree-level study.

contentBlocks.blockquote: “This course is an excellent chance to experiment with everything the university has to offer. The support from staff and use of the facilities helped me to determine the direction in which I wanted to take my career, as well as giving me a broad knowledge of art across a wide range of practices.”
contentBlocks.attribution: Taylor Harford, BA (Hons) Commercial Photography with Integrated Foundation (previously Extended BA) graduate

contentBlocks.caption: Student work by Max Wilson

items.heading: What is an Integrated Foundation Year?
items.bodyText: It’s a four-year undergraduate degree course that includes a preparatory year supporting your creative development through a broad range of art, design and media skills, as the basis for continued study in your chosen specialist subject.

items.heading: Who is the Integrated Foundation for?
items.bodyText: It is for students who may be returning to education after a break or perhaps without formal qualifications to gain the necessary skills, knowledge and experience to succeed on an undergraduate course.

items.heading: Do all undergraduate degrees offer an Integrated Foundation option?
items.bodyText: Yes. All 3-year undergraduate degrees are offered as a 4-year Integrated Foundation, and you should see the individual course page for the UCAS code.

items.heading: What will I do in the first year?
items.bodyText: You’ll develop a broad understanding of art, design and media skills and approaches, and produce a body of work that starts to reveal your personal identity and approach to your chosen programme of study.

items.heading: How will I be taught?
items.bodyText: The Integrated Foundation Year is intensive and challenging, taught through lectures, workshops and practical studio sessions, seminars and tutorials.

items.heading: What skills will I build for degree-level study?
items.bodyText: You’ll develop critical skills relevant to degree-level study while broadening your use of drawing, visual research, contextual studies, digital imaging and art and design methods.

items.heading: Will I progress automatically to my chosen degree?
items.bodyText: Yes. Successfully completing the Integrated Foundation year allows automatic progression to your chosen degree at Arts University Plymouth.

contentBlocks.caption: Students exhibit their work in their annual end of year show.

contentBlocks.blockquote: Every single person you rub shoulders with is a creative, whether it's students, staff, housekeeping, front of house, everyone is here for one reason and one reason only, to make Arts University Plymouth a family community where you can truly be yourself, find your artistic voice, and become the artist that you had only dreamed about before. Arts University Plymouth genuinely makes dreams come true, it has for me!
contentBlocks.attribution: Michele Azzopardi, BA (Hons) Craft & Material Practices with Integrated Foundation (previously Extended BA) graduate

pages.heading: MA Design (Fashion)
pages.text: Arts University Plymouth Logo Skip to Content Our Courses Open Days Apply Now Menu Apply Now Our Courses Open Days Chevron Down About Us Chevron Down Study Chevron Down International Chevron Down Student Life Alumni Chevron Down Visit Resources Chevron Down Research & Innovation Prospectus Latest News What's On Established 1856 Student Login Staff Login Contact Us Explore our Postgraduate courses MA Design (Fashion) Course Duration 1 year; full-time 2 years; part-time Admissions Contact admissions@aup.ac.uk +44 (0)1752 203434 Apply Now Register Your Interest Overview Course & Units Staff Careers & Alumni Ask a Student Resources Fees & Funding Overview MA Design (Fashion) is an opportunity to reimagine the status quo of fashion and to use a research-led, practical exploration of materials, processes and technologies to propose new strategies for the industry. Designed to foster both design entrepreneurs and creative practitioners, the course encourages you to build upon your existing knowledge or fashion experience to develop a fashion project realised through new material applications, circular production protocols and systems-thinking in a research-based, studio-centred enquiry. At a glance Award: MA Design (Fashion) Approach: research-led, practical exploration of materials, processes and technologies Project focus: new material applications, circular production protocols and systems-thinking Professional dimension: external briefs supporting an iterative evolution from concept to prototype to product or service Facilities access: Materials Lab, Biomaterials Lab, Sew Lab, CAD Lab and Fab Lab South West Research-led practice to propose new strategies This course will give you the opportunity to dive deep into current practices and theories in Fashion Design that are transforming the nature of this rapidly changing sector through a direct, critical interrogation of its standards and hands-on research. Designed to foster both design entrepreneurs and creative practitioners, our MA Design (Fashion) encourages you to build upon your existing knowledge or fashion experience to develop a fashion project realised through new material applications, circular production protocols and systems thinking in a research-based, studio centred enquiry. Your project, materials and systems-thinking You’ll build upon your existing knowledge or fashion experience to develop a fashion project realised through: New material applications Circular production protocols Systems-thinking in a research-based, studio-centred enquiry Your fashion research and creative development will happen together, using your existing practice or industry experience as the foundation for guided experiments to deconstruct and reimagine the assumptions embedded within both design education and fashion cultures. Interdisciplinary study with industry input You will benefit from embarking on this study journey within a truly interdisciplinary academic context, enriched by ongoing input from industry specialists and institutional partners who will help ground your experiments with real-world challenges and opportunities. From concept to prototype to product or service Through external briefs, your ideas and proposals will take on professional dimensions and provide you with a period of focused making through a full iterative evolution: Concept Prototype Product or service This process supports both your creative agency and the industry networks required to succeed in the field. Why choose this course? Build on your existing knowledge or industry experience to develop a project that interrogates, challenges and focuses on solutions through systems-thinking. Work within a multidisciplinary postgraduate community of makers and designers committed to leading necessary changes to current production models, providing opportunities for purposeful innovation and experimentation. Access state-of-the-art facilities and resources to develop your work, including our Materials Lab, Biomaterials Lab, Sew Lab, CAD Lab, and Fab Lab South West. Careers and future opportunities Career opportunities include: Fashion Designers, Fashion Retailers, Fashion Educators, Researchers, Entrepreneurs, Buyers, Materials Researchers and Wearables Designers. Frequently asked questions What is MA Design (Fashion) about? It is an opportunity to reimagine the status quo of fashion through a research-led, practical exploration of materials, processes and technologies to propose new strategies for the industry. Who is this course designed for? It is designed to foster both design entrepreneurs and creative practitioners, building on your existing knowledge or fashion experience. What will my MA project be realised through? Your project will be realised through new material applications, circular production protocols and systems-thinking in a research-based, studio-centred enquiry. How will research and creative development work together? Your fashion research and creative development will happen together, using your existing practice or industry experience as the foundation for guided experiments. How does the course challenge current fashion standards? You’ll undertake a direct, critical interrogation of fashion’s standards and hands-on research, deconstructing and reimagining assumptions embedded within both design education and fashion cultures. How will external briefs shape my outcomes? Through external briefs, your ideas and proposals take on professional dimensions and progress through an iterative evolution from concept to prototype to product or service. What facilities will I have access to? You’ll have access to state-of-the-art facilities including the Materials Lab, Biomaterials Lab, Sew Lab, CAD Lab and Fab Lab South West. What careers could this MA support? Career opportunities include Fashion Designers, Fashion Retailers, Fashion Educators, Researchers, Entrepreneurs, Buyers, Materials Researchers and Wearables Designers. Alumni Discount Arts University Plymouth graduates are offered a discount of 15% on Masters programme fees , regardless of when they studied with us previously. The discount applies if you studied on one of our pre-degree, foundation or undergraduate programmes. Entry Requirements MA applicants are normally expected to have an undergraduate degree at 2:2 or above. However, the strength of your creative practice and other forms of experience will be taken into account at the interview stage and we encourage you to start a conversation with us. What should my portfolio include? Your portfolio should give us an indication of the work that you have made, organised or been involved in. For our postgraduate arts, craft and design courses, we expect to see examples of work you have created. What is the deadline for applying? The best deadline to submit your MA application by is 1 July , however please be reassured that we can take late applications until the start of the course if places are still available. Get in touch Email: admissions@aup.ac.uk Tel: +44 (0)1752 203434 Want to find out more about MA Design (Fashion)? Designed to foster both design entrepreneurs and creative practitioners, the course encourages you to build upon your existing knowledge or fashion experience to develop a fashion project realised through new material applications, circular production protocols and systems-thinking in a research-based, studio-centred enquiry. At a glance

  • Award: MA Design (Fashion)

  • Approach: research-led, practical exploration of materials, processes and technologies

  • Project focus: new material applications, circular production protocols and systems-thinking

  • Professional dimension: external briefs supporting an iterative evolution from concept to prototype to product or service

  • Facilities access: Materials Lab, Biomaterials Lab, Sew Lab, CAD Lab and Fab Lab South West

Research-led practice to propose new strategies

This course will give you the opportunity to dive deep into current practices and theories in Fashion Design that are transforming the nature of this rapidly changing sector through a direct, critical interrogation of its standards and hands-on research. Designed to foster both design entrepreneurs and creative practitioners, our MA Design (Fashion) encourages you to build upon your existing knowledge or fashion experience to develop a fashion project realised through new material applications, circular production protocols and systems thinking in a research-based, studio centred enquiry.

Your project, materials and systems-thinking

You’ll build upon your existing knowledge or fashion experience to develop a fashion project realised through:

  • New material applications

  • Circular production protocols

  • Systems-thinking in a research-based, studio-centred enquiry

Your fashion research and creative development will happen together, using your existing practice or industry experience as the foundation for guided experiments to deconstruct and reimagine the assumptions embedded within both design education and fashion cultures.

Interdisciplinary study with industry input

You will benefit from embarking on this study journey within a truly interdisciplinary academic context, enriched by ongoing input from industry specialists and institutional partners who will help ground your experiments with real-world challenges and opportunities.

From concept to prototype to product or service

Through external briefs, your ideas and proposals will take on professional dimensions and provide you with a period of focused making through a full iterative evolution:

  • Concept

  • Prototype

  • Product or service

This process supports both your creative agency and the industry networks required to succeed in the field.

Why choose this course?

  • Build on your existing knowledge or industry experience to develop a project that interrogates, challenges and focuses on solutions through systems-thinking.

  • Work within a multidisciplinary postgraduate community of makers and designers committed to leading necessary changes to current production models, providing opportunities for purposeful innovation and experimentation.

  • Access state-of-the-art facilities and resources to develop your work, including our Materials Lab, Biomaterials Lab, Sew Lab, CAD Lab, and Fab Lab South West.

Careers and future opportunities

Career opportunities include: Fashion Designers, Fashion Retailers, Fashion Educators, Researchers, Entrepreneurs, Buyers, Materials Researchers and Wearables Designers.

Frequently asked questions What is MA Design (Fashion) about?

It is an opportunity to reimagine the status quo of fashion through a research-led, practical exploration of materials, processes and technologies to propose new strategies for the industry.

Who is this course designed for?

It is designed to foster both design entrepreneurs and creative practitioners, building on your existing knowledge or fashion experience.

What will my MA project be realised through?

Your project will be realised through new material applications, circular production protocols and systems-thinking in a research-based, studio-centred enquiry.

How will research and creative development work together?

Your fashion research and creative development will happen together, using your existing practice or industry experience as the foundation for guided experiments.

How does the course challenge current fashion standards?

You’ll undertake a direct, critical interrogation of fashion’s standards and hands-on research, deconstructing and reimagining assumptions embedded within both design education and fashion cultures.

How will external briefs shape my outcomes?

Through external briefs, your ideas and proposals take on professional dimensions and progress through an iterative evolution from concept to prototype to product or service.

What facilities will I have access to?

You’ll have access to state-of-the-art facilities including the Materials Lab, Biomaterials Lab, Sew Lab, CAD Lab and Fab Lab South West.

What careers could this MA support?

Career opportunities include Fashion Designers, Fashion Retailers, Fashion Educators, Researchers, Entrepreneurs, Buyers, Materials Researchers and Wearables Designers.

Alumni Discount

Arts University Plymouth graduates are offered a discount of 15% on Masters programme fees, regardless of when they studied with us previously. The discount applies if you studied on one of our pre-degree, foundation or undergraduate programmes.

Entry Requirements

MA applicants are normally expected to have an undergraduate degree at 2:2 or above. However, the strength of your creative practice and other forms of experience will be taken into account at the interview stage and we encourage you to start a conversation with us.

What should my portfolio include?

Your portfolio should give us an indication of the work that you have made, organised or been involved in. For our postgraduate arts, craft and design courses, we expect to see examples of work you have created.

What is the deadline for applying?

The best deadline to submit your MA application by is 1 July, however please be reassured that we can take late applications until the start of the course if places are still available.

Work by Zara Mcdermott Developing your style and visual methodology

This course will challenge you to deepen your personal style and approach and develop the theoretical and practical skills necessary to explore how this style can be expressed across many media and sectors.

You will learn how to develop new, emerging ideas into a visual methodology that speaks successfully in a crowded contemporary visual culture.

Work by Sue Lewry Working with briefs, partners and real-world challenges

You will have the opportunity to work collaboratively or with external partners on briefs that prioritise co-design, participation and reflective evaluation as a process that will give you the confidence to work generatively.

This course aims to expand the potential reach and form of your designs. You will be encouraged to research and identify a compelling social, environmental or business challenge made visible or more accessible through your designs, culminating in a feature project prototype or series of artefacts developed through a full journey, culminating in a feature project prototype or series of artefacts developed from concept to display for an external client.

Visual language beyond words

You will strengthen your ability to use visual language (form, colour, type, motion, light, image, character) in a dialogic process that captures the expressive potential of communication beyond words at the threshold between language and lived experience

Workshops, tools and how your work takes shape

Through your study you will have access to an extensive programme of practical workshops and material and digital resources for experimenting with how your work takes shape. You will have the opportunity to test how both traditional and emerging technologies might inspire new ways of realising your designs and ideas.

Work by Alan Qualtrough Why choose this course?

  • Build upon your previous study or experience in graphic design, illustration, photography or marketing to focus on a research project that will give you a broad cultural perspective on visual communication design.

  • Learn within a multidisciplinary community of practitioners supported by a regular visiting lecture programme of industry professionals and leading designers.

  • Professionalise your ideas by working with an external client or real-world challenge, helping you to build industry connections that sustain your career after you graduate.

Careers and future opportunities

Career opportunities include: Communication Designers, Graphic Designers, Visual Designers, Illustrators, Brand Designers, Interface Designers, Storyboard Designers and Packaging Designers.

Frequently asked questions What will I explore on MA Design (Communication)?

You’ll explore how current social, critical and technological paradigms are changing the way designers create and distribute narrative-driven artefacts or brand-led campaigns.

What kind of practice will this course help me develop?

It will challenge you to deepen your personal style and approach and develop theoretical and practical skills to explore how that style can be expressed across many media and sectors.

Will I work with external partners and real-world challenges?

Yes. You can work collaboratively or with external partners on briefs prioritising co-design, participation and reflective evaluation, and professionalise your ideas by working with an external client or real-world challenge.

What will my final outcome look like?

Your work culminates in a feature project prototype or series of artefacts developed from concept to display for an external client.

What resources will I have access to?

You’ll have access to practical workshops and resources including the Imprint Lab, Digital Print Bureau, Fab Lab South West, Multimedia Studios and Equipment Resource Centre.

Alumni Discount

Arts University Plymouth graduates are offered a discount of 15% on Masters programme fees, regardless of when they studied with us previously. The discount applies if you studied on one of our pre-degree, foundation or undergraduate programmes.

Entry Requirements

MA applicants are normally expected to have an undergraduate degree at 2:2 or above. However, the strength of your creative practice and other forms of experience will be taken into account at the interview stage and we encourage you to start a conversation with us.

What should my portfolio include?

Your portfolio should give us an indication of the work that you have made, organised or been involved in. For our postgraduate arts, craft and design courses, we expect to see examples of work you have created.

What is the deadline for applying?

The best deadline to submit your MA application by is 1 July, however please be reassured that we can take late applications until the start of the course if places are still available.

contentBlocks.text:
Build upon your knowledge and practical experience of illustration, graphic design and other communication media to explore the way current social, critical and technological paradigms are changing the way designers create and distribute narrative-driven artefacts or brand-led campaigns.

This course pushes the boundaries of how we structure and convey stories and subjects through an interdisciplinary community of practice, challenging you to deepen your personal style and approach and develop the theoretical and practical skills to explore how that style can be expressed across many media and sectors.

contentBlocks.heading: At a glance
contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Award: MA Design (Communication)

  • Who it’s for: previous study or experience in graphic design, illustration, photography or marketing

  • Project outcome: a feature project prototype or series of artefacts developed from concept to display for an external client

  • Access to workshops and resources: Imprint Lab, Digital Print Bureau, Fab Lab South West, Multimedia Studios and Equipment Resource Centre

image.title: Zara Mcdermott work for Global Challenges web res

contentBlocks.caption: Work by Zara Mcdermott

contentBlocks.heading: Developing your style and visual methodology

contentBlocks.bodyText:
This course will challenge you to deepen your personal style and approach and develop the theoretical and practical skills necessary to explore how this style can be expressed across many media and sectors.

You will learn how to develop new, emerging ideas into a visual methodology that speaks successfully in a crowded contemporary visual culture.

image.title: Sue Lewry Masters Show 2021 Plymouth College of Art 205

contentBlocks.caption: Work by Sue Lewry

contentBlocks.heading: Working with briefs, partners and real-world challenges

contentBlocks.bodyText:
You will have the opportunity to work collaboratively or with external partners on briefs that prioritise co-design, participation and reflective evaluation as a process that will give you the confidence to work generatively.

This course aims to expand the potential reach and form of your designs. You will be encouraged to research and identify a compelling social, environmental or business challenge made visible or more accessible through your designs, culminating in a feature project prototype or series of artefacts developed through a full journey, culminating in a feature project prototype or series of artefacts developed from concept to display for an external client.

You will strengthen your ability to use visual language (form, colour, type, motion, light, image, character) in a dialogic process that captures the expressive potential of communication beyond words at the threshold between language and lived experience

contentBlocks.heading: Workshops, tools and how your work takes shape

contentBlocks.bodyText: Through your study you will have access to an extensive programme of practical workshops and material and digital resources for experimenting with how your work takes shape. You will have the opportunity to test how both traditional and emerging technologies might inspire new ways of realising your designs and ideas.

contentBlocks.caption: Work by Alan Qualtrough

contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Build upon your previous study or experience in graphic design, illustration, photography or marketing to focus on a research project that will give you a broad cultural perspective on visual communication design.

  • Learn within a multidisciplinary community of practitioners supported by a regular visiting lecture programme of industry professionals and leading designers.

  • Professionalise your ideas by working with an external client or real-world challenge, helping you to build industry connections that sustain your career after you graduate.
Career opportunities include: Communication Designers, Graphic Designers, Visual Designers, Illustrators, Brand Designers, Interface Designers, Storyboard Designers and Packaging Designers.

items.heading: What will I explore on MA Design (Communication)?
items.bodyText: You’ll explore how current social, critical and technological paradigms are changing the way designers create and distribute narrative-driven artefacts or brand-led campaigns.

items.heading: What kind of practice will this course help me develop?
items.bodyText: It will challenge you to deepen your personal style and approach and develop theoretical and practical skills to explore how that style can be expressed across many media and sectors.

items.heading: Will I work with external partners and real-world challenges?
items.bodyText: Yes. You can work collaboratively or with external partners on briefs prioritising co-design, participation and reflective evaluation, and professionalise your ideas by working with an external client or real-world challenge.

items.heading: What will my final outcome look like?
items.bodyText: Your work culminates in a feature project prototype or series of artefacts developed from concept to display for an external client.

items.heading: What resources will I have access to?
items.bodyText: You’ll have access to practical workshops and resources including the Imprint Lab, Digital Print Bureau, Fab Lab South West, Multimedia Studios and Equipment Resource Centre.

contentBlocks.heading: Alumni Discount
contentBlocks.bodyText: Arts University Plymouth graduates are offered a discount of 15% on Masters programme fees, regardless of when they studied with us previously. The discount applies if you studied on one of our pre-degree, foundation or undergraduate programmes.

contentBlocks.heading: Entry Requirements
contentBlocks.bodyText: MA applicants are normally expected to have an undergraduate degree at 2:2 or above. However, the strength of your creative practice and other forms of experience will be taken into account at the interview stage and we encourage you to start a conversation with us.

contentBlocks.heading: What should my portfolio include?
contentBlocks.bodyText: Your portfolio should give us an indication of the work that you have made, organised or been involved in. For our postgraduate arts, craft and design courses, we expect to see examples of work you have created.

contentBlocks.heading: What is the deadline for applying?
contentBlocks.bodyText: The best deadline to submit your MA application by is 1 July, however please be reassured that we can take late applications until the start of the course if places are still available.

contentBlocks.heading: Get in touch
contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Email: admissions@aup.ac.uk
  • Tel: +44 (0)1752 203434
