You will learn how to approach space as a dynamic infrastructure. At a glance

  • Award: MA Design (Built Environment)

  • Learning emphasis: project-based, place-based, and open-knowledge approaches to design

  • Practice focus: co-design and practice-led research

  • Professional focus: well-being, circular production and regenerative design

How you’ll learn Develop a project within a learning environment that emphasises project-based, place-based, and open-knowledge approaches to design. Trinitatum by Paul Hillon , BA (Hons) Fine Art and MA Fine Art graduate, and now a Technical Tutor on our Fine Art courses. Multidisciplinary community and expertise

Study as part of a multidisciplinary community of practitioners who have expertise in interior design, CAD modelling, 3D photogrammetry, spatial acoustics, material innovations, and immersive media environments.

During his Erasmus exchange at Arts University Plymouth as a student on MA Design (Built Environment), Eslam ElShamy developed a project that used workshops, archival research and immersive media to explore how lost heritage might be experienced collectively. Professional practice for social and cultural change

Discover ways of working professionally, with a focus on well-being, circular production and regenerative design, to lead social and cultural change.

Why choose this course?

  • Develop a project within a learning environment that emphasises project-based, place-based, and open-knowledge approaches to design.

  • Study as part of a multidisciplinary community of practitioners with expertise in interior design, CAD modelling, 3D photogrammetry, spatial acoustics, material innovations, and immersive media environments.

  • Discover ways of working professionally, with a focus on well-being, circular production and regenerative design, to lead social and cultural change.

Careers and future opportunities

Career opportunities include: Interior Designers, Experience Designers, Production Designers, Materials Specialists, Creative Directors, Design Entrepreneurs, Product Managers and Design Production Managers.

Frequently asked questions What is MA Design (Built Environment) focused on?

It prepares you to develop a unique practice using co-design and practice-led research to transform the spaces people inhabit for increased wellbeing, social agency and sense of place.

How will I learn to think about space on this course?

You will learn how to approach space as a dynamic infrastructure.

What learning approaches are emphasised?

The course emphasises project-based, place-based, and open-knowledge approaches to design.

What kind of community will I study within?

You’ll study as part of a multidisciplinary community of practitioners with expertise in interior design, CAD modelling, 3D photogrammetry, spatial acoustics, material innovations, and immersive media environments.

What professional focus does the course develop?

It focuses on professional ways of working with an emphasis on well-being, circular production and regenerative design, to lead social and cultural change.

What careers could this MA support?

Career opportunities include Interior Designers, Experience Designers, Production Designers, Materials Specialists, Creative Directors, Design Entrepreneurs, Product Managers and Design Production Managers.

Alumni Discount

Arts University Plymouth graduates are offered a discount of 15% on Masters programme fees, regardless of when they studied with us previously. The discount applies if you studied on one of our pre-degree, foundation or undergraduate programmes.

Entry Requirements

MA applicants are normally expected to have an undergraduate degree at 2:2 or above. However, the strength of your creative practice and other forms of experience will be taken into account at the interview stage and we encourage you to start a conversation with us.

What should my portfolio include?

Your portfolio should give us an indication of the work that you have made, organised or been involved in. For our postgraduate arts, craft and design courses, we expect to see examples of work you have created.

What is the deadline for applying?

The best deadline to submit your MA application by is 1 July, however please be reassured that we can take late applications until the start of the course if places are still available.

contentBlocks.text:
MA Design (Built Environment) prepares you to develop a unique practice using methods of co-design and practice-led research to transform the spaces people inhabit for increased wellbeing, social agency and sense of place.

You will learn how to approach space as a dynamic infrastructure.

contentBlocks.heading: At a glance
contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Award: MA Design (Built Environment)

  • Learning emphasis: project-based, place-based, and open-knowledge approaches to design

  • Practice focus: co-design and practice-led research

  • Professional focus: well-being, circular production and regenerative design

contentBlocks.text: Develop a project within a learning environment that emphasises project-based, place-based, and open-knowledge approaches to design.

contentBlocks.caption: Trinitatum by Paul Hillon, BA (Hons) Fine Art and MA Fine Art graduate, and now a Technical Tutor on our Fine Art courses.

contentBlocks.bodyText: Study as part of a multidisciplinary community of practitioners who have expertise in interior design, CAD modelling, 3D photogrammetry, spatial acoustics, material innovations, and immersive media environments.

contentBlocks.caption: During his Erasmus exchange at Arts University Plymouth as a student on MA Design (Built Environment), Eslam ElShamy developed a project that used workshops, archival research and immersive media to explore how lost heritage might be experienced collectively.

contentBlocks.heading: Professional practice for social and cultural change

contentBlocks.bodyText: Discover ways of working professionally, with a focus on well-being, circular production and regenerative design, to lead social and cultural change.

• Develop a project within a learning environment that emphasises project-based, place-based, and open-knowledge approaches to design.

  • Study as part of a multidisciplinary community of practitioners with expertise in interior design, CAD modelling, 3D photogrammetry, spatial acoustics, material innovations, and immersive media environments.

  • Discover ways of working professionally, with a focus on well-being, circular production and regenerative design, to lead social and cultural change.

image.title: Work by Interior Design student Alisha Meaker

contentBlocks.bodyText: Career opportunities include: Interior Designers, Experience Designers, Production Designers, Materials Specialists, Creative Directors, Design Entrepreneurs, Product Managers and Design Production Managers.

items.heading: What is MA Design (Built Environment) focused on?
items.bodyText: It prepares you to develop a unique practice using co-design and practice-led research to transform the spaces people inhabit for increased wellbeing, social agency and sense of place.

items.heading: How will I learn to think about space on this course?
items.bodyText: You will learn how to approach space as a dynamic infrastructure.

items.heading: What learning approaches are emphasised?
items.bodyText: The course emphasises project-based, place-based, and open-knowledge approaches to design.

items.heading: What kind of community will I study within?
items.bodyText: You’ll study as part of a multidisciplinary community of practitioners with expertise in interior design, CAD modelling, 3D photogrammetry, spatial acoustics, material innovations, and immersive media environments.

items.heading: What professional focus does the course develop?
items.bodyText: It focuses on professional ways of working with an emphasis on well-being, circular production and regenerative design, to lead social and cultural change.

items.heading: What careers could this MA support?
items.bodyText: Career opportunities include Interior Designers, Experience Designers, Production Designers, Materials Specialists, Creative Directors, Design Entrepreneurs, Product Managers and Design Production Managers.

contentBlocks.heading: Alumni Discount
contentBlocks.bodyText: Arts University Plymouth graduates are offered a discount of 15% on Masters programme fees, regardless of when they studied with us previously. The discount applies if you studied on one of our pre-degree, foundation or undergraduate programmes.

contentBlocks.heading: Entry Requirements
contentBlocks.bodyText: MA applicants are normally expected to have an undergraduate degree at 2:2 or above. However, the strength of your creative practice and other forms of experience will be taken into account at the interview stage and we encourage you to start a conversation with us.

contentBlocks.heading: What should my portfolio include?
contentBlocks.bodyText: Your portfolio should give us an indication of the work that you have made, organised or been involved in. For our postgraduate arts, craft and design courses, we expect to see examples of work you have created.

contentBlocks.heading: What is the deadline for applying?
contentBlocks.bodyText: The best deadline to submit your MA application by is 1 July, however please be reassured that we can take late applications until the start of the course if places are still available.

contentBlocks.heading: Get in touch
contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Email: admissions@aup.ac.uk
  • Tel: +44 (0)1752 203434

contentBlocks.heading: Want to find out more about MA Design (Built Environment)?
contentBlocks.bodyText:

  • Becky Dodman Wainwright, Co-Course Leader for Postgraduate Studies
  • Jason Hirons, Co-Course Leader for Postgraduate Studies

pages.text: Arts University Plymouth Logo Skip to Content Our Courses Open Days Apply Now Menu Apply Now Our Courses Open Days Chevron Down About Us Chevron Down Study Chevron Down International Chevron Down Student Life Alumni Chevron Down Visit Resources Chevron Down Research & Innovation Prospectus Latest News What's On Established 1856 Student Login Staff Login Contact Us Explore our Postgraduate courses MA Design (Textiles) Course Duration 1 year; full-time 2 years; part-time Admissions Contact admissions@aup.ac.uk +44 (0)1752 203434 Apply Now Register Your Interest Overview Course & Units Staff Careers & Alumni Ask a Student Resources Fees & Funding Overview This course is focused on the research, design and production of textiles and their use in the fashion, interior, and transportation sectors. You will have the opportunity to focus on either structured or printed textiles, deploying both traditional techniques and emerging methods, using bio-based materials, natural dyeing and digital technologies in a hyperlocal and place-based context. Build upon your existing study or industry experience through a research-led, studio-based investigation of the current production methods and creative approaches to the art and science of textiles. Whether you are a small-scale studio designer or have the ambition to disrupt existing textile industries, the course curriculum will encourage you to uncover your personal objectives and allow you to tailor your research within a broad range of options. At a glance Award: MA Design (Textiles) Sectors: fashion, interior and transportation Focus options: structured textiles or printed textiles Context: hyperlocal and place-based In 2024, as part of a British Council-supported residency, Arts University Plymouth hosted a workshop by Shamji Vankar, a master weaver from the Kachchh region in north India. Research-led textiles across sectors Build upon your existing study or industry experience through a research-led, studio-based investigation of the current production methods and creative approaches to the art and science of textiles. This equips you with the historical and practical knowledge to work within a creative sector that interfaces with a large variety of contemporary industries. Structured or printed textiles, traditional and emerging methods You will have the opportunity to focus on either structured or printed textiles, deploying both traditional techniques and emerging methods. You will work with bio-based materials, natural dyeing and digital technologies in a hyperlocal and place-based context. Your objectives, from studio practice to industry disruption Whether you are a small-scale studio designer or have the ambition to disrupt existing textile industries through the development of innovative manufacturing protocols or material processes, the course curriculum will encourage you to uncover your personal objectives and allow you to tailor your research within a broad range of options. Visiting specialists, entrepreneurs and cross-disciplinary careers Working in the context of a rich programme of visiting specialists and local and international entrepreneurs, you will gain critical understanding of how contemporary textile design and manufacture are bridging ancient techniques and emerging technologies to create novel cross-disciplinary careers. Labs, facilities and your technical development This is supported through access to our Natural Dye Lab, Materials Lab, Sew Lab, Embroidery Studio, Tufting Studio, Knitting Machines, Biomaterials Lab, and Fab Lab South West, offering the opportunity to develop new skills and understanding of the structure, chemistry and fabrication of textiles. You will be encouraged to develop original expertise and thorough knowledge of fibres, pattern and print from industry standard to planet-conscious alternatives. Why choose this course? You will learn textiles from a range of perspectives and techniques preparing you for various creative roles within the fashion, textile, and design industries. Learn within an environment of experts committed to developing novel textiles and processes that put the planet and people first in design. Be part of a growing postgraduate design community using practice-based research methods to discover innovative solutions to real-world challenges. Careers and future opportunities Career opportunities include: Textile Designers, Interior Designers, Textile Researchers, Purchasers, Writers/Curators, Product Developers, Textile Artists, Artisans/Craftspeople and Entrepreneurs. Frequently asked questions What is MA Design (Textiles) focused on? It focuses on the research, design and production of textiles and their use in the fashion, interior, and transportation sectors. Can I focus on structured or printed textiles? Yes. You will have the opportunity to focus on either structured or printed textiles. What techniques and technologies will I use? You will deploy both traditional techniques and emerging methods, using bio-based materials, natural dyeing and digital technologies in a hyperlocal and place-based context. How does the course support sustainability and circular practice? It addresses the challenge of textile waste and toxicity and supports moving towards a more circular and ethical design process. What facilities will support my research and making? You will have access to the Natural Dye Lab, Materials Lab, Sew Lab, Embroidery Studio, Tufting Studio, Knitting Machines, Biomaterials Lab, and Fab Lab South West to build skills and understanding of textile structure, chemistry and fabrication. What kinds of careers could this course support? Career opportunities include Textile Designers, Interior Designers, Textile Researchers, Purchasers, Writers/Curators, Product Developers, Textile Artists, Artisans/Craftspeople and Entrepreneurs. Alumni Discount Arts University Plymouth graduates are offered a discount of 15% on Masters programme fees , regardless of when they studied with us previously. The discount applies if you studied on one of our pre-degree, foundation or undergraduate programmes. Entry Requirements MA applicants are normally expected to have an undergraduate degree at 2:2 or above. However, the strength of your creative practice and other forms of experience will be taken into account at the interview stage and we encourage you to start a conversation with us. What should my portfolio include? Your portfolio should give us an indication of the work that you have made, organised or been involved in. For our postgraduate arts, craft and design courses, we expect to see examples of work you have created. What is the deadline for applying? The best deadline to submit your MA application by is 1 July , however please be reassured that we can take late applications until the start of the course if places are still available. contentBlocks.text:
This course is focused on the research, design and production of textiles and their use in the fashion, interior, and transportation sectors. You will have the opportunity to focus on either structured or printed textiles, deploying both traditional techniques and emerging methods, using bio-based materials, natural dyeing and digital technologies in a hyperlocal and place-based context.

Build upon your existing study or industry experience through a research-led, studio-based investigation of the current production methods and creative approaches to the art and science of textiles. Whether you are a small-scale studio designer or have the ambition to disrupt existing textile industries, the course curriculum will encourage you to uncover your personal objectives and allow you to tailor your research within a broad range of options.

contentBlocks.heading: At a glance
contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Award: MA Design (Textiles)

  • Sectors: fashion, interior and transportation

  • Focus options: structured textiles or printed textiles

  • Context: hyperlocal and place-based

image.title: Becky Dodman Wainwright, Neil Rose and Stephanie Owens in discussion at Shamji Textiles Workshop at Arts University Plymouth with students and staff in the foreground

contentBlocks.caption: In 2024, as part of a British Council-supported residency, Arts University Plymouth hosted a workshop by Shamji Vankar, a master weaver from the Kachchh region in north India.

contentBlocks.bodyText: Build upon your existing study or industry experience through a research-led, studio-based investigation of the current production methods and creative approaches to the art and science of textiles. This equips you with the historical and practical knowledge to work within a creative sector that interfaces with a large variety of contemporary industries.

image.title: A female with brown hair tied in a low ponytail standing in front of a colourful textile hanging using a tufting gun

contentBlocks.heading: Structured or printed textiles, traditional and emerging methods

contentBlocks.bodyText: You will have the opportunity to focus on either structured or printed textiles, deploying both traditional techniques and emerging methods. You will work with bio-based materials, natural dyeing and digital technologies in a hyperlocal and place-based context.

contentBlocks.heading: Your objectives, from studio practice to industry disruption

contentBlocks.bodyText: Whether you are a small-scale studio designer or have the ambition to disrupt existing textile industries through the development of innovative manufacturing protocols or material processes, the course curriculum will encourage you to uncover your personal objectives and allow you to tailor your research within a broad range of options.

contentBlocks.heading: Visiting specialists, entrepreneurs and cross-disciplinary careers

contentBlocks.bodyText: Working in the context of a rich programme of visiting specialists and local and international entrepreneurs, you will gain critical understanding of how contemporary textile design and manufacture are bridging ancient techniques and emerging technologies to create novel cross-disciplinary careers.

contentBlocks.heading: Labs, facilities and your technical development

contentBlocks.bodyText:
This is supported through access to our Natural Dye Lab, Materials Lab, Sew Lab, Embroidery Studio, Tufting Studio, Knitting Machines, Biomaterials Lab, and Fab Lab South West, offering the opportunity to develop new skills and understanding of the structure, chemistry and fabrication of textiles.

You will be encouraged to develop original expertise and thorough knowledge of fibres, pattern and print from industry standard to planet-conscious alternatives.

• You will learn textiles from a range of perspectives and techniques preparing you for various creative roles within the fashion, textile, and design industries.

  • Learn within an environment of experts committed to developing novel textiles and processes that put the planet and people first in design.

  • Be part of a growing postgraduate design community using practice-based research methods to discover innovative solutions to real-world challenges.
Career opportunities include: Textile Designers, Interior Designers, Textile Researchers, Purchasers, Writers/Curators, Product Developers, Textile Artists, Artisans/Craftspeople and Entrepreneurs.

items.heading: What is MA Design (Textiles) focused on?
items.bodyText: It focuses on the research, design and production of textiles and their use in the fashion, interior, and transportation sectors.

items.heading: Can I focus on structured or printed textiles?
items.bodyText: Yes. You will have the opportunity to focus on either structured or printed textiles.

items.heading: What techniques and technologies will I use?
items.bodyText: You will deploy both traditional techniques and emerging methods, using bio-based materials, natural dyeing and digital technologies in a hyperlocal and place-based context.

items.heading: How does the course support sustainability and circular practice?
items.bodyText: It addresses the challenge of textile waste and toxicity and supports moving towards a more circular and ethical design process.

items.heading: What facilities will support my research and making?
items.bodyText: You will have access to the Natural Dye Lab, Materials Lab, Sew Lab, Embroidery Studio, Tufting Studio, Knitting Machines, Biomaterials Lab, and Fab Lab South West to build skills and understanding of textile structure, chemistry and fabrication.

items.heading: What kinds of careers could this course support?
items.bodyText: Career opportunities include Textile Designers, Interior Designers, Textile Researchers, Purchasers, Writers/Curators, Product Developers, Textile Artists, Artisans/Craftspeople and Entrepreneurs.

contentBlocks.heading: Alumni Discount
contentBlocks.bodyText: Arts University Plymouth graduates are offered a discount of 15% on Masters programme fees, regardless of when they studied with us previously. The discount applies if you studied on one of our pre-degree, foundation or undergraduate programmes.

contentBlocks.heading: Entry Requirements
contentBlocks.bodyText: MA applicants are normally expected to have an undergraduate degree at 2:2 or above. However, the strength of your creative practice and other forms of experience will be taken into account at the interview stage and we encourage you to start a conversation with us.

contentBlocks.heading: What should my portfolio include?
contentBlocks.bodyText: Your portfolio should give us an indication of the work that you have made, organised or been involved in. For our postgraduate arts, craft and design courses, we expect to see examples of work you have created.

contentBlocks.heading: What is the deadline for applying?
contentBlocks.bodyText: The best deadline to submit your MA application by is 1 July, however please be reassured that we can take late applications until the start of the course if places are still available.

contentBlocks.heading: Get in touch
contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Email: admissions@aup.ac.uk
  • Tel: +44 (0)1752 203434

This course teaches design strategies, analytical skills and existing material practices to help you reimagine the designer’s role in relation to nature and ecological systems, and the use of new and emerging technologies in the face of some of humanity’s most ‘wicked’ problems. contentBlocks.text:
Develop new products, practices and applications for contemporary society through a speculative lens to imagine design beyond the status quo of production and consumption. This course teaches design as an active mode of research that seeks to positively impact human and planetary wellbeing.

This course teaches design strategies, analytical skills and existing material practices to help you reimagine the designer’s role in relation to nature and ecological systems, and the use of new and emerging technologies in the face of some of humanity’s most ‘wicked’ problems.

contentBlocks.heading: At a glance
contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Award: MA Design

  • Approach: design as an active mode of research

  • Core values: full life-cycle awareness and a more circular production ethos

  • Facilities access: Natural Dye Lab, Biomaterials Lab, Materials Lab and Fab Lab South West

image.title: AUP Master 2022 Work by Owen Rees 48

contentBlocks.caption: Work by Owen Rees

contentBlocks.bodyText:
Your learning will follow a design process based on practice-led research methodologies and project development informed by material investigation, iterative production, co-design, prototyping, visualisation and reflective market analysis.

You will be encouraged to consider both small-scale and mass market manufacturing, identifying the ways that your designs may potentially impact communities, the economy and the environment.

image.title: Sue Lewry Masters Show 2021 Plymouth College of Art 205

contentBlocks.caption: Work by Sue Lewry

contentBlocks.heading: Life-cycle awareness, circular production and new technologies

contentBlocks.bodyText:
We value design principles based on full life-cycle awareness aimed at a more circular production ethos, now integral to an ethical approach to design, that furthers human and planetary wellbeing.

Exploring new technologies as a key driver of change is an important component of the course, being deployed in ways that make what we wear, own, experience and sell more accessible, more economical as well as desirable.

Your ideas will be refined through peer team working and in collaboration with an external partner or institution whom you identify as influential or necessary to your design ideas and target market.

Thinking through the discipline of design, you will learn to bridge the gap between the artisanal and contemporary best practices so that regardless of the changes to come, you are prepared to respond and creatively adapt.

• Open to any design discipline and for those whose design concepts do not easily fit a single area of practice.

  • Study regenerative design methodologies to learn how to reimagine traditional design processes for more sustainable futures.

  • Have unique access to our Natural Dye Lab, Biomaterials Lab, Materials Lab and Fab Lab South West, allowing you to pursue design research through novel media and processes from concept to prototype.

image.title: A series of colourful fabric swatches spread on a white table in the BA Textiles Natural Dyeing Workshop Nov 2021

contentBlocks.bodyText: Career opportunities include: Designers, Creative Directors, Design Researchers, Design Educators, Entrepreneurs, Product Managers, Production Managers, Sustainable Design Advocates and Design Writers.

items.heading: What is MA Design focused on?
items.bodyText: It develops new products, practices and applications for contemporary society through a speculative lens to imagine design beyond the status quo of production and consumption.

items.heading: How does the course approach design and its impact?
items.bodyText: It teaches design as an active mode of research, grounded in full life-cycle awareness and a more circular production ethos that furthers human and planetary wellbeing.

items.heading: What kinds of issues can my project explore?
items.bodyText: Your work can explore usability, supply-chains, models of production, fabrication technologies, life-cycle analysis, consumer behaviour and digital-material interfaces.

items.heading: What process will guide my learning?
items.bodyText: Your learning follows practice-led research methodologies and project development informed by material investigation, iterative production, co-design, prototyping, visualisation and reflective market analysis.

items.heading: Will I consider small-scale and mass market contexts?
items.bodyText: Yes. You’ll consider both small-scale and mass market manufacturing and identify how designs may potentially impact communities, the economy and the environment.

items.heading: What facilities can support my research and prototyping?
items.bodyText: You’ll have unique access to the Natural Dye Lab, Biomaterials Lab, Materials Lab and Fab Lab South West to pursue design research through novel media and processes from concept to prototype.

contentBlocks.heading: Alumni Discount
contentBlocks.bodyText: Arts University Plymouth graduates are offered a discount of 15% on Masters programme fees, regardless of when they studied with us previously. The discount applies if you studied on one of our pre-degree, foundation or undergraduate programmes.

contentBlocks.heading: Entry Requirements
contentBlocks.bodyText: MA applicants are normally expected to have an undergraduate degree at 2:2 or above. However, the strength of your creative practice and other forms of experience will be taken into account at the interview stage and we encourage you to start a conversation with us.

contentBlocks.heading: What should my portfolio include?
contentBlocks.bodyText: Your portfolio should give us an indication of the work that you have made, organised or been involved in. For our postgraduate arts, craft and design courses, we expect to see examples of work you have created.

contentBlocks.heading: What is the deadline for applying?
contentBlocks.bodyText: The best deadline to submit your MA application by is 1 July, however please be reassured that we can take late applications until the start of the course if places are still available.

contentBlocks.heading: Get in touch
contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Email: admissions@aup.ac.uk
  • Tel: +44 (0)1752 203434

contentBlocks.heading: Want to find out more about MA Design?
contentBlocks.bodyText:
If you'd like to speak about Postgraduate study, you can book an informal online chat with a member of our academic team:

  • Associate Professor Stephanie Owens, our Dean of Arts, Design and Media
  • Becky Dodman Wainwright, Co-Course Leader for Postgraduate Studies
  • Jason Hirons, Co-Course Leader for Postgraduate Studies

Click the button below to book an informal discussion with a member of our academic team.

pages.text: Arts University Plymouth Logo Skip to Content Our Courses Open Days Apply Now Menu Apply Now Our Courses Open Days Chevron Down About Us Chevron Down Study Chevron Down International Chevron Down Student Life Alumni Chevron Down Visit Resources Chevron Down Research & Innovation Prospectus Latest News What's On Established 1856 Student Login Staff Login Contact Us Explore our Postgraduate courses MA Immersive Media Course Duration 1 year; full-time 2 years; part-time Admissions Contact admissions@aup.ac.uk +44 (0)1752 203434 Apply Now Register Your Interest Overview Course & Units Staff Careers & Alumni Ask a Student Resources Fees & Funding Overview This course prepares you to translate your creative ideas and digital skills into engaging immersive content and public media for diverse audiences. You will learn digital workflows in a professional environment, including within one of Europe’s largest immersive dome theatres located at Real Ideas’ Market Hall in Plymouth. Be part of Plymouth’s creative technology movement, where you’ll develop creative concepts for this exciting and rapidly growing sector in the South West, UK. Dive into a world of immersive technology with MA Immersive Media at Arts University Plymouth. At a glance Award: MA Immersive Media Study pattern: three 60-credit units over one year, or over two years part-time Core setting: Real Ideas’ Market Hall immersive dome theatre (professional digital workflows) Core areas: immersive content and public media for diverse audiences Developing content for public and institutional spaces Led by expert staff and creative practitioners with pioneering experience in immersive media and digital world building, you will learn to develop original digital content for public and institutional spaces, including for a 360-degree dome optimised for seamless visuals and spatial audio. An audience watching a show in the Immersive Dome at Market Hall in Plymouth, the first of it's kind in Europe. Image credit: Studio Wallop Immersion, frameless media and emerging formats In addition to developing media for fully contained immersion, you will be introduced to a wide range of related technologies and approaches to frameless media, including Virtual Reality (VR), Augmented Reality (AR) and Mixed Reality (MR). These can be experienced through passive and interactive formats such as animation, game environments, surround sound, 3D visualisation, and 360-degree video and film, among other forms. Your research project and professional readiness Through a sequence of three 60-credit units over the year (or over two years part-time), you will develop an individual or collaborative research project by learning state-of-the-art technologies to develop and produce innovative media that will fully prepare you for employment in any of the many sectors now embracing this emerging cultural form. The university’s commitment to social justice and ecological citizenship provides a learning environment for developing projects that emphasise the unique aspects of public or community-led media. Real Ideas' Immersive Dome at Market Hall in Devonport, Plymouth. Image credit: Jay Stone Real Ideas partnership and the human aspects of immersion With this focused expertise, and the opportunity to develop immersive media within a social context through our partnership with Real Ideas, a social enterprise, MA Immersive Media serves as a crucible for aesthetic innovation. It is uniquely attuned to the human aspects of immersive experiences, giving graduates a distinct advantage within the industry. Why choose this course? Work within a state-of-the-art dome facility, where student projects are created for 8k visual projection and a 19.1 audio speaker array. Offered in partnership with Real Ideas/Real Immersive, based in a unique historic building at Market Hall, adapted for a 360 degree immersive dome and surrounded by production studios and suites used by industry professionals. Opportunities to connect with other media artists and designers and exhibit your work through our South West regional and international immersive networks. A packed audience watching a show at Real Ideas' Immersive Dome in Market Hall, Devonport. Image credit: Jay Stone Careers and future opportunities Career opportunities include: Games Designers, Media Artists, Immersive or Augmented Experience Designers, Heritage Education Designers, Immersive Media Designers for Tourism, Product Developers, Science Educators and work with the Healthcare Industry. Frequently asked questions What will MA Immersive Media prepare me to do? It prepares you to translate your creative ideas and digital skills into engaging immersive content and public media for diverse audiences. Where will I learn immersive production workflows? You will learn digital workflows in a professional environment, including within one of Europe’s largest immersive dome theatres located at Real Ideas’ Market Hall in Plymouth. What kinds of immersive technologies will I explore? You will be introduced to frameless media including Virtual Reality (VR), Augmented Reality (AR) and Mixed Reality (MR). What formats might my immersive work use? Your work can be experienced through passive and interactive formats such as animation, game environments, surround sound, 3D visualisation, and 360-degree video and film. How is the course structured? Through three 60-credit units over one year (or over two years part-time), you will develop an individual or collaborative research project using state-of-the-art technologies. What careers could this MA support? Career opportunities include Games Designers, Media Artists, Immersive or Augmented Experience Designers, Heritage Education Designers, Immersive Media Designers for Tourism, Product Developers, Science Educators and work with the Healthcare Industry. A dancer is silhouetted against the projections in the Immersive Dome at Market Hall. Image credit: Immersive Me Alumni Discount Arts University Plymouth graduates are offered a discount of 15% on Masters programme fees , regardless of when they studied with us previously. The discount applies if you studied on one of our pre-degree, foundation or undergraduate programmes. Entry Requirements MA applicants are normally expected to have an undergraduate degree at 2:2 or above. However, the strength of your creative practice and other forms of experience will be taken into account at the interview stage and we encourage you to start a conversation with us. What should my portfolio include? Your portfolio should give us an indication of the work that you have made, organised or been involved in. For our postgraduate arts, craft and design courses, we expect to see examples of work you have created. For our MA Museum Studies, and MA Immersive Media courses, we don't expect you to have traditional artworks; instead you can share examples of projects you have worked on, classroom experiences you have created, and so on. Please ensure that your portfolio includes descriptions, website links and visuals if they are available. What is the deadline for applying? The best deadline to submit your MA application by is 1 July , however please be reassured that we can take late applications until the start of the course if places are still available.   • Core setting: Real Ideas’ Market Hall immersive dome theatre (professional digital workflows)

  • Core areas: immersive content and public media for diverse audiences

Developing content for public and institutional spaces

Led by expert staff and creative practitioners with pioneering experience in immersive media and digital world building, you will learn to develop original digital content for public and institutional spaces, including for a 360-degree dome optimised for seamless visuals and spatial audio.

An audience watching a show in the Immersive Dome at Market Hall in Plymouth, the first of it's kind in Europe. Image credit: Studio Wallop Immersion, frameless media and emerging formats

In addition to developing media for fully contained immersion, you will be introduced to a wide range of related technologies and approaches to frameless media, including Virtual Reality (VR), Augmented Reality (AR) and Mixed Reality (MR).

These can be experienced through passive and interactive formats such as animation, game environments, surround sound, 3D visualisation, and 360-degree video and film, among other forms.

Your research project and professional readiness

Through a sequence of three 60-credit units over the year (or over two years part-time), you will develop an individual or collaborative research project by learning state-of-the-art technologies to develop and produce innovative media that will fully prepare you for employment in any of the many sectors now embracing this emerging cultural form.

The university’s commitment to social justice and ecological citizenship provides a learning environment for developing projects that emphasise the unique aspects of public or community-led media.

Real Ideas' Immersive Dome at Market Hall in Devonport, Plymouth. Image credit: Jay Stone Real Ideas partnership and the human aspects of immersion

With this focused expertise, and the opportunity to develop immersive media within a social context through our partnership with Real Ideas, a social enterprise, MA Immersive Media serves as a crucible for aesthetic innovation. It is uniquely attuned to the human aspects of immersive experiences, giving graduates a distinct advantage within the industry.

Why choose this course?

  • Work within a state-of-the-art dome facility, where student projects are created for 8k visual projection and a 19.1 audio speaker array.

  • Offered in partnership with Real Ideas/Real Immersive, based in a unique historic building at Market Hall, adapted for a 360 degree immersive dome and surrounded by production studios and suites used by industry professionals.

  • Opportunities to connect with other media artists and designers and exhibit your work through our South West regional and international immersive networks.

A packed audience watching a show at Real Ideas' Immersive Dome in Market Hall, Devonport. Image credit: Jay Stone Careers and future opportunities

Career opportunities include: Games Designers, Media Artists, Immersive or Augmented Experience Designers, Heritage Education Designers, Immersive Media Designers for Tourism, Product Developers, Science Educators and work with the Healthcare Industry.

Frequently asked questions What will MA Immersive Media prepare me to do?

It prepares you to translate your creative ideas and digital skills into engaging immersive content and public media for diverse audiences.

Where will I learn immersive production workflows?

You will learn digital workflows in a professional environment, including within one of Europe’s largest immersive dome theatres located at Real Ideas’ Market Hall in Plymouth.

What kinds of immersive technologies will I explore?

You will be introduced to frameless media including Virtual Reality (VR), Augmented Reality (AR) and Mixed Reality (MR).

What formats might my immersive work use?

Your work can be experienced through passive and interactive formats such as animation, game environments, surround sound, 3D visualisation, and 360-degree video and film.

How is the course structured?

Through three 60-credit units over one year (or over two years part-time), you will develop an individual or collaborative research project using state-of-the-art technologies.

What careers could this MA support?

Career opportunities include Games Designers, Media Artists, Immersive or Augmented Experience Designers, Heritage Education Designers, Immersive Media Designers for Tourism, Product Developers, Science Educators and work with the Healthcare Industry.

A dancer is silhouetted against the projections in the Immersive Dome at Market Hall. Image credit: Immersive Me Alumni Discount

Arts University Plymouth graduates are offered a discount of 15% on Masters programme fees, regardless of when they studied with us previously. The discount applies if you studied on one of our pre-degree, foundation or undergraduate programmes.

Entry Requirements

MA applicants are normally expected to have an undergraduate degree at 2:2 or above. However, the strength of your creative practice and other forms of experience will be taken into account at the interview stage and we encourage you to start a conversation with us.

What should my portfolio include?

Your portfolio should give us an indication of the work that you have made, organised or been involved in. For our postgraduate arts, craft and design courses, we expect to see examples of work you have created.

For our MA Museum Studies, and MA Immersive Media courses, we don't expect you to have traditional artworks; instead you can share examples of projects you have worked on, classroom experiences you have created, and so on. Please ensure that your portfolio includes descriptions, website links and visuals if they are available.

What is the deadline for applying?

The best deadline to submit your MA application by is 1 July, however please be reassured that we can take late applications until the start of the course if places are still available.

pages.text: Arts University Plymouth Logo Skip to Content Our Courses Open Days Apply Now Menu Apply Now Our Courses Open Days Chevron Down About Us Chevron Down Study Chevron Down International Chevron Down Student Life Alumni Chevron Down Visit Resources Chevron Down Research & Innovation Prospectus Latest News What's On Established 1856 Student Login Staff Login Contact Us Explore our Postgraduate courses MA Museum Studies Course Duration 1 year; full-time 2 years; part-time Admissions Contact admissions@aup.ac.uk +44 (0)1752 203434 Apply Now Register Your Interest Overview Course & Units Staff Careers & Alumni Ask a Student Resources Fees & Funding Overview MA Museum Studies offers a unique opportunity to reimagine the role of the museum within contemporary socio-political debates, working with The Box, Plymouth’s award-winning museum, art collection, gallery and archive, and a range of regional and national museums and collections including Tate St Ives, Tate Britain Archives, and RAMM Exeter. Through this programme you will propose a project that engages ideas of the contemporary museum using methods including socially engaged practice, community building and creative education as a productive and mobilising force in a rapidly transforming museum sector. At a glance Award: MA Museum Studies Work with: The Box, Plymouth, Tate St Ives, Tate Britain Archives, RAMM Exeter Project methods: socially engaged practice, community building, creative education Debates shaping the contemporary museum The museum as a cultural form will be reimagined and explored through debates around: Decolonisation The repatriation of objects Distributed digital archives The educational role of museums Diversifying collections and audiences A group of visitors look around the Another Crossing exhibition at The Box Plymouth, organised in collaboration with Arts University Plymouth and Fuller Craft in 2022. Plymouth as a living context Build on the context of Plymouth, a city forging a new identity leaving behind its colonial past to become a contemporary centre of art and culture, leading a significant reevaluation of its heritage through projects such as Mayflower 400 (2020), Another Crossing: Artists Revisit the Mayflower Voyage (2022) and British Art Show 9 (2022–23). Research support, facilities and specialist library You’ll have support to pursue your own research directions through the university’s interdisciplinary art, design and media facilities and our specialist library. Your work will include examining the complex process of design, museum curatorship and interpretation; interrogating theories of exhibition and display, audiences and museology; and initiating projects focused on the practical, pedagogical and theoretical questions underpinning museum education and outreach. The Box, Plymouth's award-winning museum, art gallery and archive, with a 2022 European Museum of the Year Special Commendation, located a short two minute walk from our main Tavistock Place campus. Why choose this course? Offered within the context of a specialist arts university, projects are realised through your formal and critical investigation of the components and conventions of exhibition display. Situated in a city and region with rich naval and cultural heritage, this course is focused on the future of the museum, seeking innovative ideas and formats for reaching broad audiences in new ways. You will be prepared to enter the workplace with the skills and knowledge to play a wide range of roles, from leading practical workshops to art management that link collections and the public. Careers and future opportunities Career opportunities include: Museum Educators, Curators, Cultural Programme Managers, Art Critics, Museum Outreach Coordinators, Heritage and Public Arts Professionals, or alternatively specialise further in postgraduate research. Frequently asked questions What is MA Museum Studies focused on? It offers a unique opportunity to reimagine the role of the museum within contemporary socio-political debates. Which museums and collections will I work with? You will work with The Box, Plymouth and museums and collections including Tate St Ives, Tate Britain Archives, and RAMM Exeter. What debates will the course explore? You’ll explore debates around decolonisation, the repatriation of objects, distributed digital archives, the educational role of museums, and diversifying collections and audiences. What kind of project will I propose? You will propose a project that engages ideas of the contemporary museum using socially engaged practice, community building and creative education. How does Plymouth shape the course? You’ll build on Plymouth’s context and its reevaluation of heritage through Mayflower 400 (2020), Another Crossing: Artists Revisit the Mayflower Voyage (2022) and British Art Show 9 (2022–23). What will my research include? Your work will include design, museum curatorship and interpretation; theories of exhibition and display, audiences and museology; and projects focused on museum education and outreach. Alumni Discount Arts University Plymouth graduates are offered a discount of 15% on Masters programme fees , regardless of when they studied with us previously. The discount applies if you studied on one of our pre-degree, foundation or undergraduate programmes. Entry Requirements MA applicants are normally expected to have an undergraduate degree at 2:2 or above. However, the strength of your creative practice and other forms of experience will be taken into account at the interview stage and we encourage you to start a conversation with us. What should my portfolio include? Your portfolio should give us an indication of the work that you have made, organised or been involved in. For our postgraduate arts, craft and design courses, we expect to see examples of work you have created. For our MA Museum Studies course, we don't expect you to have traditional artworks; instead you can share examples of projects you have worked on, classroom experiences you have created, and so on. Please ensure that your portfolio includes descriptions, website links and visuals if they are available. What is the deadline for applying? The best deadline to submit your MA application by is 1 July , however please be reassured that we can take late applications until the start of the course if places are still available. Get in touch Email: admissions@aup.ac.uk Tel: +44 (0)1752 203434 Want to find out more about MA Museum Studies? If you'd like to speak about Postgraduate study, you can book an informal online chat with a member of our academic team: Associate Professor Stephanie Owens , our Dean of Arts, Design and Media Becky Dodman Wainwright , Co-Course Leader for Postgraduate Studies Jason Hirons , Co-Course Leader for Postgraduate Studies Click the button below to book an informal discussion with a member of our academic team. contentBlocks.text:
MA Museum Studies offers a unique opportunity to reimagine the role of the museum within contemporary socio-political debates, working with The Box, Plymouth’s award-winning museum, art collection, gallery and archive, and a range of regional and national museums and collections including Tate St Ives, Tate Britain Archives, and RAMM Exeter.

Through this programme you will propose a project that engages ideas of the contemporary museum using methods including socially engaged practice, community building and creative education as a productive and mobilising force in a rapidly transforming museum sector.

contentBlocks.heading: At a glance
contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Award: MA Museum Studies

  • Work with: The Box, Plymouth, Tate St Ives, Tate Britain Archives, RAMM Exeter

  • Project methods: socially engaged practice, community building, creative education

The museum as a cultural form will be reimagined and explored through debates around:

  • Decolonisation

  • The repatriation of objects

  • Distributed digital archives

  • The educational role of museums

  • Diversifying collections and audiences

image.title: A group of visitors look around the Another Crossing exhibition at The Box Plymouth in collaboration with Arts University Plymouth and Fuller Craft in 2022

contentBlocks.caption: A group of visitors look around the Another Crossing exhibition at The Box Plymouth, organised in collaboration with Arts University Plymouth and Fuller Craft in 2022.

contentBlocks.bodyText: Build on the context of Plymouth, a city forging a new identity leaving behind its colonial past to become a contemporary centre of art and culture, leading a significant reevaluation of its heritage through projects such as Mayflower 400 (2020), Another Crossing: Artists Revisit the Mayflower Voyage (2022) and British Art Show 9 (2022–23).

image.title: Tate Crit Club Photo by Laura Palmer

contentBlocks.heading: Research support, facilities and specialist library

contentBlocks.bodyText:
You’ll have support to pursue your own research directions through the university’s interdisciplinary art, design and media facilities and our specialist library.

Your work will include examining the complex process of design, museum curatorship and interpretation; interrogating theories of exhibition and display, audiences and museology; and initiating projects focused on the practical, pedagogical and theoretical questions underpinning museum education and outreach.

image.title: The Box Plymouth view of exterior of the building

contentBlocks.caption: The Box, Plymouth's award-winning museum, art gallery and archive, with a 2022 European Museum of the Year Special Commendation, located a short two minute walk from our main Tavistock Place campus.

contentBlocks.bodyText:
Offered within the context of a specialist arts university, projects are realised through your formal and critical investigation of the components and conventions of exhibition display.

Situated in a city and region with rich naval and cultural heritage, this course is focused on the future of the museum, seeking innovative ideas and formats for reaching broad audiences in new ways.

You will be prepared to enter the workplace with the skills and knowledge to play a wide range of roles, from leading practical workshops to art management that link collections and the public.

image.title: Visitors to the Another Crossing exhibition at The Box Plymouth in collaboration with Arts University Plymouth and Fuller Craft in 2022

contentBlocks.bodyText: Career opportunities include: Museum Educators, Curators, Cultural Programme Managers, Art Critics, Museum Outreach Coordinators, Heritage and Public Arts Professionals, or alternatively specialise further in postgraduate research.

items.heading: What is MA Museum Studies focused on?
items.bodyText: It offers a unique opportunity to reimagine the role of the museum within contemporary socio-political debates.

items.heading: Which museums and collections will I work with?
items.bodyText: You will work with The Box, Plymouth and museums and collections including Tate St Ives, Tate Britain Archives, and RAMM Exeter.

items.heading: What debates will the course explore?
items.bodyText: You’ll explore debates around decolonisation, the repatriation of objects, distributed digital archives, the educational role of museums, and diversifying collections and audiences.

items.heading: What kind of project will I propose?
items.bodyText: You will propose a project that engages ideas of the contemporary museum using socially engaged practice, community building and creative education.

items.heading: How does Plymouth shape the course?
items.bodyText: You’ll build on Plymouth’s context and its reevaluation of heritage through Mayflower 400 (2020), Another Crossing: Artists Revisit the Mayflower Voyage (2022) and British Art Show 9 (2022–23).

items.heading: What will my research include?
items.bodyText: Your work will include design, museum curatorship and interpretation; theories of exhibition and display, audiences and museology; and projects focused on museum education and outreach.

contentBlocks.heading: Alumni Discount
contentBlocks.bodyText: Arts University Plymouth graduates are offered a discount of 15% on Masters programme fees, regardless of when they studied with us previously. The discount applies if you studied on one of our pre-degree, foundation or undergraduate programmes.

contentBlocks.heading: Entry Requirements
contentBlocks.bodyText: MA applicants are normally expected to have an undergraduate degree at 2:2 or above. However, the strength of your creative practice and other forms of experience will be taken into account at the interview stage and we encourage you to start a conversation with us.

contentBlocks.heading: What should my portfolio include?
contentBlocks.bodyText:
Your portfolio should give us an indication of the work that you have made, organised or been involved in. For our postgraduate arts, craft and design courses, we expect to see examples of work you have created.

For our MA Museum Studies course, we don't expect you to have traditional artworks; instead you can share examples of projects you have worked on, classroom experiences you have created, and so on. Please ensure that your portfolio includes descriptions, website links and visuals if they are available.

contentBlocks.heading: What is the deadline for applying?
contentBlocks.bodyText: The best deadline to submit your MA application by is 1 July, however please be reassured that we can take late applications until the start of the course if places are still available.

contentBlocks.bodyText:

contentBlocks.bodyText:
If you'd like to speak about Postgraduate study, you can book an informal online chat with a member of our academic team:

contentBlocks.text:
Study the unique art and refined techniques of studio glassmaking in a course dedicated to the history, material and culture of glass. Based in our world-class, state-of-the-art hot glass and kiln-formed glass studios, you will have the opportunity to study both traditional and contemporary approaches to this ancient art form, and gain the hands-on expertise necessary to master its processes as an independent maker.

You will be taught the fundamental properties and behaviours of glass and how it came to be developed as a material of significant utility and revered for unparalleled beauty. Learning its history and many applications will open up your individual pathway of practice-led research into how glass might be reimagined or innovatively applied in a contemporary context.

contentBlocks.heading: At a glance
contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Award: MA Glass

  • Studios: world-class hot glass and kiln-formed glass studios

  • Digital fabrication: Fab Lab South West located adjacent to the hot glass studio

  • Professional opportunities: professional placement or study abroad, including Murano, Venice and other glass studios

As a student of this course you will learn using:

  • A state-of-the-art glass furnace (one of only a small number of electrically powered furnaces in the UK)

  • Hot glass glory-holes and kilns

  • A glass-forming workshop with machines for grinding, shaping and polishing poured or blown glass forms

The hot glass studio includes three blowing benches, where you will explore the traditional method of working with molten transparent and coloured glass, shaping it by blowing and hot forming it with tools.

contentBlocks.caption: Balance 2, Laura Quinn, MA Glass

contentBlocks.bodyText:
Focus on a wide range of traditional and contemporary methods from glass-blowing techniques, stained glass and kiln forming, to more contemporary approaches that use digital modelling, 3D mould-making and waterjet cutting technologies.

Located adjacent to Fab Lab South West, you can work seamlessly between glass and the latest digital fabrication technologies, offering you unparalleled opportunity to unite time-honoured glass processes with innovative methods.

contentBlocks.heading: Environmentally mindful practice and future-facing making

contentBlocks.bodyText: Learn techniques and theories within an environmentally mindful community of practitioners who are developing new ways of working with recycled glass, local seaweed sourced ash, and other place-based and regenerative modes of practice that are the future of the discipline.

• Learn in one of the few remaining and long-standing university-based hot glass studios in the UK.

  • Develop your ideas for glass within a purpose built, multifaceted Materials Lab and in Fab Lab South West, located adjacent to the hot glass studio.

  • Open yourself to a professional placement or study abroad, with opportunities in Murano, Venice and other glass studios around the world through our partnerships and networks.
Career opportunities include: Product Designers, Independent Artisans, Glassware Designers, Scientific Glassblowers, Materials Specialists, Studio Glass Educators and Glass Researchers.

items.heading: What is MA Glass dedicated to?
items.bodyText: It is dedicated to the history, material and culture of glass, studying the unique art and refined techniques of studio glassmaking.

items.heading: What will I learn about glass as a material?
items.bodyText: You will be taught the fundamental properties and behaviours of glass, its history and many applications, supporting a practice-led research pathway into how glass might be reimagined or innovatively applied in a contemporary context.

items.heading: What equipment and studios will I work with?
items.bodyText: You will learn in hot glass and kiln-formed glass studios using a state-of-the-art electrically powered glass furnace, hot glass glory-holes, kilns and a glass-forming workshop for grinding, shaping and polishing poured or blown glass forms.

items.heading: What methods can I focus on?
items.bodyText: You can focus on methods from glass-blowing techniques, stained glass and kiln forming to contemporary approaches using digital modelling, 3D mould-making and waterjet cutting technologies.

items.heading: How does the course connect glassmaking with digital fabrication?
items.bodyText: With Fab Lab South West located adjacent, you can work seamlessly between glass and digital fabrication technologies to unite time-honoured glass processes with innovative methods.

items.heading: What is the environmentally mindful dimension of the course?
items.bodyText: You’ll learn within a community developing new ways of working with recycled glass, local seaweed sourced ash and other place-based and regenerative modes of practice.

items.heading: Are there opportunities for placement or study abroad?
items.bodyText: Yes. You can open yourself to a professional placement or study abroad, including opportunities in Murano, Venice and other glass studios through partnerships and networks.

items.heading: What careers could this MA support?
items.bodyText: Career opportunities include Product Designers, Independent Artisans, Glassware Designers, Scientific Glassblowers, Materials Specialists, Studio Glass Educators and Glass Researchers.

contentBlocks.heading: Alumni Discount
contentBlocks.bodyText: Arts University Plymouth graduates are offered a discount of 15% on Masters programme fees, regardless of when they studied with us previously. The discount applies if you studied on one of our pre-degree, foundation or undergraduate programmes.

contentBlocks.heading: Entry Requirements
contentBlocks.bodyText: MA applicants are normally expected to have an undergraduate degree at 2:2 or above. However, the strength of your creative practice and other forms of experience will be taken into account at the interview stage and we encourage you to start a conversation with us.

contentBlocks.heading: What should my portfolio include?
contentBlocks.bodyText: Your portfolio should give us an indication of the work that you have made, organised or been involved in. For our postgraduate arts, craft and design courses, we expect to see examples of work you have created.

contentBlocks.heading: What is the deadline for applying?
contentBlocks.bodyText: The best deadline to submit your MA application by is 1 July, however please be reassured that we can take late applications until the start of the course if places are still available.

contentBlocks.heading: Get in touch
contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Email: admissions@aup.ac.uk
  • Tel: +44 (0)1752 203434

contentBlocks.bodyText:

  • Associate Professor Stephanie Owens, our Dean of Arts, Design and Media
  • Becky Dodman Wainwright, Co-Course Leader for Postgraduate Studies

Steeped in tacit knowledge often transmitted through hands-on skills and heritage traditions, you will be guided in material-led research processes in clay, glass, wood, biomaterials, metals, fibre or other materials that lead to personal discovery and future-oriented, contemporary professional practice. Through instruction that takes place in our spacious, highly resourced material labs, workshops and studios, you will be encouraged to expand your knowledge of materials and traditional methods of making into new territories of practice open to alternative materials, conceptual frameworks and cross-sector understanding of how materially led innovation is shaping the world. At a glance Award: MA Craft & Material Practices Approach: practice-led, materials-focused curriculum Postgraduate structure: shared units with MA students in other disciplines (critiques, seminars, research intensives, external site visits and lectures) Vortex Whiskey Tumblers, Laura Quinn Materials, studios and resources Your creative study will bring you into contact with the ideas and professional practices of artisans, artists, designers, material researchers, product designers, urban planners, architects and others who are working directly with the behaviour and potential of materials in both expressive and applied design. You will have access to specialist studios and resources including: Hot glass Kiln-formed glass Ceramics 3D clay-printing Biomaterials Wood-working Small metals Fab Lab South West digital tools (open-source, digital and distributed fabrication) Interdisciplinary postgraduate structure Your materials exploration in craft is guided by the interdisciplinary structure of the postgraduate course. You will share a common series of units with MA students in other disciplines for critiques, seminars, research intensives, external site visits and lectures. Specialist instruction in craft and other material practices is taught through smaller seminars where you will concentrate on contemporary ideas and models of practice. Contemporary ideas, debates and models of practice You will broaden your understanding of craft to see its relationship to current debates in art theory, design-thinking, materials science and engineering, social or community-based making, climate change, and sustainability. Why choose this course? Deepen your knowledge and experience of your craft in a practice-led, materials-focused curriculum that provides unique opportunities for personal and professional development. Discover new and emerging methods of making within a vast, purpose-built studio building that unites material exploration in ceramics, glass, wood, metals and biomaterials with state-of-the-art digital fabrication. Explore the cultural and community-based traditions of craft through a contemporary and critical lens, aligning your practice to relevant theories, research methods and professional opportunities for exhibition. Careers and future opportunities Career opportunities include: Designers, Makers, Craftspeople, Artisans, Craft Entrepreneurs, Materials Specialists, Artists and Crafts Educators. Frequently asked questions What is MA Craft & Material Practices about? It takes craft as a starting point rather than a destination, guiding you in material-led research processes that support personal discovery and future-oriented, contemporary professional practice. What materials can I explore through the course? You can explore material-led research processes in clay, glass, wood, biomaterials, metals, fibre or other materials. What specialist resources will I have access to? You will have access to specialist studios and resources in hot glass, kiln-formed glass, ceramics, 3D clay-printing, biomaterials, wood-working, small metals, and Fab Lab South West digital tools. How is the MA structured alongside other postgraduate disciplines? You will share units with MA students in other disciplines for critiques, seminars, research intensives, external site visits and lectures, alongside smaller specialist seminars in craft and material practices. What debates and contexts will shape my thinking? You will connect craft practice to current debates in art theory, design-thinking, materials science and engineering, social or community-based making, climate change, and sustainability. What careers could this MA support? Career opportunities include Designers, Makers, Craftspeople, Artisans, Craft Entrepreneurs, Materials Specialists, Artists and Crafts Educators. Entry Requirements MA applicants are normally expected to have an undergraduate degree at 2:2 or above. However, the strength of your creative practice and other forms of experience will be taken into account at the interview stage and we encourage you to start a conversation with us. What should my portfolio include? Your portfolio should give us an indication of the work that you have made, organised or been involved in. For our postgraduate arts, craft and design courses, we expect to see examples of work you have created. For our MA by Research and MA Museum Studies courses, we don't expect you to have traditional artworks; instead you can share examples of projects you have worked on, classroom experiences you have created, and so on. Please ensure that your portfolio includes descriptions, website links and visuals if they are available. What is the deadline for applying? contentBlocks.text:
MA Craft & Material Practices is a course that takes craft as a starting point rather than a destination. Steeped in tacit knowledge often transmitted through hands-on skills and heritage traditions, you will be guided in material-led research processes in clay, glass, wood, biomaterials, metals, fibre or other materials that lead to personal discovery and future-oriented, contemporary professional practice.

Through instruction that takes place in our spacious, highly resourced material labs, workshops and studios, you will be encouraged to expand your knowledge of materials and traditional methods of making into new territories of practice open to alternative materials, conceptual frameworks and cross-sector understanding of how materially led innovation is shaping the world.

contentBlocks.heading: At a glance
contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Award: MA Craft & Material Practices

  • Approach: practice-led, materials-focused curriculum

  • Postgraduate structure: shared units with MA students in other disciplines (critiques, seminars, research intensives, external site visits and lectures)

contentBlocks.caption: Vortex Whiskey Tumblers, Laura Quinn

contentBlocks.bodyText:
Your creative study will bring you into contact with the ideas and professional practices of artisans, artists, designers, material researchers, product designers, urban planners, architects and others who are working directly with the behaviour and potential of materials in both expressive and applied design.

You will have access to specialist studios and resources including:

  • Hot glass

  • Kiln-formed glass

  • Ceramics

  • 3D clay-printing

  • Biomaterials

  • Wood-working

  • Small metals

  • Fab Lab South West digital tools (open-source, digital and distributed fabrication)

image.title: Plymouth College of Art Contemporary Craft Studios 2
image.caption: Craft studios with pottery wheels and person using pottery wheel for ceramics

contentBlocks.bodyText:
Your materials exploration in craft is guided by the interdisciplinary structure of the postgraduate course. You will share a common series of units with MA students in other disciplines for critiques, seminars, research intensives, external site visits and lectures.

Specialist instruction in craft and other material practices is taught through smaller seminars where you will concentrate on contemporary ideas and models of practice.

contentBlocks.heading: Contemporary ideas, debates and models of practice

contentBlocks.bodyText: You will broaden your understanding of craft to see its relationship to current debates in art theory, design-thinking, materials science and engineering, social or community-based making, climate change, and sustainability.

• Deepen your knowledge and experience of your craft in a practice-led, materials-focused curriculum that provides unique opportunities for personal and professional development.

  • Discover new and emerging methods of making within a vast, purpose-built studio building that unites material exploration in ceramics, glass, wood, metals and biomaterials with state-of-the-art digital fabrication.

  • Explore the cultural and community-based traditions of craft through a contemporary and critical lens, aligning your practice to relevant theories, research methods and professional opportunities for exhibition.
Career opportunities include: Designers, Makers, Craftspeople, Artisans, Craft Entrepreneurs, Materials Specialists, Artists and Crafts Educators.

items.heading: What is MA Craft & Material Practices about?
items.bodyText: It takes craft as a starting point rather than a destination, guiding you in material-led research processes that support personal discovery and future-oriented, contemporary professional practice.

items.heading: What materials can I explore through the course?
items.bodyText: You can explore material-led research processes in clay, glass, wood, biomaterials, metals, fibre or other materials.

items.heading: What specialist resources will I have access to?
items.bodyText: You will have access to specialist studios and resources in hot glass, kiln-formed glass, ceramics, 3D clay-printing, biomaterials, wood-working, small metals, and Fab Lab South West digital tools.

items.heading: How is the MA structured alongside other postgraduate disciplines?
items.bodyText: You will share units with MA students in other disciplines for critiques, seminars, research intensives, external site visits and lectures, alongside smaller specialist seminars in craft and material practices.

items.heading: What debates and contexts will shape my thinking?
items.bodyText: You will connect craft practice to current debates in art theory, design-thinking, materials science and engineering, social or community-based making, climate change, and sustainability.

items.heading: What careers could this MA support?
items.bodyText: Career opportunities include Designers, Makers, Craftspeople, Artisans, Craft Entrepreneurs, Materials Specialists, Artists and Crafts Educators.

image.title: Photograph of biomaterials created by Arts University Plymouth MA Student Natalia Lombardi

contentBlocks.caption: Crafts student Renovat Moody takes us on a tour through the university's breathtaking glass workshop.

contentBlocks.heading: Alumni Discount
contentBlocks.bodyText: Arts University Plymouth graduates are offered a discount of 15% on Masters programme fees, regardless of when they studied with us previously. The discount applies if you studied on one of our pre-degree, foundation or undergraduate programmes.

contentBlocks.heading: Entry Requirements
contentBlocks.bodyText: MA applicants are normally expected to have an undergraduate degree at 2:2 or above. However, the strength of your creative practice and other forms of experience will be taken into account at the interview stage and we encourage you to start a conversation with us.

contentBlocks.heading: What should my portfolio include?
contentBlocks.bodyText:
Your portfolio should give us an indication of the work that you have made, organised or been involved in. For our postgraduate arts, craft and design courses, we expect to see examples of work you have created.

For our MA by Research and MA Museum Studies courses, we don't expect you to have traditional artworks; instead you can share examples of projects you have worked on, classroom experiences you have created, and so on. Please ensure that your portfolio includes descriptions, website links and visuals if they are available.

contentBlocks.heading: What is the deadline for applying?
contentBlocks.bodyText: The best deadline to submit your MA application by is 1 July, however please be reassured that we can take late applications until the start of the course if places are still available.

contentBlocks.heading: Get in touch
contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Email: admissions@aup.ac.uk
  • Tel: +44 (0)1752 203434

contentBlocks.heading: Want to find out more about MA Craft & Material Practices?
contentBlocks.bodyText:
If you'd like to speak about Postgraduate study, you can book an informal online chat with a member of our academic team:

  • Associate Professor Stephanie Owens, our Dean of Arts, Design and Media
  • Becky Dodman Wainwright, Co-Course Leader for Postgraduate Studies
  • Jason Hirons, Co-Course Leader for Postgraduate Studies

Click the button below to book an informal discussion with a member of our academic team.

What facilities will support my making and experimentation?

You’ll be taught within material and media labs for ceramics, glass, biomaterials, print media, digital media, fabric and textiles, with opportunities to experiment and exhibit.

What careers could this MA support?

Career opportunities include Artists, Art Educators, Curators, Art Writers/Critics, Gallerists, Museum Professionals and Creative Entrepreneurs.

Alumni Discount

Arts University Plymouth graduates are offered a discount of 15% on Masters programme fees, regardless of when they studied with us previously. The discount applies if you studied on one of our pre-degree, foundation or undergraduate programmes.

Entry Requirements

MA applicants are normally expected to have an undergraduate degree at 2:2 or above. However, the strength of your creative practice and other forms of experience will be taken into account at the interview stage and we encourage you to start a conversation with us.

What should my portfolio include?

Your portfolio should give us an indication of the work that you have made, organised or been involved in. For our postgraduate arts, craft and design courses, we expect to see examples of work you have created.

What is the deadline for applying?

The best deadline to submit your MA application by is 1 July, however please be reassured that we can take late applications until the start of the course if places are still available.

contentBlocks.text:
MA Fine Art deepens your studio practice by helping you to situate it within critical and contemporary contexts, providing you with the opportunity to develop your ideas and work in a practice-led, interdisciplinary environment.

Whether you work with painting, printmaking, drawing, photography, moving image, performance, social practice or installation, you are encouraged to explore ideas through a process of making and experimentation that extends into new understanding or innovative creative directions.

contentBlocks.heading: At a glance
contentBlocks.bodyText:
• Award: MA Fine Art

  • Ways you’ll learn: visiting lecturers, seminars, research intensives, critiques and site visits

  • Course structure: three units designed to push beyond known forms into current, international cultural debates

  • Facilities access: material and media labs for ceramics, glass, biomaterials, print media, digital media, fabric and textiles

contentBlocks.heading: How contemporary art operates in the world

contentBlocks.bodyText: You will be introduced, through ongoing visiting lecturers, seminars, research intensives, critiques and site visits, to the ways in which contemporary art inhabits a range of contexts, from traditional gallery exhibitions to public art projects and socially engaged collaborations.

image.title: Presence in Absence by Paul Hillon MA Fine Art

contentBlocks.caption: Presence in Absence, Paul Hillon, MA Fine Art

contentBlocks.heading: Three units to push beyond known forms

contentBlocks.bodyText: The development of your work is done through three units designed to encourage you to push beyond known forms to unexpected, surprising new ways of understanding your work within current, international cultural debates.

contentBlocks.heading: Research, visits and building your knowledge

contentBlocks.bodyText: Through your research into relevant topics and visits to galleries, museums and artists’ studios, you will be supported to build a body of knowledge and practice that demonstrates what it means to be an artist in the 21st century.

contentBlocks.heading: Facilities, labs and your creative community

contentBlocks.bodyText:
Taught within a rich network of material and media labs, including those for ceramics, glass, biomaterials, print media, digital media, fabric, and textiles, you will develop a body of work enriched by opportunities to experiment and exhibit.

You’ll do this with a community of active practitioners who will challenge, guide and accelerate your creative development.

• Access one of the most diverse and spacious ecosystems of workshops, studios and labs known in a contemporary art and design school.

  • Develop your work within a supportive, challenging learning environment that gives you the critical and professional skills necessary for becoming an independent artist or cultural producer.

  • Study within a multidisciplinary community enriched by visiting lecturers, visiting artists, study trips, peer feedback and opportunities to publicly exhibit your work.
Career opportunities include: Artists, Art Educators, Curators, Art Writers/Critics, Gallerists, Museum Professionals and Creative Entrepreneurs.
